European Union: EU AI Act (risk-based classification, prohibited practices, transparency requirements)
Canada: Federal Anti-Fraud Strategy, OSFI guidance on model risk and AI governance
United States: OCC guidance, FCAC consumer protection, state-level AI regulations
UK: UK AI Bill, FCA expectations
APAC: MAS AI governance frameworks, Australian Scams Prevention Framework

Assess implications for RBC's AI programs and audit coverage strategy

Lead Regulatory Issue Validation and Coordinate Regulatory Exam Responses

Validate management's remediation of regulatory issues related to AI (e.g., GRM AI Governance issues, Capital Markets AI Governance Framework issues)
Coordinate responses to regulatory exams on AI governance, model risk management, and data governance
Liaise with regulatory affairs teams and external auditors to ensure consistent messaging

Ensure Audit Coverage Addresses Regulatory Expectations Across Jurisdictions

Job Description

Senior Director, AI Product Management

What's the opportunity?

We're looking for a product leader who can turn a strategic product vision into shipped reality at scale. Ecosystem health: Ensuring the community and partnership programs sustain engagement and healthy adoption across the RBC user base

You're our ideal candidate if you:

Have 10+ years of product management experience, including 3+ years leading multi-team product organizations as a manager of managers
Have a track record of customer discovery and translating user needs into product strategy and prioritization
Have hands-on experience delivering end-user facing AI products — ideally generative or agentic AI — at production scale
Have run large-scale internal or enterprise product launches with measurable adoption outcomes

Drive AI transformation at one of Canada's largest and most respected financial institutions, with exposure to senior leadership across RBC

jobs.description:
At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go. Join EY and help to build a better working world.

The opportunity

EY has curated a dynamic ecosystem of Alliance and Ecosystem relationships which creates new forms of customer value to help our clients rapidly and digitally transform. Our ecosystem consists of more than 100 relationships which allow us to provide a wide range of collaborative opportunities and solutions to our clients. We help them tap into the latest technologies to achieve transformational outcomes and be more agile, innovative, resilient and better equipped to respond to disruptive change.

The EY–Microsoft Alliance plays a critical role in driving revenue growth by identifying, shaping, and closing joint transformation opportunities between EY, Microsoft, and our clients.

As a Global Microsoft Presales Leader for AI Business Solutions, you will play a pivotal role in scaling EY’s ability to win complex, high-value deals. This role is focused on defining and leading global presales strategy, establishing best practices, and shaping major pursuits across priority markets in alignment with Microsoft’s go-to-market model.

You will work closely with global alliance leadership, Microsoft sales teams and regional stakeholders to architect compelling solutions, strengthen EY’s value proposition, and ensure a consistent, high-quality presales approach across the business.

This role requires a strong understanding of enterprise technology and the Microsoft ecosystem, with specialist knowledge in AI Business Solutions, combined with the ability to distill complex ideas into clear, compelling narratives for clients, Microsoft and EY teams.

Your Key Responsibilities

Your primary responsibilities will include:

Global Presales Leadership: Define and lead the global presales strategy for the EY–Microsoft Alliance within a Solution Area, establishing repeatable methods, governance, and best practices to improve pursuit quality and win rates.

Microsoft Alignment: Work with EY Solution Area Directors to align presales approaches to Microsoft’s AI Business Solution Area and Sales Plays, co-sell motions and field priorities, ensuring effective joint engagement with Microsoft stakeholders.

Client Engagement: Engage with senior client stakeholders to shape transformation opportunities and articulate clear, outcome-driven value propositions.
Presales Assets & Enablement: Develop reusable assets, proposal content, and playbooks to enable consistent, scalable presales execution across regions and teams.
Solution Innovation: Help shape differentiated EY–Microsoft solutions, leveraging the latest Microsoft technology and EY industry capabilities to address priority market opportunities.

This role is Global, optimal base on US, Canada, Europe (UK, Netherlands, France, Germany, Italy, Poland) or Singapore. You can anticipate a mix of virtual work along with regular coordination with other team members across Global and across the Globe. The role will require some travel.

Skills And Attributes For Success

Proven Presales and Sales Experience: 8+ years in presales, solution architecture, or enterprise technology sales, with experience supporting complex, high-value pursuits.
Microsoft Ecosystem Expertise: Strong working knowledge of Microsoft technologies (e.g. Azure, Data & AI, Security, Business Applications, Copilot) and go-to-market models. Specialism is require in AI Business Solutions.
Strategic Advisory Skills: Ability to translate technology into business value, shaping client strategies, providing advisory context and enabling transformation journeys.
Solution Development Expertise: Experience developing end-to-end solutions, including business case, value articulation, delivery approach and commercial model.
Exceptional Communication Skills: Strong storytelling, presentation and proposal-writing capabilities, with experience influencing C-level stakeholders.
Leadership and Stakeholder Management: Proven ability to lead cross-functional, global teams and influence senior stakeholders without direct authority.
Results-Driven Mindset: Track record of shaping and winning strategic opportunities, with the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, global environment.

Preferred Qualifications:

Global Experience: Experience working across regions in a global alliance, partner or ecosystem-led sales model.
Industry Knowledge: Familiarity with key sectors such as financial services, healthcare, technology and public sector. Depth of experience and knowledge in particular sectors or industry is preferrable.
Commercial Acumen: Experience with complex deal structures and non-traditional commercial models for large-scale transformation.
Certifications: Relevant Microsoft or enterprise technology certifications.

What we look for:

A self-starter who is able to work independently while also communicating progress and challenges with others on the team
Comfortable escalating complex issues with recommendations to leadership
Strong organizational skills and ability to multi-task in support of multiple projects at a time
Comfortable working with others within EY with unique personalities, cultures and working styles and can adapt your approach to best interact.

Other geographies will follow their local salary guidelines, which may not be a direct conversion of published US salary ranges. Learn more at ey.com/us/careers.

We offer a comprehensive compensation and benefits package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to the business. The base salary range for this job is:

New York City, Boston, and Washington DC Metro Areas, Washington State, and Southern California offices – $198,900 to $357,900
Bay Area California offices – $207,100 to $372,900

Individual salaries within these ranges are determined through a wide variety of factors including but not limited to education, experience, knowledge, skills and geography. In addition, our Total Rewards package includes medical and dental coverage, pension and 401(k) plans, and a wide range of paid time off options.
Under our flexible vacation policy, you’ll decide how much vacation time you need based on your own personal circumstances. You’ll also be granted time off for designated EY Paid Holidays, Winter/Summer breaks, Personal/Family Care, and other leaves of absence when needed to support your physical, financial, and emotional well-being.

Have 8+ years in product marketing, community management, change management, or enterprise adoption, with demonstrated enterprise-scale impact
Have a proven track record of driving technology adoption across large organizations

You'll bring both the technical depth to make sound platform decisions and the people leadership to grow and run a team operating at scale.

We're hiring for this role in Palo Alto, Irvine, or Vancouver. We are happy to work with whichever location suits you best.

Responsibilities

Define and drive the data strategy and roadmap across vehicle telemetry, manufacturing, and enterprise data domains, aligning with engineering, product, and business stakeholders.

jobs.title: Director, AI & Data Science (Marketing Measurement & Effectiveness)
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Artefact is an applied AI company. We build systems that run in production, in our clients' own cloud, and keep running after we leave. 2,500+ people across 27 countries and 1,000 clients, including some of the largest consumer brands in the world. Not a strategy house that discovered AI eighteen months ago, and not a prototype shop that hands you something you will rebuild from scratch.

Three ingredients make that possible, and very few firms have all three: the data, real and messy and at enterprise scale; an applied AI team that can put a model into a governed production environment; and the transformation muscle to make people actually use it.

Agentic AI lands on marketing before it lands anywhere else. Agents browse, compare and buy; clicks stop meaning what they meant; the shelf turns into an API. Every senior marketing and commerce leader we talk to is asking the same two questions — am I still visible, and can I still prove what worked — and almost nobody can answer them.

The Role

We are hiring a Director to lead marketing measurement and effectiveness for our US client portfolio, starting with a large, in-flight measurement program for a major US financial services client.

This is a player-coach role. You will own the methodology and the client relationship, lead a multi-workstream data science team, and stay close enough to the models to challenge assumptions, review code and unblock hard technical problems yourself. You will also help us productize what we build — turning measurement work into reusable accelerators and points of view that scale across accounts.

You should be able to step into a live, complex measurement program quickly and earn credibility with senior client stakeholders in the first weeks, not the first quarter.

What You'll Do

You will own the hardest question in marketing: what actually caused the sales. Marketing Mix Modeling, incrementality testing, geo-lift, attribution — for a brand where a few points of budget reallocation is worth more than most consulting engagements. You will do it as a hands-on scientist and as a trusted advisor to senior client stakeholders — both, not either.

Lead measurement programs

Own the design, execution and interpretation of marketing measurement programs: MMM, geo and incrementality testing, attribution, experimentation and marketing optimization.
Own the statistical modeling architecture and the scientific rigor behind it — model specification, validation, calibration against live experimental results, honest treatment of uncertainty, and identification assumptions worked through with people who care as much as you do about getting them right.
Adapt frameworks to messy commercial reality: long consideration cycles, CRM-driven demand, short flights, campaign overlap, brand and long-term effects, channel and regional constraints, and privacy-constrained measurement where the easy signal has disappeared.
Translate model output into media investment, budget allocation and scenario-planning decisions the client can act on.

Own the outcome, not just the deliverable

Work in the client's environment from day zero and stay there after launch — no prototype handoffs. When something breaks in production, you're close enough to see it and fix it.
Build and deploy GenAI and agentic applications into production that change how measurement gets done and consumed: automated model diagnostics, insight generation, analyst copilots, conversational access to measurement results.
Contribute to Artefact's reusable measurement offerings, accelerators and IP.
Get direct access to the frontier labs — we work with Anthropic, Google, OpenAI and Mistral as partners, not vendors on a procurement list, with early access and the freedom to build with what shipped this quarter.

Build and lead the team

Lead and develop data scientists and analysts across parallel workstreams; grow senior talent.
Set the delivery standards — reproducibility, documentation, QA and validation of analytical deliverables.
Work alongside scientists, engineers, creatives and strategists who will pick your models apart and then help you fix them — nobody here ships alone.

Grow the account

Shape solutions, support proposals and scope new work; expand the relationship beyond the initial mandate.
Represent Artefact externally — white papers, conference talks, published methodologies.
Help decide what we productize next, what we stop doing, and how we take it to market — measurement is not a finished product.
Get direct access to senior client stakeholders, not a workstream lead reporting up through three layers: you present the method, defend it, own the recommendation, and you're in the room during qualification, before anything is signed.

What We're Looking For

Deep marketing measurement expertise. Approximately 10+ years building — not just presenting — Marketing Mix Modeling, incrementality and attribution work, applied statistics, causal inference, experimentation and marketing optimization, or the depth to match. You have shipped models that changed how a real budget was spent, and you can talk about the ones that failed.
Genuine marketing fluency. You know how retail media behaves differently from paid social, why brand-building resists short-term measurement, and what a media planner is actually going to do with your output on Monday morning. Measurement without marketing intuition produces confident nonsense.
Serious data science. Causal inference and Bayesian methods as a working craft, not vocabulary — comfortable across the wider toolkit: forecasting, optimization, experimentation platforms, and applied GenAI, with experience shipping generative AI or agentic AI applications into production for marketing, analytics and decision-making. You're still writing code yourself — you'd rather debug it than delegate it.
Executive-grade communication. Strong client-facing and executive communication skills — able to make rigorous methodology legible to executives and business stakeholders, and to defend analytical approaches with skeptical senior stakeholders. You can hold a technical audience for an hour on the identification strategy and a senior client stakeholder for ninety seconds on what to do about it, and be trusted by both — including saying "the result is inconclusive" when it is.Hands-on program leadership. The ability to lead complex and ambiguous measurement programs while remaining close enough to the work to challenge methodologies, review models and solve difficult technical problems yourself.
Team leadership. Experience leading and developing data-science teams across multiple workstreams. A consulting and commercial mindset — shaping solutions, supporting proposals and expanding client relationships, and being in the room during qualification and solution design, not handed a signed scope.
Production instincts. MLOps and cloud industrialization — a model living in a notebook is a hobby, not a deliverable. AI-native ways of working. You use AI on your own work daily. If you would rather keep the ways of working you already know, ours will frustrate you.
Master's degree (or higher) in computer science, engineering, statistics/mathematics, or a related field, or equivalent research/industry experience.

Preferred

Financial-services experience, ideally in banking, wealth management, asset management, credit cards or insurance — this is domain depth we do not have internally and it transfers across accounts, so it's a priority filter, but we will trade it against exceptional measurement and AI strength.
Consulting, agency, measurement-vendor or platform background across data-intensive industries such as retail, CPG, healthcare or financial services (e.g., MMM/measurement providers, media agencies, or in-house measurement functions).
Experience with brand and long-term marketing measurement (brand tracking, brand equity, long-term effects alongside short-term performance).
Experience with major media platforms and ecosystems (Google, Meta, retail media, CTV) and their measurement products.
Evidence of external thought leadership: white papers, published methodologies, conference participation, or development of reusable measurement offerings.
Visualization and delivery tooling: Looker, Tableau, Power BI or equivalent; cloud data platforms (BigQuery, Snowflake, Databricks).

Why Join Us

We are united by our values
and strengthened by our hybrid expertise.

There is always a way: We're from the breed of does, of diggers, of makers. Because ideas are valuable only if executed.
Client trust is won on the field: Addressing client needs flows better hands on at their side.
If not used, it is useless: Our love for technology translates into a steep desire for adoption. True brilliance is about impact.
If not shared, our work is not done: Sharing knowledge is the best way to button up a mission, benefiting clients and colleagues.
We learn every day: Tech is a land where everything moves at the speed of light. You better be ready to challenge yourself.

How We Support Our People

In addition to our values-driven culture, we offer a range of benefits and programs designed to support our employees' growth and well-being, including:

Learning and Development: Work alongside a multidisciplinary team of AI, data, and consulting experts who are committed to continuous learning, knowledge sharing, and professional growth.
Hybrid Flexibility: Our hybrid work model gives you the flexibility to balance collaboration, client needs, and personal commitments.
Comprehensive Benefits: We offer a competitive benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) plan with company matching, and paid parental leave.
Time to Recharge: We believe sustainable performance matters. That's why we offer unlimited paid time off, giving you the flexibility to take the time you need.
Growth Opportunities: As a rapidly growing organization, you'll have the opportunity to expand your skills, take on new challenges, and help shape the future of the company.

The estimated base compensation for this role starts at $200,000 (NYC location). Individual compensation is determined by skills, qualifications, and experience. In addition, this role is eligible for competitive benefits.

jobs.title: Director of Enterprise Architecture - Information Technology
jobs.description:
Alberta Blue Cross® is an Alberta based organization dedicated to delivering exceptional customer experience and community leadership. We’re committed to providing the best health coverage to over 1.8 million members and take an active role in promoting wellness. We believe in what we do—and place trust in our employees to deliver our vision.

Working at Alberta Blue Cross® means having a career where you’ll be recognized for your contributions. We value diversity, encourage our team members to maintain a healthy work-life balance and provide opportunities for career growth.

OVERVIEW:

We have an exciting opportunity for a Director of Enterprise Architecture to provide senior enterprise architecture leadership for Alberta Blue Cross. Reporting to the Chief Architect, the Director of Enterprise Architecture leads and operates the Enterprise Architecture function, provides people leadership to Domain Architects, and plays a key role in EA governance. The role translates enterprise architecture strategy and executive direction into practical operating practices, standards, reference architectures, guardrails, compliance measures, and governance outcomes across the organization.

This senior leadership role establishes and matures the enterprise architecture framework that enables strategy execution, modernization, disciplined investment, risk management, and consistent decision-making across portfolios and domains. The role works closely with business, technology, security, privacy, risk, finance, EPMO, portfolio, solution, and domain architecture stakeholders to ensure enterprise architecture guidance is clear, credible, actionable, and consistently applied. The Director of Enterprise Architecture advises senior leaders by translating complex architectural implications into clear options, risks, dependencies, and recommendations that balance business outcomes, cost, complexity, resiliency, compliance, and long-term sustainability.

The Director of Enterprise Architecture is a senior people leadership and architecture governance role focused on enterprise-wide architecture direction, architecture discipline, domain alignment, and executive decision support. The role directly leads Domain Architects and coordinates federated design authority across business, data and AI, application, integration, cloud, security, identity, experience, and technology domains.

Success in this role is achieved by:

Operating and maturing the enterprise architecture function in alignment with IT strategy, EA mandate, governance expectations, and executive decision-making needs.
Setting and enforcing enterprise-level architecture principles, standards, reference architectures, guardrails, compliance expectations, and governance practices across domains and portfolios.
Providing people leadership, coaching, performance support, and prioritization guidance for Domain Architects as direct reports.
Establishing architecture as a trusted advisory and governance function with clear OKRs, KPIs, compliance measures, and value indicators.
Driving coherent, reusable, resilient, secure, compliant, and sustainable architecture decisions across the enterprise.

WHAT YOU WILL DO:

Lead and operate the Enterprise Architecture function, ensuring architecture practices, standards, governance forums, and decision processes are consistently applied across the organization.
Set, evolve, and steward enterprise architecture principles, standards, reference architectures, guardrails, compliance expectations, and governance practices that guide enterprise-wide decisions.
Translate corporate strategy, business priorities, technology trends, regulatory expectations, and enterprise risks into actionable architecture guidance.
Chair, guide, or support senior architecture governance forums, including decision rights, review processes, compliance expectations, escalation paths, and transparent decision records.
Establish and monitor enterprise architecture OKRs, KPIs, compliance measures, and value indicators to demonstrate adoption, effectiveness, risk reduction, and enterprise value.
Develop and steward enterprise reference architectures that guide business, information, application, integration, cloud, security, identity, data, AI, experience, and technology decisions.
Provide enterprise architecture oversight for major programs, platforms, partnerships, modernization initiatives, and strategic investments.
Partner with Portfolio Architects to ensure portfolio target architectures and modernization roadmaps align to enterprise strategy, principles, reference architectures, guardrails, and governance expectations.
Lead Domain Architects as direct reports, providing coaching, prioritization guidance, performance support, role clarity, and alignment across domain-specific design authority.
Coordinate Domain Architects so federated design authority remains aligned to enterprise direction while avoiding duplication with business, data, security, digital, delivery, and operations teams.
Identify enterprise-level architectural risks, duplication, fragmentation, technical debt, capability gaps, and architectural drift, and recommend priorities for leadership action.
Advise senior business and technology leaders on architecture options, risks, dependencies, enterprise implications, and recommended courses of action in clear business terms.
Escalate unresolved cross-domain conflicts, material exceptions, or enterprise-level trade-offs through formal governance forums as appropriate.

POSITION SCOPE:

Reports to the Chief Architect and leads the operational execution, EA governance, and people leadership of the Enterprise Architecture function.
Provides enterprise-wide architecture discipline, domain alignment, and governance practices that guide strategic technology decisions.
Owns enterprise architecture principles, reference architectures, guardrails, standards, governance practices, OKRs, KPIs, compliance measures, and architecture effectiveness reporting.
Provides direct leadership, coaching, prioritization guidance, performance support, and development for Domain Architects, who report to the Director of Enterprise Architecture.
Works across senior business, technology, security, privacy, risk, finance, EPMO, portfolio, solution, domain architecture, delivery, and operations stakeholders.
Acts as a trusted senior advisor to business and technology leaders by shaping enterprise technology direction, risk visibility, investment confidence, and strategic decision quality.
Provides senior architecture oversight and governance for major enterprise decisions, while remaining distinct from initiative-level solution design, delivery-team management, and operational execution.

ACCOUNTABILITY BOUNDARIES AND ROLE CLARITY:

The Director of Enterprise Architecture reports to the Chief Architect and is accountable for leading, operating, and maturing the Enterprise Architecture function, including playing a key role in EA governance. The role translates enterprise architecture strategy into clear operating practices, governance forums, standards, reference architectures, guardrails, compliance measures, and domain-level execution.

The Director of Enterprise Architecture provides direct people leadership for Domain Architects and is accountable for ensuring domain-specific design authority is coordinated, consistent, and aligned to enterprise direction. Domain Architects remain federated design authorities for their areas of specialty, including business, data and AI, experience, application, integration and API, cloud, security, identity, and technology architecture. This role ensures these domain accountabilities operate as one coherent enterprise capability rather than as isolated specialty functions.

The Director of Enterprise Architecture does not replace or duplicate Portfolio Architect accountabilities. Portfolio Architects own portfolio target architectures, transition states, and 2–3 year modernization roadmaps. They translate enterprise direction into portfolio-specific sequencing, investment alignment, roadmaps, and architecture runway priorities. The Director of Enterprise Architecture governs the enterprise architecture framework within which those portfolio decisions are made and ensures cross-portfolio consistency, standards compliance, and escalation of enterprise-level risks.

The Director of Enterprise Architecture does not replace or duplicate Solution Architect accountabilities. Solution Architects own initiative-level solution architecture and design within approved enterprise and portfolio guardrails. The Director of Enterprise Architecture clarifies standards, decision constraints, exception paths, and governance expectations so solution decisions remain aligned to the approved enterprise and portfolio target states.

This separation of accountabilities ensures clear decision rights: the Director of Enterprise Architecture leads the EA function, governance model, domain architecture capability, and people leadership; Portfolio Architects translate enterprise direction into portfolio roadmaps; Domain Architects provide federated design authority; and Solution Architects design delivery-ready solutions within approved guardrails.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES:

Lead, operate, and mature the Enterprise Architecture function, including playing a key role in EA governance, in alignment with the enterprise architecture mandate and executive direction.
Own the enterprise architecture operating model, principles, reference architectures, guardrails, governance practices, standards, compliance expectations, and architecture effectiveness measures.
Provide direct people leadership for Domain Architects, including coaching, prioritization guidance, performance support, development planning, and coordination of domain-level work.
Maintain enterprise architecture OKRs, KPIs, compliance measures, decision records, and executive-level reporting that demonstrate value, adoption, governance effectiveness, and risk reduction.
Ensure architecture governance is pragmatic, transparent, authoritative, and consistently applied across portfolios, domains, major initiatives, and enterprise decision forums.
Provide enterprise architecture oversight for major platform, modernization, integration, cloud, security, data, AI, identity, experience, and application decisions with organization-wide implications.
Promote consistency, reuse, interoperability, security, compliance, resiliency, cost discipline, and long-term sustainability across enterprise solutions.
Identify architectural risks, gaps, duplication, capability constraints, technical debt, and cross-domain conflicts, and guide senior leadership on enterprise-level remediation priorities.
Facilitate architecture decision-making across Portfolio Architects, Solution Architects, Domain Architects, delivery teams, business leaders, and enterprise stakeholders without assuming their distinct delivery, roadmap, or solution design accountabilities.
Partner with executive, business, and technology leaders to embed architecture-by-design into strategy, planning, investment, governance, and delivery decisions.
Escalate unresolved enterprise architecture conflicts, material exceptions, and strategic trade-offs through formal governance forums.

KEY SUCCESS MEASURES:

Enterprise architecture principles, guardrails, standards, reference architectures, and governance practices are adopted and consistently used to guide major decisions.
Architecture OKRs, KPIs, compliance measures, and executive reporting demonstrate measurable adoption, quality, risk reduction, governance effectiveness, and enterprise value.
Domain Architects are aligned, effective, well-led, and operating as a coordinated enterprise capability with clear priorities, accountabilities, and development support.
Portfolio, domain, and solution architecture decisions are materially better aligned to enterprise direction, strategic priorities,

jobs.title: Director of Product, Content Intelligence & Growth
jobs.description:
Scribd, Inc. is on a mission to advance human understanding. Our four products — Scribd®, Slideshare®, Everand™, and Fable — help billions of people across the globe move beyond access and into insight, application, and expertise.

Culture at Scribd, Inc.

We support a culture where our employees can be real and be bold; where we debate and commit as we embrace plot twists; and where every employee is empowered to take action as we prioritize the customer.

We believe the best work happens when individual flexibility is balanced with meaningful community connection. Scribd Flex empowers employees to choose the workstyle and location that support their best performance, while committing to intentional in-person moments that strengthen collaboration and culture. Occasional in-person attendance is required for all Scribd, Inc. employees, regardless of location.

So what are we looking for in new team members? At Scribd, Inc., we hire for “GRIT.” Traditionally defined as the intersection of passion and perseverance toward long-term goals, GRIT reflects the mindset we expect from every employee. For us, it also serves as a practical framework for how we work: setting and achieving Goals, delivering Results within your role, contributing Innovative ideas and solutions, and strengthening the broader Team through collaboration and attitude.

This posting reflects an approved, open position within the organization.

The team

Content is the foundation of everything we build at Scribd, Inc. Our UGC corpus—more than 400 million user-uploaded documents, distinct from the rights-protected premium catalogs behind Everand and Fable—powers the consumer experience on Scribd and Slideshare and differentiates our search and discovery.

The Content pillar is the team responsible for that asset. It spans three connected areas—trust & safety (protecting the corpus), understanding (knowing it), and supply (growing it)—each with dedicated product and engineering leadership, embedded analysts, and applied ML capability.

We have high standards, give real feedback, and always bias toward action. Everyone owns their work end-to-end. There's high trust, low hand-holding, and a genuine expectation that you'll push the people around you toward sharper thinking and better outcomes.

We celebrate wins, learn from our losses, and laugh through both.

Join us!

The role

We're hiring a Director of Content Intelligence & Supply to own knowing our UGC corpus and growing it as an asset. This is a new role, and it comes at a moment when content has become central to our strategy: the UGC corpus powers our consumer products and feeds search and discovery.

You'll bring content intelligence and content supply under one point of leadership—connecting what we know about the corpus (classification, metadata, quality, gaps) with the decisions about how we grow it. Today those efforts run in different parts of the org; your job is to run them as one portfolio with one roadmap. We build products that turn information into understanding, grounded in trusted human-created sources—and we own the data structure and intelligence that make a corpus this large useful.

This role reports to the Chief Product Officer. You'll inherit an established team—a content understanding program with its own charter and dedicated engineering squad, and a UGC supply squad that owns the end-to-end contributor experience—with room to shape the org's direction, structure, and future growth.

We're looking for a product leader with real data fluency: probably not a traditional consumer product manager, but someone with a foot in the data science world—as comfortable interrogating a classification model as running a product review—who gets excited about turning a 400-million-document UGC corpus into a strategic asset.

Know the corpus

Own the content understanding roadmap: classification, enrichment, metadata, and quality across the UGC corpus.
Drive corpus gap analysis: where the corpus is deep, where it's thin, and how user-generated and partner content behave differently.
Make the corpus legible—to our own products (search, discovery, recommendations) and to the teams and systems that build on it.
Set direction for classification and corpus-analysis work with credibility, in close partnership with applied ML, engineering, and data science teams.

Grow the supply

Own UGC supply end to end: uploads, conversions, and the supply-side user experience. The people who add content to our platforms are your customer.
Unify content acquisition strategy: set priorities across user-generated supply, partnerships, and other related programs that today run independently—coordinating the strategy while execution stays with the teams closest to it.
Connect supply to demand: partner with the consumer product orgs so the corpus grows where it creates the most value for readers, learners, and subscribers.

Build the knowledge infrastructure for AI

jobs.title: Interim Vice President, Finance & Transformation
jobs.description:
IMMEDIATE INTERIM OPPORTUNITY

Interim Vice President, Finance & Transformation

Reports To: Chief Executive Officer

Duration: 12 months

Location: Downtown Toronto

(Hybrid)

This is an exceptional opportunity to lead a high-impact transformation mandate within a well-known, mission-driven organization undertaking a significant modernization journey. Few interim mandates offer the opportunity to influence both organizational transformation and finance modernization at this scale. Our client is embarking on an ambitious journey to strengthen its capabilities, modernize core operations, and position itself for long-term success.

As the Interim, you will be at the center of that journey. Working directly with the CEO and senior leadership team, you will assess the effectiveness of the finance organization, redesign key processes and structures, oversee the implementation of a modern accounting platform, strengthen governance and reporting capabilities, and help create a high-performing finance function that delivers meaningful insight and strategic value. This is an opportunity to make a visible impact, build lasting capability, and leave behind a stronger, more modern organization than the one you inherited.

Key Priorities

1. Assess and Shape the Finance Transformation Roadmap

Conduct a focused current-state assessment of finance processes, controls, reporting, governance and supporting capabilities.
Identify gaps, risks, inefficiencies and opportunities to strengthen the maturity and effectiveness of the finance function.
Develop and sequence a practical transformation roadmap with clear priorities, accountabilities and measurable outcomes.

2. Strengthen Financial Planning, Reporting and Decision Support

Review budgeting, forecasting, financial planning and management reporting practices.
Improve the quality, consistency and usefulness of financial information available to executives, the Finance & Audit Committee and the Board.
Help translate financial information into clear implications, options and recommendations for decision-making.

3. Enhance Governance, Controls and Risk Management

Strengthen financial policies, internal controls, documentation and oversight practices.
Support the identification, assessment and management of financial risks.
Provide guidance related to internal and external audit readiness and follow-through.

4. Drive Process Improvement and Operational Excellence

Review workflows to identify bottlenecks, manual workarounds, duplication and control gaps.
Standardize and simplify processes to improve accuracy, efficiency, accountability and service delivery.
Promote effective collaboration between finance and organizational stakeholders.

5. Enable Technology and Reporting Modernization

Assess how existing financial systems and reporting tools are being used.
Identify practical opportunities to improve budgeting, forecasting, reporting and analytics capabilities.
Reduce unnecessary reliance on manual processes and spreadsheets where feasible.

6. Build Sustainable Capability

Create practical tools, templates, policies, procedures and standard operating practices.
Support knowledge transfer, coaching and capability-building within the finance team.
Leave behind a clear transition plan and roadmap for continued improvement beyond the assignment.

Expected Deliverables

A validated current-state assessment and prioritized finance transformation roadmap.
Strengthened budgeting, forecasting, reporting and decision-support practices.
Improved financial policies, controls, governance documentation and risk oversight.
Standardized and more efficient finance processes and workflows.
Enhanced utilization of financial systems, reporting tools and analytics capabilities.
Practical implementation support, knowledge transfer and a sustainable transition plan.

The Ideal Candidate

The successful candidate will be a seasoned finance transformation leader who combines strategic judgment with a practical, implementation-oriented approach. They will be comfortable advising senior leaders and governance stakeholders while working directly with teams to translate recommendations into durable improvements.

University degree in finance, accounting, business administration or a related discipline.
Professional accounting designation in good standing is strongly preferred.
10+ years of progressively senior finance and leadership experience, including executive or senior management exposure.
Demonstrated experience leading finance transformation, strengthening controls and improving management reporting.
Experience supporting a Board, Finance & Audit Committee or an equivalent governance body.
Strong process improvement, change management, project leadership and implementation capability.
Ability to provide clear, practical and candid advice and to translate financial information for varied stakeholders.
Experience in a regulatory, public-sector, healthcare, not-for-profit or other public-interest organization is considered an asset.
High integrity, discretion, accountability and commitment to public-interest stewardship.

We are seeking a Director of GTM Planning and Compensation
to own and evolve Clio’s global GTM planning, territory design, and incentive compensation functions as a core lever of growth, performance, and behavior change. This role is available to candidates in Vancouver, Calgary, or Toronto, or remotely across Canada (excluding Québec) and the US.

This role is responsible for translating company and GTM strategy into capacity plans, territories, quotas, and incentive design that drives the right outcomes across Sales, Channel, and Customer Success. You will operate as a strategic advisor to GTM and Finance leadership, balancing competitiveness, simplicity, scalability, and financial discipline.

You will lead capacity planning, territory design and maintenance, and incentive compensation planning, governance, and administration globally, oversee compensation systems and analytics, and build a high-performing sales planning function that scales with Clio’s rapid expansion. Your work will directly influence revenue predictability, seller behavior, retention, and long-term growth.

What you’ll work on:

GTM Planning, Capacity & Quotas

Leading GTM capacity planning and quota-setting, translating growth targets into coverage, headcount, and productivity plans across Sales and CS.
Developing and evolving quota-setting methodologies, ensuring targets are grounded in market opportunity, historical performance, and productivity expectations.
Partnering with Finance and GTM leadership to model capacity needs, ramp assumptions, productivity, and hiring requirements for annual and long-range planning, including scenario models that show the tradeoffs between headcount, coverage, quotas, productivity, compensation, and revenue before decisions are made.
Establishing planning frameworks and analytics to monitor capacity, quota attainment, and productivity and inform in-year adjustments.
Owning quota exceptions, relief policies, and disputes, balancing consistency with practical business judgment.

Territory Design & Maintenance

Leading territory design and account segmentation, aligning selling resources with company strategy.
Translating revenue targets into coverage models and account assignments, and identifying where the organization is over- or under-covered and what needs to change.
Owning ongoing territory maintenance, including account assignments and in-year territory changes.

Compensation Strategy & Plan Design

Owning and evolving Clio's global GTM compensation and rewards strategy spanning SMB and Enterprise segments, partnering with Sales, Channel, and CS leadership to ensure alignment with company objectives, GTM motions, and growth stages.
Leading the design, modeling, and optimization of Sales and CS compensation plans, pay mix, quotas, accelerators, SPIFFs, and performance levers that drive desired behaviors, improve productivity, and support multi-year growth.
Partnering with Finance and Sales/CS Ops to model plan effectiveness, risk, and ROI, leading quarterly and annual compensation effectiveness reviews (attainment distribution, cost of sale, capacity utilization), and ensuring plans support revenue predictability, margin targets, and financial planning.
Developing and delivering clear, compelling compensation education and enablement programs for leaders, managers, and individual contributors, translating complex compensation concepts into simple, actionable narratives that build trust across GTM teams.

jobs.title: Director, Technical Operations (Platform)
jobs.description:
Job Type:
Permanent Full Time

Location:
Full Onsite - Toronto, Ontario

Reporting to:
Chief Technology Officer

Salary
: $150,000 – $170,000 CAD

Job Purpose

The Director, Technical Operations owns the operational health of the platforms Goway sells and services travel on: our reservations platform, the infrastructure it runs on, the supplier, air and distribution integrations it depends on, and the automation and data pipelines built around it.

This is a practice-building role. You will define and own Goway's technical operations discipline: service levels, incident management, change control, observability and operational readiness, and you will make them the standard across our technology organisation. You will work alongside other Technology leaders. You will own the technology operations of our platform. You will have the CTO's mandate and backing to build the practice.

What will be your key responsibilities?

Reliability and service management

Define, publish and report service levels and service-level objectives for revenue-critical services, starting with quoting, booking, payment and traveller servicing.
Own incident management end to end: severity definitions, escalation, incident command, communication during an incident, and post-incident review with corrective actions.
Own RCA and problem management.
Own change and release management as a company standard, balancing delivery throughput against change failure rate.
Build observability sufficient to detect degradation.
Own disaster recovery and business continuity for platform services, tested and documented on a stated cadence.

Integration and supplier platform operations

Monitoring of integration paths, error and failure-rate thresholds, and defined fallback behaviour when a partner degrades.
Maintain a dependency map of the external platforms our revenue-generating flows rely on, with assessed operational risk and mitigation for each.
Own operational readiness for new integrations and new product lines entering the platform.
Own the operational reliability of automation and data pipelines in production.

Platform and cloud operations

Day-to-day operation of the AWS and managed hosting infrastructure serving our platform estate: environments, provisioning, patching and lifecycle management.
Own hosting cost governance: visibility by service, a unit-cost measure, and an annual optimisation target.
Lead capacity planning against forecast booking and travel volumes.
Reduce manual, repeatable operational work through automation.
Address seasonal capacity planning, change freezes and enhanced coverage aligned to our booking and departure peaks and to new product launches.

Vendors, partners and compliance

Platform, hosting and integration partner relationships: SLA definition, enforcement and structured performance review.
Reduce single points of dependency, whether on a vendor or an individual.
Partner with security on vulnerability management, patch compliance, access control and audit readiness.

Practice leadership and stakeholder engagement

Build and maintain a multi-year technical operations roadmap aligned to Goway's growth plans.
Report operational performance, risk and investment needs to the CTO and executive team in business terms.

What are we looking for?

Required

8 or more years in platform operations, technical operations, infrastructure or site reliability engineering, including 5 or more years in a lead or leadership capacity.
Demonstrated accountability for the availability and performance of a revenue-critical transactional platform.
Evidence of having built operational practice where little existed: SLOs, incident management, change control and observability introduced from the ground up, with measurable improvement to show for it.
Hands-on depth in AWS, including cost management and multi-environment operation.
Substantial experience operating and governing third-party platforms and integrations, including holding vendors to service levels.
Ability to set standards and drive adoption across teams.
Ability to communicate operational risk and performance.

Preferred

Experience stabilising and operationalising new systems.
Infrastructure-as-code and container orchestration experience.
AWS Certified DevOps Engineer (Professional), or AWS Certified CloudOps Engineer (Associate). Solutions Architect certifications are welcome, but less relevant to this role than the operations-focused ones.
Bachelor's degree in computer science, information technology, engineering or equivalent practical experience.

What can you expect from Goway?

Imagine working for a company where your career feels like an adventure. At Goway, you’ll join a global community that supports one another:
We offer a competitive salary accompanied by performance incentives, and we place real importance on time away from work, such as paid personal days for when life calls for them and your birthday off each year.
Our commitment to professional growth means you’ll have access to continuous learning and industry-leading training that keeps you at the forefront of travel innovation.
You’ll enjoy generous paid time off, including [three] weeks of vacation, [six] personal days, and a dedicated day off to celebrate your birthday.
Travel is in our DNA, so you’ll enjoy exclusive perks and discounts on worldwide getaways.
Since we operate across Toronto, Vancouver, Los Angeles, Manila, Sydney, and beyond, you’ll collaborate across cultures and shape a career path that reflects your ambitions.
Goway is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate differences and are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace for everyone. We appreciate every applicant’s interest. Please be advised that only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

How To Apply

If this role feels like your next step, click "Apply Now" to create your profile, upload your CV, and share a few details about yourself. Our talent team reviews every application, and if your experience aligns with our needs, we will reach out to set up the next step.

AI Screening Disclosure

To help us fairly and efficiently review applications, we use an automated screening process to assess responses to pre-determined questions. This initial step ensures all candidates are evaluated consistently. Qualified applicants will be reviewed by our recruitment team for further consideration.

Additional Notes

Goway Travel Ltd will retain applications, notifications, and records related to this posting for three years, reflecting our commitment to fair and equitable hiring practices.

Recruitment Scams & Fraud Warning

Please be aware of any suspicious emails or WhatsApp activity from individuals pretending to be recruiters or senior personnel at Goway Travel. We will never ask you to install an app during the recruitment process. If you receive a message of this nature, please ignore it and report it to Goway.

About Goway

Founded in Toronto in 1970 by Australian economist Bruce Hodge, Goway has evolved from a one-person dream into a family-owned global leader in tailor-made travel. With our headquarters in Toronto and hubs in Vancouver, Los Angeles, Sydney, and Manila, our team of over 800 talented employees designs travel experiences in more than 115 countries across all seven continents. We’re united by a passion for travel and are committed to doing the right thing: supporting diversity, equity, inclusion, and sustainable tourism that enriches local communities. Whether working remotely or side by side in one of our offices, we operate as one forward-thinking team, transforming wanderlust into life-changing adventures for our fellow Globetrotters. Discover more at goway.com.

About UJA Federation of Greater Toronto

At UJA Federation of Greater Toronto, our vision is to lead the most vibrant Jewish community in North America - a community characterized by its diversity, unity, compassion, generosity and commitment to Jewish values. Together with our philanthropic, volunteer and professional leadership, we’re changing lives.
As one of North America’s leading Jewish non-profits, UJA Federation of Greater Toronto works to preserve and strengthen the quality of Jewish life in Greater Toronto, Canada, Israel and around the world. UJA advances this mission through fundraising, programs, and research focused on our strategic pillars: fighting poverty and improving well-being, growing Jewish education and identity, countering antisemitism and hate, and strengthening connections with Israel and Jewish communities worldwide.
About the Opportunity

The team is looking to amplify and strengthen our fundraising strategy. As part of this initiative, we are hiring an Associate Director, Data Analytics & Prospecting
to own UJA's donor intelligence ecosystem — driving the data strategy, prospecting vision, and analytical frameworks that equip leadership, frontline fundraisers and operational teams with the intelligence they need to deepen cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and campaign performance across the organization. Reporting to the Senior Director of Data, Analytics and Reporting, this role serves as the operational lead to the Senior Director within the function and acts as delegate to the Senior Director when needed.
Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Strategic Leadership & Organizational Influence
Own and evolve UJA's end-to-end donor intelligence ecosystem, encompassing analytics strategy, prospect identification, data governance, and performance measurement.
Serve as a strategic operational lead alongside the Senior Director, driving the vision and roadmap for how data and prospecting power UJA's fundraising goals.
Act as delegate to the Senior Director in their absence, representing the function to senior leadership and ensuring continuity of strategic priorities.
Drive organization-wide decisions by translating donor intelligence into fundraising strategy — influencing campaign planning, gift officer deployment, portfolio design, and solicitation priorities.
Present insights, strategic recommendations, and performance reporting to executive leadership, and key stakeholders across the organization.
Champion a data-driven culture across the Integrated Development division, shaping how teams think about and use donor intelligence in their work.

Team Leadership & Cross-Functional Impact
Lead, mentor, and develop a team of two direct reports, fostering analytical excellence, professional growth, and high performance.
Spearhead cross-functional initiatives with Research, IT/Salesforce, Marketing, and frontline fundraising teams to embed analytics and prospecting insights into day-to-day operations.
Build and strengthen collaborative partnerships with senior fundraisers and division leaders, serving as a trusted advisor on donor strategy, capacity analysis, and prospect prioritization.
Establish and continuously improve standards, workflows, and best practices that scale the function's impact across the organization.

Donor Analytics & Performance Accountability
Design and own predictive models, donor scoring methodologies, and segmentation strategies that directly contribute to pipeline growth, major gift acquisition, and campaign performance targets.
Develop and maintain executive-level dashboards and reporting that connect analytics outputs to fundraising outcomes — tracking prospect conversion, portfolio health, upgrade rates, and campaign progress.
Deliver strategic portfolio and capacity analysis that equips operational teams with the intelligence they need to optimize fundraiser assignments, close capacity gaps, and act on high-potential upgrade and re-engagement opportunities.
Establish the KPIs and success metrics that hold the donor intelligence function accountable to fundraising impact, and ensure the resulting data sets are delivered to the operations team to inform execution and performance tracking
Evaluate and implement emerging technologies, including AI and automation, to deepen donor intelligence capabilities and accelerate prospecting at scale.
Establish and enforce data quality standards and governance practices to ensure accuracy and integrity across all systems and outputs.

Prospect Strategy & Pipeline Development
Set the strategic direction for prospect research and identification, ensuring the function proactively feeds the major gifts and campaign pipeline with qualified, high-value prospects.
Oversee the delivery of timely, high-quality research profiles, briefings, and due diligence that enable senior fundraisers to engage with confidence.
Drive innovation in prospect identification through wealth screening, data mining, predictive analytics, and community network analysis.
Develop and refine prospecting policies, processes, and frameworks that support the Integrated Development division's growth objectives.

Qualifications:

Relevant education or equivalent experience.
7+ years of progressive experience in fundraising analytics, prospect research, data strategy, or nonprofit development, with increasing strategic leadership responsibility.
3+ years of experience managing, mentoring, and developing staff, with demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and influence beyond direct reports.
Passionate advocate and visible champion of UJA’s mission, values, and goals, inspiring others through action and unwavering commitment to advancing our shared purpose.
Proven track record of driving fundraising outcomes through data — not just delivering reports, but shaping strategy and influencing organizational decisions.
Deep expertise in predictive modeling, donor scoring, portfolio segmentation, and performance measurement frameworks.
Proficient with CRM systems (Salesforce preferred) and experienced working with large, complex datasets.
Strong understanding of AI and emerging technologies, with a track record of implementing tools that drive efficiency and strategic advantage.
Executive-level communication and presentation skills, with comfort presenting to senior leadership, and key stakeholders across the organization.
Familiarity with donor intelligence and wealth screening platforms such as iWave or similar tools.
Actively engaged in, and/or familiar with groups, networks, or organizations in the Jewish community, with the ability to engage, build relationships, and surface potential new donor prospects.
Strong project management skills with the ability to balance strategic priorities and operational demands.
Maintains a high degree of discretion, confidentiality, and respect for donor privacy.

We are looking for an experienced Director of Finance, a leader to oversee the financial direction of our clients' organization in Perth County, Ontario. This role provides strategic guidance across planning, reporting, controls, and performance management while supporting sound business decisions with accurate financial insight. Responsibilities:

La confiance est le fondement de chaque expérience client et de chaque flux de travail basé sur l’IA que nous proposons. Nous sommes ouverts aux candidatures à distance provenant des États-Unis et du Canada.

Représenter la stratégie de confiance d’Autodesk auprès des clients professionnels, des partenaires stratégiques et des forums sectoriels

Position: Head of Enterprise Architecture & Applications

Location: Vaudreuil-Dorion, QC

Flexible Hybrid Work Model: We support collaboration and connection through a hybrid work arrangement requiring a minimum of 3 days per week on-site.

Status: Permanent, full-time (1)

Lead the architecture behind a growing North American business
.

Quadra’s CRM, ERP, transportation, analytics, employee experience, regulatory compliance and AI platforms are core to how we operate across North America.

We are creating the Head of Enterprise Architecture & Applications role to unify these platforms under one architecture and delivery standard. The role leads Quadra Digital’s (QD) Design Authority
pillar alongside Business Authority and Digital Workplace & Infrastructure.

Reporting to our CDIO, this visible, hands-on leader will guide the team, own the budget and investment portfolio, review designs and delivery practices, and partner with business leaders to turn priorities into measurable value.

At Quadra, we put people first so that together, we can reimagine what's possible.

For more than 50 years, Quadra has placed its 650+ employees at the heart of its success across North America. We offer an engaging culture, a collaborative and human environment, and a high level of autonomy and flexibility. Joining Quadra means being part of a professional, innovative and passionate team, within a growing, people-focused organization certified Great Place to Work®. We have also been recognized as one of Canada's Best Managed Companies for over 20 years.

A leader in the distribution of chemicals and ingredients, Quadra continues to grow with a strong commitment to its teams. If you are driven by excellence, you belong here!

Why This Role Matters

Own enterprise architecture, business capability and process architecture, enterprise information architecture and master data governance, and AI-solution architecture and governance across CRM, ERP, transportation, analytics, employee experience and AI, as well as Quadra-critical regulatory platforms (Intelligent SDS Authoring, labelling, product stewardship and compliance).
Lead the platform managers, product owners, delivery squads, project management and QA under one intake and delivery model.
Enforce design, security, testing and release standards to make delivery predictable.
Own the digital budget and investment portfolio with Finance, the CDIO and business leaders.
Measure digital outcomes through revenue, margin, cost, service, working capital and productivity.

What would be your main responsibilities as Head of Enterprise Architecture & Applications?:

Define and govern target architecture across applications, integrations, data, security and AI; approve major designs, configurations, developments and releases.
Directly manage the platform managers, product owners, project management, QA, development and functional specialists—setting priorities, capacity, performance and development expectations.
Own delivery from qualified demand through release and Level 3 support, including application security, published SLAs and clear technical ownership.
Set and enforce delivery standards for requirements, backlogs, acceptance criteria, UAT, Jira, testing and Definition of Done.
Bring the roadmap and enhancement portfolio to the quarterly QD Prioritisation Board and provide technical validation for production changes.
Map business capabilities, processes and applications to align investments, reduce duplication and challenge proposed solutions early.
Evaluate AI and regulatory platforms (e.g., SDS authoring, labelling, product stewardship) against security, compliance, integration, data and business-value requirements.
Own digital opex and capex planning, business-case quality, stage gates and value realization with Finance, Business Authority and the relevant Key Account.
Advise business leaders on roadmap, feasibility, cost and sequencing; lead vendor selection and performance management.
Assess and integrate application landscapes acquired through mergers and acquisitions.

What are the required qualifications and experience to succeed in this role:

15+ years in enterprise/solution architecture, application management or digital delivery, including 5+ years leading specialists or Product Owners.
Bachelor’s degree in information systems, computer science, software or industrial engineering, or equivalent experience.
Proven design-authority experience across multiple platforms, including solution, integration and release approvals.
Hands-on experience with at least two of: Salesforce, Oracle JD Edwards E1 or similar ERP, Oracle OTM/TMS
Strong integration and API architecture experience across ERP, CRM and TMS in cloud or hybrid environments.
Strong business acumen and ability to translate commercial, operational and financial priorities into practical technology decisions.
Strong oral presentation skills: clear, confident communication of complex ideas, analysis outcomes, architectural concepts and design decisions—and their justification—tailored to diverse audiences and stakeholder needs.
Experience governing requirements, backlogs, Jira or Azure DevOps, SDLC controls, change management, segregation of duties and audit/compliance reviews.
Demonstrated creative thinking and ability to challenge stakeholders, defend decisions, bring stakeholders to understand and accept new approaches and deliver measurable business benefits.
Proven experience owning and managing significant technology operating and capital budgets and investment portfolios, in partnership with Finance and business leaders, with accountability for forecasting, prioritization, cost control and value realization.
Advanced written and verbal communication skills in both French and English.
Assets: MuleSoft or similar API integration platform experience; TOGAF, Zachman, AWS/Azure, Microsoft Power Platform, Power BI/Fabric, Agile/SAFe or Scrum certification; distribution, chemicals, supply chain, regulatory/product stewardship or post-acquisition integration experience.

Working Conditions

Permanent, full-time senior leadership role based in Vaudreuil-Dorion, with three full office days per week.
Travel up to 15% across Canada and the United States.
Occasional off-hours involvement for major releases, incidents or critical business events.

You Might Be the Right Person If…

You are a pragmatic, hands-on leader who can review architecture, lead a team and own a budget. You set standards appropriate for a 650-person company, enforce them without becoming a bottleneck, challenge unclear value and hold delivery accountable for measurable results.

We want to meet you!

Here Are Some Of The Perks Of Choosing Quadra

Permanent, full-time leadership opportunity: Join a growing organization where you can make a meaningful impact and help shape future success.
Competitive compensation & performance incentives: We recognize and reward strong performance with a competitive salary and incentive program.
Lead with impact: Partner with talented teams and contribute to strategic initiatives that drive business growth and operational excellence.
Comprehensive benefits package: Medical, dental, healthcare spending account, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and access to virtual healthcare.
Retirement savings program: Build for the future with our matched pension plan.
Flexible time off: Vacation, personal days, and wellness initiatives that support work-life balance.
Professional growth opportunities: Expand your leadership capabilities through challenging projects, cross-functional collaboration, and ongoing development.
Values-driven culture: Be part of a collaborative organization built on integrity, accountability, entrepreneurship, and care for people.
Family-owned with long-term vision: Enjoy the stability of a privately owned company that takes a long-term approach to investing in its people and business.
Award-winning workplace: Proudly recognized as a Great Place to Work® and one of Canada's Best Managed Companies.
Inclusive and collaborative environment: We value diverse perspectives and foster a culture where people can thrive and contribute.
Community involvement: Participate in volunteer and community initiatives that make a positive impact.
Recognition and appreciation: Celebrate achievements through our recognition programs and culture of acknowledgment.
And much more!

Who We Are

At Northland, we’re enablers of change, united by our journey to transform the energy sector into the foundation for a sustainable future.

Since our inception, we’ve been early movers in the energy industry, adopting new initiatives that pave the way for communities across the globe and helping forge their path towards a carbon-neutral landscape.

We’re a different kind of independent power producer. As developers, owners and operators who are at the forefront of the energy transition, we’re uniquely positioned to leave a lasting impact in the regions where we operate. We’ve expanded our business across Canada, the United States, Latin America, Europe and Asia to become a global leader, all by bringing together industry experts to find solutions with an entrepreneurial mindset.

While our work powers communities across the globe, Northland is powered by our people.

What You’ll Do

The Head of Market Intelligence & Analytics is accountable for building and leading Northland’s enterprise market intelligence and analytics capabilities. The role establishes independent, decision-ready views of wholesale power and related commodity markets, translates those views into consistent commercial assumptions, and ensures those insights are applied across strategy, development, M&A, financing, market operations, asset management and portfolio optimization.

Establish scalable in-house forecasting and modelling capabilities, guide market analysts and technical resources, and determine where external specialists remain appropriate. The successful candidate combines deep electricity-market judgment, strong quantitative fluency, practical model-development oversight and the ability to communicate complex market dynamics to executive and investment audiences.

Build a global centre of expertise that protects, optimizes and sustainably grows the commercial value of Northland’s contracted and merchant portfolio, while underpinning new development opportunities with rigorous market intelligence, forward curves, fundamental analysis, scenario modelling and asset-level commercial insight. The initial priority is to establish repeatable capabilities for core markets and then scale them across Northland’s broader international portfolio.

The role is required to work in the Toronto office 4 days per week with one flexible day to work from home.

Key Responsibilities

Market Intelligence

Working with the Director of Regulatory & Market Affairs, lead the development of Northland’s wholesale market strategy across relevant jurisdictions, identifying long-term trends, structural opportunities, downside risks and implications for capital allocation.
Develop and maintain internal views on supply and demand evolution, market design, natural gas, carbon, capacity, ancillary services, environmental attributes and other material value drivers.
Create a consistent market-outlook and assumption-setting process for use across business cases, investment decisions, budgets, forecasts and commercial strategies.
Working with the Director of Regulatory & Market Affairs, translate market, policy and regulatory developments into alerts and actionable recommendations for internal stakeholders.

Forecasting, Modelling and Analytics

Own the roadmap and delivery of internal forward curves (short and long term), market-level fundamental models and supporting analytical tools, beginning with priority markets and scaling as business needs and capability mature.
Set modelling architecture, scenarios, input assumptions and quality standards; provide sufficient technical depth to review, challenge and guide Python-based and commercial-platform model development.
Develop scenario and sensitivity analysis covering load growth, generation additions and retirements, fuel and carbon prices, weather, transmission build-out, policy, technology costs, capture rates and operating constraints.
Build dashboards and repeatable reporting that make market views, assumptions, risks and forecast changes transparent and accessible to decision-makers.

Asset, Portfolio and Transaction Decision Support

Lead market analysis supporting development, acquisitions, divestitures, financing, budgeting and optimization of operating assets, including merchant revenue forecasts and high-level asset valuations.
Provide dispatch, capture-price, congestion, basis, curtailment, ancillary-service and other commercial analyses appropriate to each market, technology and contract structure.
Support hedging decisions, PPA and offtake strategy, competitive bid and RFP analysis, route-to-market decisions, commercial operating strategies and portfolio risk discussions.
Partner with Finance and transaction teams on lender, sale and investment processes, using independent third-party forecasts where external validation is required while maintaining a clear Northland view.

Capability, Data and Model Governance

Establish a practical build-versus-buy strategy for data, tools, modelling platforms and external advisory support, with clear accountabilities, budgets and service standards.
Implement model governance covering documentation, version control, assumption ownership, change management, validation, back-testing [CS3.1]and independent challenge proportionate to the decision being supported.
Define data requirements and partner with Technical Performance Management, Data, Digital and IT teams to develop reliable and scalable market-data infrastructure.
Manage relationships with market-data providers, modelling vendors and consultants; reduce avoidable external dependence while retaining specialist support where it adds value or is required by third parties.

Leadership and Stakeholder Partnerships

Build, lead and develop a high-performing market intelligence and analytics team, setting priorities and balancing recurring market coverage with transaction and asset-specific demands.
Act as a senior thought partner to Development, Regulatory & Market Affairs, Government Affairs, Asset Management, Risk, Finance and executive leadership.
Present complex market conclusions, model limitations and key uncertainties in a clear, decision-oriented manner for investment committees, senior leaders and boards.

Who You Are

A strategic market leader: You possess deep expertise in wholesale power and commodity markets and can translate market trends, risks and opportunities into commercial strategy, investment decisions and portfolio outcomes. 
An analytical and technically credible expert: You combine strong quantitative capabilities with hands-on experience in market modelling, forecasting and data analytics, bringing the ability to challenge assumptions, interrogate models and drive rigorous decision-making. 
A builder of capabilities: You thrive in creating and scaling new functions, frameworks and governance models, balancing internal capability development with the strategic use of external tools, data and advisory support. 
A trusted advisor and communicator: You can distill complex market dynamics, forecasts and uncertainties into clear, actionable insights that influence executives, investment committees and boards. 
A collaborative and inspiring leader: You build high-performing teams, foster technical excellence and partner effectively across functions, geographies and stakeholder groups to deliver business value. 

Qualifications And Experience

Bachelor’s degree in economics, engineering, mathematics, statistics, finance, computer science or a related discipline; a relevant master’s degree or MBA is an asset.
10 or more years of progressive experience in wholesale power markets, energy-market analytics, fundamental forecasting, commercial strategy or a closely related field, including leadership of people or major analytical programs.
Demonstrated experience developing or directing power-market forecasts, fundamental models, dispatch and revenue analysis, scenario frameworks and asset-valuation inputs.
Deep understanding of electricity-market design and commercial drivers; experience across more than one ISO/RTO or international market is strongly preferred.
Experience across a diverse technology portfolio, such as wind, solar, storage and gas-fired generation, and with contracted and merchant revenue structures.
Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders, manage external advisors and convert complex analytical work into clear commercial decisions.

What’s In It for You:

Our employees are the driving force behind our achievements. We are unwavering in our commitment to not only recognise your contributions but also to empower
you to excel in every aspect of your life. Here's a glimpse of why Northland is the place where you'll truly thrive: 

Thoughtful benefits – A competitive RRSP matching scheme of 8%; extended health, dental and vision benefits for yourself and your immediate family from day one; paid parental leave; Accident and Life Insurance and disability benefits are just a few of the benefits you’ll be able to access. 
Wellbeing first – Staying true to our taking care of ourselves and each other value, you will have access to our global Wellness Program and Employee Assistance Program, including access to mental health resources. 
Floating days and Birthdays off – As part of our commitment to promoting a healthy work-life balance, you will get your birthday off so you can celebrate however you choose! You will also receive three additional days off annually to observe any other events that are important to you.

We hire talented and passionate people from different backgrounds. If you’re excited about a role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with this job description, we still encourage you to apply. Learn more about our diversity, inclusion and belonging commitments.
