User experience: Owning the end-to-end product experience across the platform — how users discover, adopt, build with, and get value from it — including the self-service builder, templates, and connector catalog as part of a coherent whole.
Product analytics: Building and maintaining adoption dashboards, usage telemetry, and value-realization measurement to drive decisions
Delivery partnership: Partnering with engineering on acceptance criteria, backlog, and delivery quality, staying engaged to protect the user outcome
Responsible AI in practice: Embedding the safety, governance, and transparency standards set by the AI Group's Safety and Responsible AI function into the roadmap and release gates
Market awareness: Conducting competitive and market analysis to inform platform direction

You're our ideal candidate if you:

Have 8+ years of product management experience, including 3+ in AI/ML products or enterprise platforms
Have a strong product-experience and design sensibility — able to shape how users discover, adopt, and succeed with a product, not only what features it has.
Have a deep working understanding of agentic AI: LLMs, tool-use, MCP connectors, RAG, and multi-agent orchestration
Have owned and delivered a product roadmap with measurable adoption outcomes
Are strongly analytical — able to define and track adoption metrics, build dashboards, and interpret telemetry
Have the technical fluency to partner with engineers on architecture decisions without writing code

Display creative thinking and consulting skills to deliver a continually improving service for the client

Experience with GSOC and intelligence tools, including threat monitoring, OSINT, and SOCMINT platforms

a leading global player in international healthcare and insurance solutions for internationally expatriate individuals and local high net worth individual in emerging countries.

It mainly operates as an insurance seller of health coverage products for corporates, individual expatriates, international students and travelers, and as a Third-Party Administrator for health insurance related claims.

The CFO will be relied upon to provide timely and meaningful monthly financial reporting, assist with the analysis of growth opportunities in foreign markets, prepare and monitor cash flow forecasts and provide insight into the ongoing strategic planning objectives for the organization.

Management of the adequate financial and accounting processes:
review and, if need be, recommendation for improvement, of the financial and accounting procedures and policies: revenue and expenses recognition, follow up and recognition of cash (insurer’s / own cash), balance sheet presentation;
ensure cash management is performed according to the Group rules and professional best practices;
check compliance with the accounting standards, and with local financial regulations;

Pluriannual financial business plans and yearly budget; recurring reforecast;

monthly, quarterly and yearly reporting sent to the MSH group’s management, to shareholders (including the Group reporting), and when need be to external auditors, in relation to all financial related information: budget, forecasts, management reporting (including headcount and litigation related provisions), financial accounts, cash management, impairment tests…;
ad hoc analysis of the business development, profitability profile and cash management outcome of the subsidiaries

Contribution to acquisitions and local development from the financial standpoint, within the frame of the acquisition policies and procedures of Group:
financial analysis of the target performance;
review of the business plan, analysis of value and financial support to the various steps of the negotiation;
supervision of financial due diligences;

Ensure all tax reports are delivered in due course and adequate form, and that all relevant taxes are acquitted
Optimize, within the frame of relevant regulation, tax incurred by the group companies;

Risk and compliance

Connection is everything. It drives us to innovate, explore, and stay close to what matters to us most. At Bell, we’re building a more connected future through world-class networks, AI-powered solutions, and digital experiences that elevate how people live, work, and play every day.

We believe in empowering people. That’s why we equip our teams with cutting-edge technology, AI tools, and a collaborative environment that supports creativity and growth. Want to be part of a diverse team where your work makes a real impact? If you’re inspired by innovation that advances how people connect and transforms what’s possible, you belong on #TeamBell.

At Bell, your skills and expertise will help set us apart as we continue to be the leading provider of digital connections and next generation services to businesses and governments.

Summary

Bell AI Fabric is building Canada's largest sovereign AI infrastructure platform. As Director, Strategy, you will work at the centre of its most important strategic, commercial, and operational priorities, helping shape decisions that will influence the future of AI infrastructure in Canada and ensuring those decisions translate into action and results.

This is a highly visible internal consulting and execution role with unusual breadth and access. Working directly with senior executives, Bell AI Fabric Board members, governments, customers, investors, and strategic partners, you will tackle complex questions with no obvious answer, bring clarity to competing perspectives, and help move the organization from discussion to decision to delivery.

Your work will span corporate strategy, partnerships, government engagement, commercial negotiations, major customer opportunities, and organizational execution. You will build the plans and governance required to deliver, step into critical moments where additional leadership or problem-solving is needed and see recommendations through to real-world outcomes.

This is a unique opportunity for a strategy or consulting professional who wants to help build something consequential, learn quickly across a wide range of issues, and have visible impact. You do not need to arrive knowing every part of the business; success will come from curiosity, sound judgment, strong execution, and a willingness to invest the effort required to figure things out.

Act as a trusted strategy partner and extension of the executive team, bringing independent judgment, anticipating what is required, and providing hands-on leadership on Bell AI Fabric's highest-priority opportunities and issues.
Lead structured problem-solving on complex questions related to growth, market positioning, commercial models, partnerships, major initiatives, and organizational scalability; distill complexity into clear choices, decisions, and actions.
Rapidly develop command of unfamiliar commercial, technical, operational, and stakeholder issues by identifying the critical facts, connecting perspectives, and isolating what matters most.

Evaluate and advance strategic partnerships, commercial opportunities, government initiatives, customer opportunities, and other priorities that support long-term growth.

A strong orientation toward quality and detail, with the ability to reconcile analyses, narratives, decisions, and deliverables across multiple workstreams.
Sound commercial judgment and negotiation capability, with the persistence to help close agreements, decisions, and outstanding projects.
Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to govern, align, and mobilize senior stakeholders without formal authority.
High capacity and strong organization, with the ability to manage several urgent priorities, sustain pace, and improve the completeness and quality of the work.
Ability to operate with increasing independence, anticipate needs, step into unfamiliar issues, and invest the effort required to build understanding and deliver results.

Management consulting experience or equivalent training in structured problem-solving, analysis, executive communication, and high-quality delivery.
Strong research and synthesis capability, intellectual curiosity, and a demonstrated interest in learning and becoming credible on new topics.
Experience supporting partnerships, complex commercial negotiations, or major infrastructure and technology initiatives.

What's In It for You?

You won't inherit a playbook. You'll write it. You'll define the operating model, the culture, and the technical direction for a brand-new function, and shape a small, sharp team of 2 from day one. You'll report directly to the CTO and work closely with the Senior Leadership Team, as well as the Engineering, Product, Sales, and People teams. You'll tackle big questions like how to govern AI agents connected to company systems, and your answers will set policy at Klue. As Klue grows, so do the team and your scope. You have the power to shape what that looks like.

What You'll Do

Own security posture and incident readiness. Mature how Klue prevents, detects, and responds to security issues. Design the incident response process and governance, and make sure everyone knows their role before something goes wrong.
Run the compliance engine. Own the annual audit cycle against SOC 2 Type II, NIST CSF, and BSIMM, plus penetration testing, from evidence collection to a successful finish. Build audit methodology and documentation that make reviews faster and less painful for the whole company.
Be the security answer for go-to-market. Keep customer questionnaires, external assessments, and audits moving on time. Review and negotiate data protection agreements and security exhibits with customers and vendors so what we sign matches what we do.
Govern vendors, data, and privacy. Run full-spectrum vendor reviews, including sub-processor qualification. Own DLP, data retention, and the privacy framework for an international customer base, including data subject access requests.
Set the rules for AI and high-risk access. Own AI security governance: policies, risk acceptance, data handling, and permissioning for AI tools, agents, and integrations connected to company systems. Define and enforce access governance for high-risk systems, including admin access reviews, service accounts vs. individual credentials, and controls on sensitive logs and data.
Make security engineering's job easier. Set the security and compliance standard for Engineering's security work. Give the team the tooling, policy, and guidelines to build against, and translate their technical work into terms leadership and customers can act on.
Equip and enable every Kluebee. Own devices, access, and tooling across the full employee lifecycle. Manage the vendors behind our IT stack, set and hit reliability targets (SLOs) for corporate systems, and replace ad hoc fixes with repeatable processes that scale. Partner with People so onboarding and offboarding run smoothly. (Product infrastructure stays with Engineering.)

What Success Looks Like

One team, one roadmap. Within two quarters, Security, Compliance, and IT operate as one team with a shared roadmap and a regular operating rhythm.
Customers get fast, consistent answers. Questionnaires, audits, and sub-processor reviews are completed on time and in a repeatable way.
AI and access are governed, not improvised. High-risk systems and AI tools are covered by clear, documented policy, and admin access reviews are routine, not reactive.
Corporate systems are reliable. You define clear SLOs in your first quarter, and Klue meets or beats them.
We're ready when it counts. Incident response governance is documented and understood, and Engineering's security engineers have the tooling and guidelines to respond fast.
Day 1 just works. Every new Kluebee has working equipment and access on their first day, with no scrambling.
The budget is a set of clear choices. You actively manage the function's budget and make defensible tradeoffs between tooling, vendors, and headcount.
You're the default owner. The CTO and SLT turn to you for security, compliance, and IT. Engineering and GTM teams see you as the partner who makes their job easier, not another layer to work around.

What You Bring

Must Haves

You've run security and compliance at a company handling sensitive customer data. You're comfortable owning DLP, data retention, and privacy frameworks, and you can work through a security questionnaire or audit without panic.
You've led IT operations for a whole company, covering equipment, access, and tooling.
You know security frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST) and global privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA) in depth.
You're comfortable with ambiguity and building without a playbook.
You communicate clearly with both technical peers and non-technical leaders, and can explain a risk to an engineer and to a CEO.
You've negotiated data protection agreements and security exhibits in vendor and customer contracts.
You understand AI security and governance: data retention commitments, access and permissioning for AI agents and integrations, and risk acceptance for AI tooling.
You've worked closely with product and engineering teams to turn security and compliance goals into reality.

Nice-to-Haves

You've owned a DevOps and/or security engineering function inside a larger engineering org.
You've brought previously siloed security, compliance, and IT teams together under one roof.
You know privacy and data residency frameworks for an international customer base.
You've managed distributed or hybrid teams.

The Associate Director, AI & Automation leads the implementation of artificial intelligence and process automation adoption for Thompson Rivers University. Reporting to the CIO and serving as a key advisor, this role supports TRU's AI and automation portfolio:
setting strategic direction and governance standards,
adoption review,
directing the Power Team initiative and future programs,
and building the team, partnerships, and institutional capability needed to scale responsible AI use across the university.

Some of the key accountabilities for this role are:

Strategic Leadership & Governance

Support TRU's institution-wide AI and automation strategy, setting direction, priorities, and success metrics in alignment with the university's strategic plan.
Adjudicating risk classification and review of proposed AI and automation use cases (e.g., under the Safe Start framework).
Serve as a key advisor to the CIO on AI strategy, opportunity, and risk; hold a standing voice in ITS leadership team.
Set institutional standards and policy guardrails for responsible AI and automation adoption.
Direct and mentor a growing team in the design, governance, and deployment of AI and automation solutions.
Maintain working command of MLOps principles (model versioning, monitoring, and deployment) to guide the team's technical practice.

Strategic Planning & Program Delivery

Develop and execute the multi-year roadmap for integrating AI and RPA into administrative and academic-support workflows, with Power Team as the flagship program.
Identify, prioritize, and business-case new automation and AI opportunities based on time, accuracy, consistency, and risk impact.
Set and track program-level goals (time saved, error reduction, adoption, satisfaction) and report progress against a defined roadmap, not just individual pilots.
Own budget planning and vendor/contract management for the AI and automation portfolio, including delegated authority for AI tool and automation procurement decisions.

Team Leadership & Resourcing

Build, structure, and grow the AI & Automation team, with accountability for hiring, performance management, and career development.
Define team structure and resourcing plans that scale with institutional demand, including a stated growth trajectory as the portfolio expands.

Training & Capability Building

Direct the design and delivery of training and enablement programs for administrative leaders and support staff on AI and automation tools.
Foster a culture of curiosity, experimentation, and responsible use across the institution.

Institutional & External Engagement

Represent TRU externally on AI and automation practice, including engagement with the BC/national peer community, sector consultations, and conference or panel participation.
Build and maintain relationships with administrative leaders, ITS teams, AI/automation vendors, and industry experts.
Contributes to the institutional narrative around AI and automation, building stakeholder trust and sustained momentum through regular communication of progress and outcomes.

Feedback, Metrics & Continuous Improvement

Establish a portfolio-level measurement framework and report efficiency gains, adoption rates, risk posture, and challenges to senior leadership on a regular cadence.
Collect and act on feedback from training sessions and pilot/program implementations to refine strategy, tools, and governance.
Hold the team accountable for outcomes, documenting both successes and lessons learned to inform the next phase of the roadmap

Required Skills, Experience and Knowledge

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Administration, or a related field required; Master's degree in a related field strongly preferred and weighted favourably.
At least five (5) years of leadership experience, ideally within a post-secondary or complex institutional setting, including experience building or scaling a team.
At least three (3) years of hands-on experience in software development, scripting, or automation engineering, with a strong foundation in coding best practices.
Demonstrated experience developing institutional policy, governance frameworks, or risk/adoption review processes — not solely technical delivery.
Experience managing vendor relationships, contracts, and budget for a technology program or portfolio.
Strong understanding of AI and RPA technologies and their institutional applications; prior experience building AI/ML platforms.
Familiarity with cloud AI/ML platforms such as AWS SageMaker, Azure Machine Learning, or equivalent.
Familiarity with organizational change management methodologies; experience leading change management and stakeholder engagement at an institutional level.
Excellent leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills, including experience representing an organization externally (peer institutions, sector bodies, conferences).
Ability to analyze data and feedback to drive continuous improvement across a program portfolio.

If the above position profile excites you and you would like to learn or know more about this great opportunity, then please contact Matt Norton, Associate Vice President Digital Strategies and Chief Information Officer, Information Technology Services at mnorton@tru.ca or call Matt at 250 852 6383 and please reference the position title.

jobs.title: Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, Trilogy (Remote) - $800,000/year USD
jobs.description:
Most finance executives inherit a system. You will redesign one, then decide where the capital goes.

Trilogy is looking for the executive who can turn a portfolio of businesses into a capital allocation system: continuously ranking where the next dollar should go, backing those decisions with rigorous models, and moving capital toward its highest-return uses. You will own the calls that matter: fund or kill a business line; invest or hold; acquire or walk away; refinance or pay down debt. Every recommendation must connect strategy to cash, liquidity, covenants, risk, and enterprise value.

Just as important, you will architect an AI-native finance function built to scale without decision bottlenecks. This does not mean sprinkling AI tools onto a traditional finance organization. You will redesign reporting, planning, controls, portfolio monitoring, and decision support around what AI and automation can now do. You won't need to personally build every workflow, but you must use AI deeply enough to know its edges: where it accelerates analysis, where it fails, and where expert judgment must take over. The result should be a smaller, more senior, higher-leverage finance organization rather than a growing pyramid of people and processes.

You will operate directly with Trilogy's CEO, board, lenders, and capital partners, with personal accountability for the financial truth behind major decisions. This is an $800K W-2 salaried role for someone who has already earned credibility at serious financial scale and now wants the mandate to compound enterprise value across an entire portfolio. If you want your impact measured by the quality of your capital decisions and the financial system you leave behind, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Allocating capital across the portfolio: Run capital and portfolio reviews, rank competing uses of capital on risk-adjusted return, and make clear fund, hold, restructure, exit, debt-paydown, or acquisition recommendations.
Architecting an AI-native finance system: Redesign planning, reporting, consolidation, controls, portfolio monitoring, and financial workflows around AI, automation, and scalable systems rather than additional headcount.
Driving investments and transactions: Build and defend the financial case for strategic investments, M&A, financing, and refinancing, including integrated models, downside scenarios, capital structure, covenant implications, and execution plans.
Owning board and capital-partner communication: Give the CEO, board, lenders, and capital partners fast, quantified, defensible truth, with recommendations that make the decision and trade-offs explicit.
Building a high-leverage finance leadership team: Set the bar for a small group of exceptional finance leaders while creating systems that allow new ventures and greater complexity to be absorbed without linear organizational growth.

What You Won’t Be Doing

Running finance as a reporting factory. Closing the books and producing audit workpapers are the Controller's responsibilities. Your job is to turn financial information into better capital decisions.
Building a large finance organization to handle complexity. Scale should come from better systems, AI leverage, automation, and exceptional people, not layers of management.
Adding AI as a superficial productivity tool. You will architect workflows around its real capabilities and limitations, which requires substantial firsthand use.
Producing strategy decks without financial consequences. Major recommendations must carry the integrated model, downside case, capital implications, and execution guardrails behind them.
Managing the board through narrative. The numbers, assumptions, risks, and recommended action should be clear enough to withstand scrutiny.

Executive Vice President And Chief Financial Officer Key Responsibilities

You will define and own the multi-year AI product strategy and roadmap for the Solutions business unit, spanning agentic commerce, discovery, offer optimization and partner operations. You will turn that strategy into funded priorities, make trade-offs with executives, partners and engineering, and own outcomes including partner revenue, adoption, model quality and cost to serve. Six months: The team is staffed with builders and operating for speed, with clear ownership and rhythms with AI Product Operations and engineering; multiple AI products have gone from idea to live partner test in weeks.

10 or more years in product, including several years leading and developing product managers or applied AI teams, ideally in a B2B or platform business.
Hands-on experience designing and shipping ML, LLM or agent-based products that customers pay for, with a practical understanding of model drift, evaluation, hallucination, latency and cost trade-offs.
A track record of accelerating teams, hiring and developing builders, and moving products from idea to prototype to live partner test.
Strong commercial instincts: you connect product decisions to revenue, margin and partner outcomes, and collaborate effectively with engineering, data science, design and partner-facing teams.
Clear, direct communication with executives, partners and technical teams. Experience in travel, loyalty, e-commerce, marketplaces or pricing is an asset but not mandatory.

Travel is about the moments that make a journey feel personal. At Plusgrade, we build the technology that makes those moments possible, from upgrade offers and loyalty experiences to revenue tools used by 575+ airline, hospitality, cruise, rail, and financial services partners worldwide.

Job Description

The Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Data Center Development organization leads the planning, design, and delivery of the next generation of Oracle’s global data center portfolio. We are seeking a Senior Director of Data Center Development to provide strategic leadership and organizational oversight for the design of mission-critical infrastructure across OCI’s rapidly expanding global footprint.

This role is responsible for establishing and executing OCI’s data center design strategy across a portfolio of large-scale, highly complex developments. The Senior Director will lead a team of design management professionals and provide executive-level oversight of multidisciplinary design activities spanning architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, controls, and mission-critical infrastructure systems.

The position requires a combination of organizational leadership, technical depth, design governance, and portfolio management. The successful candidate will establish clear design requirements, drive consistency across projects and delivery partners, manage technical risk, and ensure that OCI’s facilities meet established requirements for performance, reliability, resiliency, scalability, constructability, and operational readiness.

The Senior Director will serve as a senior technical and organizational leader within OCI Data Center Development, partnering closely with Construction, Engineering, Operations, Network, Capacity Planning, Energy, Security, and other internal organizations. The role will also provide senior-level direction to colocation partners, architects, engineers, consultants, contractors, and other external stakeholders responsible for delivering OCI

Responsibilities

Responsibilities:

Lead the Data Center Design Management function for an assigned global or multi-region portfolio of hyperscale and mission-critical infrastructure projects.
Establish organizational priorities, expectations, governance processes, and performance standards for the design management team.
Lead, develop, and mentor design managers and design leadership personnel, establishing clear accountability for project execution, technical quality, and professional development.
Provide portfolio-level oversight of multidisciplinary data center design across architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, controls, life safety, and supporting infrastructure systems.
Establish and maintain design governance throughout the project lifecycle, from early planning and Basis of Design development through schematic design, design development, construction documentation, construction support, commissioning, and record documentation.
Ensure projects maintain alignment with OCI technical requirements, design standards, operational requirements, reliability objectives, and infrastructure strategies.
Provide senior technical leadership for high-density compute environments, including mechanical systems, liquid cooling, electrical infrastructure, controls, and other mission-critical systems supporting next-generation cloud and AI infrastructure.
Drive consistent implementation and continuous improvement of OCI global data center design standards, specifications, design criteria, and best practices.
Establish effective design review, technical approval, change management, and decision-making processes across the portfolio.
Identify systemic and project-specific design risks and ensure appropriate mitigation, escalation, and resolution before those risks impact construction, schedule, cost, reliability, or operations.
Lead resolution of complex multidisciplinary technical issues requiring coordination across internal organizations, design consultants, construction teams, operators, and external delivery partners.
Partner with Construction, Engineering, Operations, Network, Capacity Planning, Energy, Security, and other OCI organizations to ensure infrastructure requirements are coordinated and incorporated into project designs.
Provide senior-level oversight of architects, engineers, consultants, colocation providers, and other design partners responsible for delivering OCI infrastructure.
Establish expectations for consultant scope, performance, technical quality, schedule adherence, and design deliverables.
Ensure Basis of Design, SD, DD, permit, IFC, and record design packages meet OCI requirements and are appropriately reviewed and approved.
Drive standardization and repeatability while maintaining the flexibility necessary to address regional requirements, site conditions, utility constraints, code requirements, and evolving technology.
Evaluate proposed design changes and deviations to determine portfolio-level impacts to reliability, operations, schedule, cost, standards, and future scalability.
Develop and monitor design performance metrics, portfolio risks, technical issues, and organizational priorities, providing clear reporting and recommendations to executive leadership.
Support strategic planning for future data center capacity, emerging technologies, new infrastructure architectures, and evolving cloud and AI requirements.
Represent OCI Data Center Design Management in executive reviews, technical workshops, partner engagements, design reviews, and other internal and external forums.
Build a culture of technical rigor, accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and disciplined design governance across the organization.

Required Qualifications:

Professional licensure required as a Registered Architect (RA) or Professional Engineer (PE).
Accredited degree in Architecture, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Structural Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
12+ years of progressively responsible experience in data center, mission-critical, industrial, or large-scale infrastructure design and development.
Significant leadership experience managing design professionals, multidisciplinary technical teams, and external architecture and engineering organizations.
Demonstrated experience leading large-scale hyperscale, cloud, colocation, or mission-critical infrastructure programs.
Strong multidisciplinary understanding of data center architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, controls, life safety, and supporting infrastructure systems.
Demonstrated ability to establish and manage design governance, standards, technical requirements, and change control across multiple concurrent projects.
Experience managing complex project portfolios involving multiple sites, delivery partners, consultants, and internal stakeholders.
Strong understanding of data center mechanical and cooling infrastructure, with experience in high-density and liquid-cooled environments strongly preferred.
Strong understanding of data center electrical distribution, resiliency strategies, controls, commissioning, and operational requirements.
Demonstrated ability to identify, communicate, and resolve complex technical and organizational risks.
Experience working within accelerated design and construction programs where schedule, scalability, repeatability, and technical quality are critical.
Strong executive communication, organizational leadership, negotiation, and decision-making skills.
Ability to communicate complex technical issues clearly to both executive and technical audiences.
Working knowledge of applicable data center codes, standards, and industry guidance, including NFPA, ASHRAE, IBC, and other applicable international, national, and local requirements.

Preferred Qualifications:

15+ years of experience in mission-critical or large-scale infrastructure design and development.
Experience leading design organizations supporting hyperscale cloud or AI infrastructure.
Experience managing global or multi-region data center portfolios.
Experience developing and implementing enterprise-level data center design standards, specifications, and governance programs.
Experience with high-density compute environments, direct-to-chip liquid cooling, advanced thermal management, and next-generation data center infrastructure.
Experience with colocation and developer-led delivery models, including oversight of third-party design and construction partners.
Experience implementing formal design review, technical deviation, change management, and lessons-learned processes.
Working knowledge of BIM, digital design coordination, document management, and design collaboration platforms.
LEED AP, Uptime ATD, or other relevant mission-critical industry certifications.
Demonstrated experience developing high-performing technical teams and future organizational leaders.

jobs.title: Director, Global Strategy - Enterprise Planning
jobs.description:
Owning the design, governance, and continuous evolution of the enterprise planning system, ensuring strategic planning, annual operating planning, resource allocation, and performance reporting operate as an integrated enterprise process

 Leading the execution of the enterprise planning cycle, including Strategic Planning Kickoff, Long-Term Strategic Planning, and Quarterly Business Reviews, and partnering with Finance on Annual Operating Plan (AOP) and budget prioritization connected to business strategy

 Establishing and governing the enterprise planning cadence, ensuring cross-functional alignment, decision readiness, and the timely progression of key strategic milestones

 Building and maintaining the decision frameworks, governance structures, and planning standards that support enterprise-wide prioritization, accountability, and effective decision-making

 Partnering closely with Finance and business leaders to translate strategic priorities into actionable plans, resource allocation decisions, and measurable outcomes

 Leading the planning and coordination of Executive Committee and Board reviews, ensuring strategic issues are clearly framed, decisions are supported by relevant insights, and resulting actions are effectively tracked

 Managing the enterprise portfolio of strategic initiatives, tracking progress, interdependencies, risks, and outcomes while escalating issues requiring executive attention

 Developing scenarios, business cases, and trade-off analyses that enable leaders to evaluate opportunities, risks, investments, and resource allocation decisions

 Providing fact-based analysis, insights, and recommendations to support executive decision-making, prioritization, and enterprise performance discussions

 Establishing enterprise performance management frameworks, scorecards, KPIs, and reporting mechanisms that drive accountability, transparency, and execution against strategic objectives

 Driving alignment across executive leadership, functions, regions, Finance, and Amer Sports to establish a consistent enterprise planning and performance management operating model

 Maintaining visibility to key strategic and execution risks, ensuring mitigation plans are developed, monitored, and integrated into enterprise planning processes

 Developing executive-level communications, planning documents, and leadership briefings that translate complex business information into clear priorities, recommendations, and actions

 Serving as the steward of enterprise planning effectiveness, continuously evaluating planning processes, governance, and reporting mechanisms to improve decision quality, organizational alignment, and business outcomes

 Developing and maintaining the tools, templates, governance processes, and planning methodologies that strengthen enterprise planning capability and support execution against strategic and business plans
Evolving the enterprise planning system as the business scales—adding new planning horizons, integrating regional complexity, and improving the speed and quality of decisions

 Building repeatable frameworks and playbooks for planning processes that reduce dependency on heroic individual effort and increase organizational capability

 Partnering with Finance and regional teams to develop integrated financial and strategic planning models that connect long-range ambition to annual resource reality

 Developing the next generation of performance management tools—moving from tracking to accountability, and from reporting to action

 Supporting the Strategy team’s broader operating model evolution as new capability areas come online
You have a bachelor’s degree in business, strategy, or related field

 You have 10+ years of professional work experience in strategic planning, management consulting, project management, consumer products and/or retail

 You have a demonstrated track record as an outstanding problem solver and strategic You think in systems – you can see how the strategic planning connects to the budget planning, how the QBR connects to accountability, and how the strategic calendar creates or destroys leadership bandwidth

 You are a credible executive partner with the communication skills to work directly with a CDR and functional leaders, and to translate complexity into decisions

 You have significant experience partnering with Finance on resource allocation, budget prioritization, and performance tracking

 You bring sharp analytical capability and strong written communication, and you can build a rigorous framework and write a clear executive brief

 You have experience working across regional and global operating models, ideally with exposure to retail or consumer-facing businesses

 You are organized without being rigid, and you know when the plan needs to change and how to move the system accordingly

 You demonstrate high emotional intelligence, sound judgment, and the ability to influence without authority across senior stakeholders

 You hold yourself and others to a high standard for quality of thinking, clarity of communication, and follow-through
The salary range for this role is CAD$149,000 - CAD$195,000

 TD is committed to providing fair and equitable compensation opportunities to all colleagues. Growth opportunities and skill development are defining features of the colleague experience at TD. Our compensation policies and practices have been designed to allow colleagues to progress through the salary range over time as they progress in their role. The base pay actually offered may vary based upon the candidate's skills and experience, job-related knowledge, geographic location, and other specific business and organizational needs.

 As a candidate, you are encouraged to ask compensation related questions and have an open dialogue with your recruiter who can provide you more specific details for this role.

 Job Description: 
 We are looking for a strategic and collaborative executive to shape and deliver the enterprise Risk Data Strategy. As Vice President, Risk Data Strategy and Transformation, you will lead the roadmap, governance, quality, architecture, and lifecycle management of Risk data products and platforms, building capabilities that strengthen risk management, regulatory compliance, analytics, reporting, and decision-making.

 Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Risk Transformation and Enablement, you will work across Risk Management and with enterprise partners to modernize data capabilities, strengthen governance, and enable scalable, transparent, and resilient solutions. This is an opportunity to influence enterprise priorities and advance data-informed decision-making in a highly regulated environment.

 Key Accountabilities 
 Set the enterprise Risk Data Strategy, target-state capabilities, investment priorities, and multi-year roadmap.
 Lead the governance and lifecycle management of Risk data products and platforms, including ownership, quality, lineage, standards, and controls.
 Shape the evolution of Risk data architecture and integration strategies to support scalable, transparent, and resilient capabilities.
 Translate Risk priorities into practical roadmaps, including the technology, data, governance, and implementation considerations required for delivery.
 Lead portfolio planning and prioritization for Risk data initiatives, balancing strategic value, capacity, dependencies, regulatory expectations, and risk.
 Oversee the funding, delivery, benefits tracking, and value realization of Risk data products and initiatives.
 Establish governance and reporting that give senior leaders clear visibility into progress, outcomes, risks, issues, and decisions.
 Advance data modernization by applying emerging technologies, industry trends, and leading practices where they add value.
 Anticipate and manage delivery risks, resolve obstacles, and bring forward timely recommendations and trade-offs.
 Build strong partnerships across Risk, Technology, Enterprise Data and Analytics, Finance, Regulatory Reporting, and other shared-service teams.
 Lead with empathy and transparency, creating an environment where colleagues feel heard, supported, and confident navigating change.
 Develop an inclusive, high-performing environment where different perspectives are valued and teams are empowered to deliver.

 Key Partnerships 
 Risk Management leaders and teams across all Risk pillars.
 Enterprise partners across Risk Technology, Enterprise Data and Analytics, Enterprise Architecture, Finance, Regulatory Reporting, Governance and Control, and shared services.
 Senior executives, governance forums, and program sponsors responsible for strategic prioritization and decision-making.
 Product, platform, architecture, and delivery teams responsible for building and sustaining Risk data capabilities.

 What You Bring 
 Significant leadership experience in one or more of the following areas: data strategy, data management, data products, technology, analytics, transformation, or risk management.
 Experience leading complex, enterprise-scale data initiatives and operating model change in a matrixed organization.
 A track record of translating strategy into clear priorities, practical roadmaps, and measurable outcomes.
 Strong judgment and the ability to influence, challenge constructively, and build alignment with senior leaders and cross-functional partners.
 Experience with data governance, data quality, architecture, data products, platform operating models, portfolio planning, or benefits tracking.
 Experience with data technology and product management across major platforms and tools. Familiarity with Rahona, Technology Asset Platform, Databricks, Power BI, or comparable technologies is an asset.
 Ability to navigate ambiguity, competing priorities, and regulatory or operational pressure while maintaining momentum.
 Inclusive leadership skills and a commitment to creating an environment where people with different backgrounds and perspectives can contribute and succeed.
 Demonstrated emotional intelligence and executive presence, with the ability to listen with curiosity, build trust, navigate sensitive conversations, and bring diverse stakeholders together through complex change.
 A post-secondary degree or an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience. Advanced education or professional credentials may be an asset but are not required.

 We recognize that strong candidates may bring different combinations of education, career paths, and lived experience. We encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every qualification listed.

 Who We Are: 
 TD is one of the world's leading global financial institutions and is the fifth largest bank in North America by branches/stores. Every day, we strive to make every interaction, product, and experience remarkably human and refreshingly simple for over 27 million households and businesses in Canada, the United States and around the world. More than 95,000 TD colleagues bring their skills, talent, and creativity to foster deeper relationships, ensure disciplined execution, and build a simpler, faster banking experience. TD is deeply committed to being a leader in client experience, that is why we believe that all colleagues, no matter where they work, are client facing. Together, we are reimagining what banking can be for our clients, colleagues and communities. 

 Our Total Rewards Package 
Our Total Rewards package reflects the investments we make in our colleagues to help them and their families achieve their financial, physical, and mental well-being goals. Total Rewards at TD includes a base salary, variable compensation, and several other key plans such as health and well-being benefits, savings and retirement programs, paid time off, banking benefits and discounts, career development, and reward and recognition programs. Learn more 

 Additional Information: 
We’re delighted that you’re considering building a career with TD. Through regular development conversations, training programs, and a competitive benefits plan, we’re committed to providing the support our colleagues need to thrive both at work and at home.

 Please be advised that this job opportunity is subject to provincial regulation for employment purposes. It is imperative to acknowledge that each province or territory within the jurisdiction of Canada may have its own set of regulations, requirements.

 Colleague Development 
 If you’re interested in a specific career path or are looking to build certain skills, we want to help you succeed. You’ll have regular career, development, and performance conversations with your manager, as well as access to an online learning platform and a variety of mentoring programs to help you unlock future opportunities.

 If you’re passionate about helping clients and building deep, lasting relationships, TD offers diverse career paths where you can grow your expertise and make a meaningful impact.  

 We're committed to your success and foster a respectful workplace where diverse perspectives are valued, everyone has fair opportunities to grow, and you can unlock your full potential to achieve your career goals. Here at TD, we hire and develop the best.

 Training & Onboarding 
We will provide training and onboarding sessions to ensure that you’ve got everything you need to succeed in your new role.

 Interview Process  
We’ll reach out to candidates of interest to schedule an interview. We do our best to communicate outcomes to all applicants by email or phone call.

 Accommodation 
Your accessibility is important to us. Please let us know if you’d like accommodations (including accessible meeting rooms, captioning for virtual interviews, etc.) to help us remove barriers so that you can participate throughout the interview process.

We look forward to hearing from you!

jobs.title: Senior Java Engineer – Backend & AI-Assistant Vice President
jobs.description:
Citi is looking for a Senior Java Engineer to design and deliver high-performance backend systems at the intersection of enterprise software development and applied AI tooling. Based within Citi's Technology organization, this role offers the opportunity to build production-grade Java applications using Spring Boot and MongoDB while actively integrating modern AI-assisted development practices into everyday engineering workflows. You will operate with meaningful autonomy, owning application modules end-to-end and contributing to the standards that shape how the team builds and ships software.

Responsibilities

Design, develop, and deploy robust backend applications using Java and Spring Boot, with MongoDB as the primary data store, ensuring performance, reliability, and maintainability at scale.
Build and maintain RESTful APIs and microservices that meet defined business requirements, translating complex functional needs into clean, efficient backend solutions.
Own and deliver discrete application modules from requirements through to production, maintaining accountability across the full software development lifecycle including analysis, design, construction, testing, and release.
Identify and surface technical and delivery risks early, proposing concrete mitigation plans to keep projects on track.
Integrate and champion AI-assisted development tools — including GitHub Copilot, Devin, Claude, and Codex — to accelerate delivery and improve code quality across the team.
Define and uphold engineering standards and operational processes, contributing to a consistent and high-quality development practice.
Apply sound technical judgement when assessing the impact of decisions on system integrity, data quality, and business outcomes, escalating issues transparently where needed.

Required Qualifications & Skills

5+ years of backend software engineering experience, with a focus on Java application development in commercial or enterprise environments.
Deep expertise across the Spring Framework ecosystem, including Spring Boot, Spring MVC, Spring Data JPA, and Spring Security.
Demonstrated ability to design and implement RESTful APIs and microservices architectures that are scalable, secure, and well-documented.
Hands-on experience with CI/CD pipelines and tooling, including Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, Docker, Kubernetes, and Maven or Gradle.
Solid command of Git version control and established branching strategies such as Gitflow, applied in a team delivery context.
Practical experience working with AI-assisted development tools such as GitHub Copilot, Devin, Claude, Codex, or equivalent, as part of a professional engineering workflow.
Familiarity with web service standards including REST and SOAP, and data formats including XML and JSON.

Beneficial Skills & Qualifications

Frontend development experience using Angular, enabling collaboration with full stack teams and contribution to end-to-end feature delivery is nice to have.
Experience managing or contributing to software delivery projects, with the ability to coordinate workstreams and meet shifting deadlines effectively.
Exposure to project management or consulting methodologies that support structured delivery in complex engineering environments.
A bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field — or equivalent practical experience.

What We Offer

At Citi, you will work on technology that operates at genuine global scale, within a team that values engineering craft, clear ownership, and continuous improvement. This is a role where your backend expertise will have direct impact — not just on internal systems, but on how Citi delivers for its clients worldwide.

A hybrid working arrangement with 3 days in the office and 2 days working remotely, giving you flexibility alongside meaningful in-person collaboration.
The opportunity to work at the forefront of AI-augmented software engineering, using tools like GitHub Copilot, Devin, and Claude as a standard part of how the team builds.
Clear scope for technical growth, with exposure to complex, high-stakes backend systems and the autonomy to shape how they evolve.
Access to learning and development resources that support progression across both technical depth and broader engineering leadership.
A performance-driven environment where your contributions are visible, your ownership is real, and the problems you solve carry meaningful consequences.
Competitive compensation and a benefits package designed to support your financial wellbeing, health, and long-term career at one of the world's leading financial institutions.

Apply now to bring your backend Java expertise to Citi and help shape the next generation of high-performance, AI-augmented financial technology

jobs.description:
**Position Title:** Senior Director – Enterprise Performance, Evaluation and Strategic Initiatives

**Employment Status:** Permanent Full Time


**Position Status:** This is a Non\-Bargaining Unit position


This posting is for a new vacancy.

**Hours of Work:** Monday to Friday, 35 Hours

**Position Reports to:** Chief Executive Officer

**Salary Range: $**125,000 \- $140,000, commensurate on skills and experience, plus participation in HOOPP and Group Benefits.

**Primary work location:** Oshawa (Hybrid work environment); Staff may be requested to work out of other DCHC’s sites in Pickering, Whitby, Ajax, Oshawa South and Oshawa North (Airport Road) as required.

**Direct Reports**: 5


* Manager
* Quality Improvement Coordinator \- 1
* Health Information Specialist \- 1
* Data Analyst \- 2

 **Organization**


Who We Are: Durham Community Health Centre (DCHC) is a charitable registered organization that provides integrated, accessible, and equitable community\-based primary care, wellness services, and health education for Durham community members facing barriers to health and well\-being.

  

Who We Serve: DCHC offers equity\-focused programs and services for priority populations, including Indigenous peoples, Black communities, 2SLGBTQI\+ community members, newcomers to Canada, seniors, and clients without a family doctor. This approach helps community members access both preventive care and care when they are ill.

  

How We Work: Our interprofessional team includes physicians, nurse practitioners, nurses, counsellors, dietitians, outreach workers, medical secretaries, and administrative staff. Together, we place each client at the centre of care and respond to their needs through integrated clinical care, wellness support, and health education.

  

Why Join Now: This is an exciting time to join DCHC as we advance an energizing path toward greater impact in local health care. Guided by our Strategic Plan, Theory of Change, brand, client stories, and resources, we are diversifying, expanding, and strengthening how we serve the community.

 **Position Overview**


Durham Community Health Center (DCHC) is seeking an exceptional, self\-driven leader to take on the role of Senior Director, Enterprise Performance, Evaluation and Strategic Initiatives. The role demands a leader who thrives in complexity, excels in driving enterprise\-wide performance, and is relentless in the pursuit of excellence.

  

At DCHC we are committed to a collaborative culture where strategic thinking, execution discipline and shared leadership are at the core of everything we do. As a key member of the Executive Leadership Team, the Senior Director will be responsible for aligning enterprise performance, strategic initiatives, and quality improvement with DCHC’s long\-term vision.

  

This role is a unique opportunity for an innovative leader to build high\-impact frameworks for evaluation, decision support, special project execution and quality transformation. The right candidate will be a visionary, a doer and a collaborator; someone who can seamlessly transition between strategy and execution while fostering an organizational culture of continuous improvement and strategic excellence.

 **KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**


As a member of the Executive Leadership Team and strategic advisor to the CEO, the Senior Director provides enterprise leadership across strategy execution, performance intelligence, transformation, risk, quality, accreditation, and organizational alignment.

  

1\. **Enterprise Strategy \& Execution**

* Translate DCHC’s strategic plan into clear annual priorities, business operating plans, performance measures, and funder accountabilities.
* Lead enterprise strategy execution and monitor progress against strategic commitments, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and long\-term strategic objectives.
* Ensure alignment between Board priorities, CEO direction, ELT accountabilities, resource management, and organizational initiatives execution.

**2\. Enterprise Performance \& Intelligence**

* Establish DCHC’s enterprise performance management framework.
* Develop integrated, real\-time dashboards, scorecards, quality indicators, and performance reporting tools.
* Lead enterprise analytics, program evaluation, KPIs, outcome measurement, governance reporting, and data\-informed decision\-making.
* Provide the CEO and ELT with timely intelligence focusing on trends to support strategic decisions and performance improvement.

**3\. Strategic Initiatives \& Transformation**

* Lead CEO and ELT\-sponsored strategic initiatives, complex enterprise projects, and transformational initiatives that improve service delivery and operational effectiveness.
* Establish clear governance framework, milestones, accountabilities, and measures for all organizational initiatives aligned to DCHC corporate balance scorecard.

**4\. Enterprise Risk, Quality \& Organizational Excellence**

jobs.description:
IMMEDIATE INTERIM OPPORTUNITY

Interim Senior Vice President, Finance

Reports to: Chief Financial Officer

Location: Waterloo, Ontario

Duration: 6-12 Months

Hybrid

A global organization is seeking a Senior Vice President, Finance to strengthen its administrative and financial leadership capacity and support continued growth. Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, this executive will provide overall direction for finance, accounting, tax planning, credit and treasury activities worldwide.

The Senior Vice President will also provide financial support and analysis for strategic initiatives, including mergers and acquisitions, due diligence and integration, and the implementation of new technology systems and tools.

The Mandate

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Senior Vice President of Finance will:

Global Finance Leadership

Together with the CFO, contribute to the development of strategic goals and objectives by managing and developing high-performing finance teams around the world.
Provide overall direction for finance, accounting, tax, planning, credit, and treasury functions globally.
Lead the Vice President of Financial Planning & Analytics, the Vice President - Group Controller, and other members of the finance leadership team.
Act as a strategic partner to the executive team and Strategic Business Unit Managers, providing insights and decision support on commercial and operational matters.
Participate in global governance committees and contribute collaboratively to enterprise-wide decision-making.

Planning, Reporting and Performance Management

Prepare and implement financial plans aligned with the global strategy, including annual business plans and budgets that support profitable growth.
Lead the long-range plan, three-year strategic plan, annual operating plan and budget, quarterly closing, monthly reporting, and Board meeting preparation.
Prepare and present financial budgets, monthly profit and loss results, forecast-versus-budget analyses, balance sheets, and cash flow statements to the CFO, CEO, and Executive Committee.
Evaluate internal investment decisions to maximize returns and promote the efficient use of capital.
Drive value creation through operational transformation, margin expansion, improved working capital, and disciplined performance management.

Financial Control, Risk and Compliance

Ensure statutory accounts are published within agreed timelines and in accordance with applicable accounting standards.
Maintain high-quality financial reporting and effective internal controls, including compliance with IFRS and applicable financial and tax regulations.
Serve as a key contact for external auditors and manage the preparation and support required for external audits.
Set high standards for internal control, internal audit, and financial risk management, including foreign exchange exposure.
Monitor debt, maintain control of the balance sheet, and work with the CFO to manage banking facilities and relationships.

Transactions, Systems and Transformation

Work with the CFO on acquisitions, joint ventures, and partnerships, ensuring high-quality due diligence, deal execution, and integration.
Provide financial analysis and support for other strategic initiatives, including the implementation of new technology systems and tools.
Supervise the effective operation of financial systems, databases, and financial software.
Enhance and optimize financial and accounting systems, processes, tools, and control frameworks.
Lead efficiency initiatives that improve quality, reduce costs, and keep critical systems current and secure.

Leadership and Team Development

Reinforce the global finance organization and establish clear standards of accountability, collaboration, and performance.
Recruit, interview, and hire finance employees as required.
Develop culturally sensitive, high-performing teams that can operate effectively across a variety of regions and business environments .

Key Internal and External Relationships

The Senior Vice President of Finance will work closely with:
Chief Financial Officer
Chief Executive Officer and Executive Committee
Strategic Business Unit Managers
Finance leadership teams and employees globally
All levels of management and staff
Banks and external auditors
Customers, suppliers, insurance brokers, and other professional advisors

Ideal Candidate Profile

The successful candidate will bring:

15+ years of progressive finance leadership experience, ideally beginning in a large international organization recognized for strong financial processes and business performance.
Experience in a mid-sized organization is considered an asset.
Proven experience leading finance across a global scope.
A strong record of strengthening finance organizations and developing effective leadership teams.
Demonstrated value creation through operational transformation, margin expansion and disciplined execution.
Experience in life sciences, research and development, or manufacturing is an asset.
University or master’s degree with a specialization in Finance; an MBA is considered an asset.
Fluency in English is required; French-language capability is considered an asset.

Leadership Attributes

Credible and natural leadership with a positive, pragmatic, and hands-on approach.
Strong commercial judgment, analytical capability, and the ability to identify trends, issues, and opportunities.
Personal maturity, integrity, accountability, and the ability to operate effectively in a family-owned business.
A collaborative style and the ability to interact effectively with a broad range of stakeholders and cultures.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, cultural sensitivity, and multicultural openness.
A results-driven mindset with the energy and commitment to deliver meaningful improvements.

The Ideal Interim Executive

This assignment is best suited for a seasoned global finance executive who combines strategic insight with practical execution. The successful leader will be comfortable operating across planning, performance management, controllership, treasury, transactions, systems, and transformation while strengthening the global finance team.
The executive will bring credibility with senior leaders, Board-level finance processes, auditors, banks, and business partners, and will establish the disciplined processes, controls, and decision support required to advance profitable growth.

jobs.title: Director of Finance & Operations
jobs.description:
Help Shape the Future of Healthcare in the Comox Valley

Are you a collaborative, solutions-oriented finance professional who is passionate about making a meaningful difference in your community?

The Comox Valley Healthcare Foundation is seeking a Director, Finance & Operations
to join our dedicated team. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to an organization that helps bring exceptional healthcare closer to home by funding priority equipment, programs, education, research, and facility improvements throughout the Comox Valley.

Reporting directly to the Co-Executive Directors, the Director, Finance & Operations plays a key leadership role in ensuring the Foundation's financial integrity, operational effectiveness, governance support, and organizational sustainability. Working collaboratively with a small, high-performing team, this position ensures donor gifts are stewarded responsibly while supporting the Foundation's mission to enhance healthcare for people of all ages throughout our region. As a member of the leadership team, you will help guide the Foundation's financial stewardship and operational excellence during an exciting period of continued community investment in healthcare.

The ideal candidate brings strong financial management expertise, exceptional attention to detail, a proactive mindset, and a commitment to stewardship, accountability, and community impact.

Core Responsibilities

Finance, Accounting & Financial Stewardship

•Lead all accounting, bookkeeping, and financial management activities for the Foundation.
•Maintain and oversee the Foundation's accounting systems, banking relationships, investment records, and cash flow management.
•Monitor financial performance and prepare regular financial reporting, forecasts, analyses, and recommendations for management and the Board of Directors.
•Develop annual operating budgets in collaboration with the Co-Executive Directors and support long-term financial planning.
•Coordinate annual audit preparation and serve as primary liaison with external auditors.
•Ensure compliance with all Canada Revenue Agency charitable reporting requirements, including T3010 filings and charitable receipting standards.
•Complete GST reporting, payroll administration, T4 preparation, benefit administration, and statutory remittances. Maintain rigorous internal controls, financial policies, and risk management practices to safeguard organizational assets.
• Manage financial tracking and reporting of restricted donations, designated funds, grants, endowments, and donor-directed healthcare initiatives.
• Provide financial analysis and reporting related to healthcare equipment purchases, capital projects, community healthcare programs, and special funding initiatives.
• Ensure data integrity and effective integration across financial, donor, payroll, and reporting systems.
• Process, reconcile, and report donations and charitable receipts accurately and in a timely manner.

Governance & Board Support

• Prepare financial reports, dashboards, and supporting materials for Board and committee meetings.
• Attend Board meetings and Finance Committee meetings as requested.
• Provide financial analysis and recommendations to support strategic decision-making.
• Assist with onboarding and orientation of Board members relating to financial governance and compliance responsibilities.
• Maintain governance records and support required organizational filings and corporate records.
• Support implementation and review of governance policies, financial policies, and organizational practices consistent with best practices for charitable organizations.

Operations & Administration

• Oversee operational systems, policies, and procedures that promote efficiency, accountability, and compliance.
• Ensure compliance with employment standards, privacy requirements, charitable regulations, and other applicable legislation.
• Support human resources administration, employee record management, benefits administration, and policy implementation.
• Coordinate external service providers, including auditors, legal counsel, IT consultants, HR specialists, and insurance providers.
• Develop and maintain operational policies and procedures that support organizational effectiveness and continuous improvement.

Strategic Leadership & Organizational Development

• Support implementation of the Foundation's strategic plan and organizational priorities.
• Assist in developing financial strategies that advance sustainable growth and maximize mission impact.
• Provide financial oversight and reporting for major fundraising initiatives, healthcare campaigns, grants, and donor-funded projects.
•Support business planning, policy development, and organizational evaluation initiatives.
•Participate in projects that strengthen organizational capacity, operational excellence, and long-term sustainability.
•Support organizational storytelling by helping quantify and communicate the impact of donor investments in local healthcare.

Qualifications Required

•Undergraduate degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Commerce, or a related field.
•Minimum five years of progressive experience in financial management, accounting, or operations leadership.
•Advanced proficiency with accounting software, payroll systems, and Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.
•Demonstrated experience preparing budgets, financial statements, audits, and regulatory filings.
•Strong organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail and accuracy.
•Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
•Ability to work independently while contributing effectively to a collaborative team environment.
•Valid BC Class 5 Driver's License.
•Ability to successfully complete a Criminal Record Check.
Preferred

•Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation.
•Experience working within the charitable, nonprofit, healthcare, or public sectors.
•Experience supporting Boards of Directors, governance processes, and committee reporting.
•Knowledge of charitable accounting, donor-restricted funds, and CRA charitable compliance requirements.
•Knowledge of Financial Edge and Raiser’s Edge is an asset.

What We Offer

•Meaningful work that directly impacts healthcare services in the Comox Valley.
•A collaborative, supportive and mission-focused workplace culture.
•Opportunity to work alongside dedicated staff, volunteers, healthcare leaders, donors and community partners.
•Flexible and hybrid part-time schedule supporting work-life balance.
•Competitive compensation, including five weeks of paid vacation (prorated to the positions part-time schedule).
•Opportunities for professional development and leadership growth.
•Opportunity to lead strategic initiatives that strengthen healthcare services and enhance the experiences of patients and families throughout our region.

About the Comox Valley Healthcare Foundation

The Comox Valley Healthcare Foundation is a registered charity established in 1993 and governed by a volunteer Board of Directors. Working in partnership with generous donors, healthcare professionals, community organizations, and healthcare leadership, the Foundation raises funds to enhance quality healthcare throughout the Comox Valley.

Through community support, the Foundation helps fund priority medical equipment, healthcare programs, staff education, research initiatives, facility enhancements, and patient comfort resources in hospital, community-based, and long-term care settings. The Foundation's goal is to ensure residents have access to exceptional healthcare close to home.

We are committed to creating a respectful, inclusive, and welcoming workplace where diverse perspectives are valued and everyone is empowered to contribute to our shared mission of improving local healthcare. As a small, collaborative team, we value integrity, accountability, innovation, and continuous learning. We support one another, encourage new ideas, and recognize that every team member plays an important role in advancing our mission.

How to Apply

To apply, please submit your résumé and cover letter outlining your qualifications and interest in the position to info@cvhealthcarefoundation.com by October 21, 2026. Applications will be reviewed as they are received and accepted until the position is filled. We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. Join us in helping bring exceptional healthcare closer to home.

jobs.description:
VP of Capital Markets & Structured Finance | 1Legion | Remote (Europe or North America) with travel | Reports to the CFO, working directly with the CEO on every raise
The role
You will build and run the financing engine behind 1Legion's growth. Every GPU cluster we deploy is backed by a long-term customer contract and funded through a mix of equipment finance, structured debt and capital partnerships. You will structure and close those facilities, run the lender and investor processes, and design the financing structures that let us say yes to the next contract.
What you will do
Structure and close GPU-backed debt: equipment leases, delayed-draw term loans, asset-backed facilities and vendor financing
Structure SPVs and capital partnerships with investors who fund hardware against contracted revenue
Own the lender model: covenants, residual value, cash flows per deployment, and the scenarios lenders ask for
Run diligence processes end to end from the issuer side: data rooms, term sheet negotiation, documentation with counsel, closing
Build and maintain relationships with lenders, infrastructure funds and capital partners in North America and Europe
Support the equity raise and public-market readiness work alongside the CFO and CEO
Match financing structures to take-or-pay contract terms so that delivery, billing and debt service line up

What we are looking for
8+ years in structured finance, project finance, infrastructure debt, leveraged finance or corporate development at an infrastructure company
You have closed asset-backed or project financings, ideally in data centres, GPU compute, telecom or energy infrastructure
Strong modelling: you have built lender-grade models that were used to close transactions
You have run a financing process from the issuer side, not only advised on one
You understand how lenders underwrite contracted revenue and residual value on hardware
You work comfortably across US, Canadian and European capital markets

Nice to have
Experience in the finance team of a GPU cloud or neocloud
Public listing or public-company finance experience
Vendor financing with NVIDIA or major OEMs
