jobs.description:
Company Description
PORTA – Tradizione Italiana is one of North America’s fastest-growing frozen pizza brands, bringing authentic Italian craftsmanship to over 3,000 retail locations across the U.S. and Canada. Developed by the culinary team behind Terroni, PORTA combines chef-curated recipes with premium ingredients sourced from Italy to elevate frozen food standards. The brand uses traditional techniques, such as slow-fermented dough and flash-freezing at peak freshness, to deliver restaurant-quality pizza at home in under 15 minutes. While pizza is the foundation, PORTA’s broader mission is to make authentic Italian cuisine effortless at home and bring the best of Italy to more tables. Applicants will join a growing company with strong presence in natural retailers and a focus on quality, innovation, and customer experience.

Role Description
The Director / VP of Finance is a full-time, remote role with its head office in Toronto, Canada. This position oversees all finance and accounting operations, including budgeting, forecasting, cash flow management, and monthly, quarterly, and annual closing activities. The role is responsible for preparing, reviewing, and analyzing financial statements and reports, ensuring accuracy, compliance, and timely delivery to leadership and stakeholders. The Director / VP of Finance will support strategic decision-making by providing financial insights, modeling business scenarios, and evaluating investments, pricing, and product profitability. Day-to-day tasks include managing financial controls, coordinating with external auditors, optimizing systems and processes, partnering with cross-functional teams (such as operations, sales, and supply chain), and building a scalable finance function to support PORTA’s rapid growth.

Qualifications
Strong Finance foundation, including experience leading financial operations and partnering with executive leadership.
Expertise in Financial Planning, including budgeting, forecasting, and long-range financial modeling.
Ability to prepare, interpret, and present Financial Statements, with a deep understanding of accounting principles.
Proficiency in Financial Reporting, including management reporting, KPI dashboards, and board-level presentations.
Advanced Analytical Skills to evaluate performance, assess risk, support strategic decisions, and drive process improvements.
Experience in CPG, food and beverage, or retail environments is strongly preferred.
Proven leadership experience managing teams and building finance capabilities in a growth-oriented company.
Professional designation (CPA, CFA, or equivalent) and a university degree

About You

University or college degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field; MBA or CPA an asset
8+ years of progressive finance experience, ideally in CPG, food & beverage, or consumer products. Startup experience is an asset.
Deep FP&A expertise with a proven ability to turn data into strategic recommendations
Strong command of retail and grocery economics, including trade spend, slotting, deductions, retailer margin, and velocity metrics
Commercially minded, with a track record of partnering cross-functionally and influencing senior decision-makers
Experience supporting investors, board reporting, or fundraising, ideally in an early or growth-stage company
Hands-on and resourceful, comfortable operating with a lean team and directing analysts and outsourced support
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to make finance accessible to non-finance stakeholders
Deadline-driven and highly organized, with strong attention to detail
Ability to operate in a fast-paced environment with changing priorities

The Perks

Competitive compensation package
Benefits
Remote work
Free pizza!

Location

This role is hybrid for candidates based in Toronto and fully remote for candidates elsewhere in Canada.

To Apply

Interested in joining the PORTA team? Email careers@eatporta.com

PORTA is committed to providing a diverse, equitable and inclusive workplace. Our people are our business and we celebrate our differences, encourage a breadth of perspectives, and offer equal opportunity for all employees to join and excel at our company. PORTA gladly provides accommodations to candidates if necessary, so please send us an email if you would like us to do that for you: careers@eatporta.com!

Our momentum is growing, and is fueled by innovation, collaboration, and a shared entrepreneurial spirit that drives real results. Founded in 2012 in Mississauga, Ontario, OSL delivers customized sales solutions in retail, direct sales, and customer acquisition, all built on a foundation of integrity, respect, and passion. Our culture thrives on connection, purpose, and growth. If you’re looking for a place where your talents are valued, your ideas matter, and your career can grow, we’d love to meet you.

About the opportunity:

Director, Information Technology and Digital Transformation

OSL Retail Services is a technology-enabled sales and retail services organization supporting some of North America’s leading brands. As Director, Information Technology and Digital Transformation, you will lead the delivery and evolution of enterprise technology services that support corporate operations, field teams, client programs, analytics, and business transformation initiatives.

Reporting to the SVP, Data and Technology, you will lead a team of managers and technical leads, alongside external partners and managed service providers. You will be responsible for ensuring OSL’s technology ecosystem, including cloud platforms, cybersecurity, enterprise applications, service management, AI governance, and digital workplace services, remains secure, scalable, resilient, and aligned to business objectives.

This role is the critical bridge between the SVP’s strategic direction and day to day technology delivery, translating strategy into measurable outcomes, while maintaining a strong focus on governance, operational excellence and value realization.

Location: Mississauga

Role Responsibilities:

Technology Strategy & Direction

Contribute to and execute the multi-year technology strategy in partnership with the SVP, Data and Technology, translating strategic direction into delivery roadmaps, programs, and measurable outcomes.
Identify opportunities where technology, automation, analytics, and AI can improve productivity, compliance, and competitive differentiation, and bring forward business cases for prioritization.
Provide leadership and oversight for technology governance, architecture standards, and enterprise technology decision-making within the role's mandate.
Ensure technology investments are prioritized based on business value, risk reduction, operational efficiency, and strategic alignment.

Enterprise Architecture & Technology Governance

Establish and maintain technology standards, reference architectures, and governance processes across the enterprise.
Ensure technology solutions are scalable, supportable, secure, and aligned with long-term business requirements.
Oversee Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) governance, source code management, release management, and deployment controls.
Drive technology rationalization and reduction of technical debt through platform consolidation and modernization initiatives.
Maintain oversight of enterprise SaaS platforms and ensure effective integration across business systems.

IT Operations & Service Delivery

Oversee enterprise IT service delivery across applications, infrastructure, networks, and SaaS platforms.
Ensure systems are stable, secure, and performant to support retail, field, and corporate environments.
Establish and maintain governance for incident management, change management, and release processes.
Drive continuous improvement in service reliability, responsiveness, and user experience
Ensure technology services support a geographically distributed workforce across retail, field, and corporate environments while maintaining consistent service levels and user experience.

Digital Transformation, Automation & AI Enablement

Lead enterprise modernization initiatives including cloud adoption, platform consolidation, workflow automation, and digital workplace transformation.
Operationalize and mature OSL's established enterprise AI governance program, aligned to ISO 42001 and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, covering employee AI use, AI capabilities within SaaS platforms, and internally developed solutions.
Partner with business leaders to identify automation opportunities that improve productivity, reduce manual effort, and enhance data quality.
Deliver scalable, integrated solutions that support analytics, reporting, and operational decision-making, in partnership with the Business Intelligence and Data Services teams.
Balance innovation with operational resilience, cybersecurity requirements, compliance obligations, and cost management.

Financial Stewardship & Vendor Management

Manage the operational technology budget and contribute to the annual technology planning and investment prioritization led by the Executive Leadership Team.
Establish business cases and ROI measures for major technology investments and transformation programs.
Identify opportunities to optimize cost‑to‑serve through consolidation, automation, and strategic sourcing.
Manage vendor relationships, contract renewals, and licensing across the technology portfolio.

Cross Functional Partnership & Enablement

Build strong partnerships with Operations, Client Services, Finance, HR, Sales, and Analytics teams.
Act as a trusted technology advisor to business leaders, translating needs into scalable, secure solutions.
Represent IT in cross‑functional planning forums, transformation initiatives, and program reviews.
Ensuring technology decisions reflect both business value and operational reality.

Leadership & Team Development

Lead, coach and develop a technology team, alongside external partners responsible for the delivery of enterprise technology services.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and customer service excellence.
Establish succession planning, skills development, and workforce planning strategies that support future organizational growth.
Ensure team objectives, performance measures, and priorities are aligned to corporate goals.

What You Bring to the Table

10+ years of progressive Information Technology experience, including leadership responsibility for enterprise infrastructure, cybersecurity, applications, or digital transformation initiatives.
5+ years in a senior leadership role managing cross-functional technology teams, including experience leading through managers or team leads.
Experience leading enterprise cloud transformation initiatives utilizing Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365 platforms.
Experience operating within a regulated or compliance-driven environment, including responding to clients or external security and audit requirements.
Experience supporting ISO 27001 or comparable security and governance frameworks.
Experience managing enterprise service management platforms and ITIL-based processes.
Experience evaluating and governing emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence and automation platforms.
Experience managing technology budgets and contributing to enterprise-level financial planning.
Experience supporting geographically distributed workforces across retail, field, and corporate environments.
Bachelor’s degree in information technology, Computer Science, or related field or equivalent experience.

Preferred Certifications

ITIL Foundation or higher
CISSP, CISM, CRISC, or equivalent security certification
Microsoft Azure certification
ISO 27001 Lead Implementer or Lead Auditor (asset)
Project Management certification (PMP or equivalent) (asset)

Let's Talk Perks

The salary range for this role is $150K to $170K, your final compensation will reflect your years of experience and beyond the numbers, we’re proud to offer a holistic package that includes:

Generous time off: Start with 3 weeks of vacation.
Comprehensive benefits package: Includes medical, dental, vision and a health spending account.
Retirement support: Company-sponsored RRSP matching program to help build your financial future.
Award-winning culture: Proud to be one of Canada’s Best Managed Companies for 8 years running — now a Platinum Club member.
Invested in you: Structured employee development programs designed to help you thrive.

We’re committed to supporting your success every step of the way. What are the next steps?

Interview Steps:

Step 2: The next step is an in-person interview with the SVP, Data and Technology.
Step 3: Final step is an in-person interview with the Chief Operating Officer.

If this sounds like you and you’re excited to be a member of our team, please apply now.

jobs.title: National Director, Information Technology
jobs.description:
We’re excited to share that JDRF Canada is now Breakthrough T1D.

We’re the same organization, with the same mission and determination to realize a world free from type 1 diabetes (T1D) – just with a new name and look that reflects what the T1D community needs now and next.

It’s an exciting time to join Breakthrough T1D as we continue to break barriers to help people better manage the disease and enjoy full, healthy lives. Curing T1D is and always will be our north star and we will not stop until breakthroughs get us to a world free from T1D.
Breakthrough T1D is searching for an experienced leader in Information Technology for the role of National Director, Information Technology.

If you’re a strategic, innovative and collaborative leader who would like to lead the next chapter of the organization’s digital evolution by developing and delivering a multi-year information technology strategy, roadmap and portfolio aligned with Breakthrough T1D’s strategic priorities, please read on to see if this is the right fit for you.

Here’s what your primary responsibilities would be:

Works with the Senior Leadership Team to develop and execute a multi-year IT and digital strategy, roadmap and investment portfolio aligned with organizational priorities and supported by business cases, resource plans, budgets, performance measures and clear accountabilities.
Leads Breakthrough T1D’s responsible AI strategy and portfolio, including governance, approved-use standards, privacy and security controls, vendor due diligence, human oversight, staff education, prioritized use cases and benefits measurement.
Provides planning, resourcing, oversight and accountability for the IT portfolio, including enterprise applications, infrastructure, digital platforms, data and analytics, cybersecurity, service delivery and technology-enabled innovation.
Partners with business leaders to assess needs, select solutions and oversee the design, implementation and integration of technologies that support mission delivery, research collaboration, fundraising, advocacy and organizational operations.
Develops, implements and maintains Breakthrough T1D’s cybersecurity framework, policies and controls, aligned with organizational risk, privacy and data sovereignty requirements and applicable standards.
Leads the enterprise data and analytics strategy, including data ownership, quality, classification, integration, retention, privacy, governance, reporting and the development of trusted organizational and constituent insights.
Builds, motivates and retains a highly engaged, customer-centred information technology team aligned with Breakthrough T1D’s values, vision and strategic priorities.

Here’s what we’re looking for:

Knowledge/Skills/Experience
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information systems, business technology or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
A minimum of seven (7) years of progressive leadership experience across information technology, digital transformation, project and portfolio management, enterprise applications, infrastructure, cybersecurity, data and service delivery, including experience leading complex enterprise-wide initiatives and multidisciplinary teams.
Demonstrated experience managing IT environments with cybersecurity, privacy, and data sovereignty requirements comparable to those of federally Canadian organizations.
Demonstrated experience leading enterprise digital transformation involving cloud platforms, enterprise architecture, systems integration, digital products, vendor ecosystems and organizational change.

Working Style
Applies sound judgment, initiative and a strong sense of organization and urgency in a changing environment.
Communicates complex information clearly and credibly to technical and non-technical stakeholders, senior executives and governance bodies.
Demonstrates strong business analysis, project and financial management capabilities and a record of leading successful cross-functional initiatives.
Builds trusted relationships through a collaborative, customer-centred and business-focused approach.

Other position requirements to note:
Demonstrated experience overseeing high-volume transactional websites, CRM platforms, digital fundraising or engagement solutions, and internal collaboration and information-sharing platforms; experience with not-for-profit enterprise systems is an asset.
Strong knowledge of cybersecurity, privacy, data sovereignty, records and information management, accessibility, responsible AI, cyber resilience and third-party technology risk in a Canadian context.
Project, program, technology governance, security or service management certification is an asset.
Translates organizational strategy and stakeholder needs into practical technology priorities, investment decisions and outcomes.

The salary range for this role is anticipated to be $125,000 - $160,000, commensurate with skills and experience level of the selected candidate.

Location Preference:
Anywhere within Canada

Application Deadline:
Please submit your resume through our careers website by October 12, 2026.

About Breakthrough T1D

Breakthrough T1D is the leading type 1 diabetes (T1D) research and advocacy non-profit organization in Canada. As we drive toward curing type 1 diabetes, we help to make every day better for the people who live with it.

Breakthrough T1D (formerly JDRF) began in Canada as a grassroots organization in 1974, when a group of dedicated parents came together with a singular goal of finding a cure for T1D. Since the discovery of insulin, Breakthrough T1D has remained at the forefront of T1D research. Breakthrough T1D is committed to investing in the most promising research, advocating for progress by working with governments to address issues that impact the T1D community, and supporting individuals living with this disease.

Breakthrough T1D has a company culture rooted in our Core Values; Adapt and Thrive, Collaborate, Accountable, Innovate, Act with Purpose – if our core values are exemplified in the way that you work, we might be a great fit for each other.

Here’s a few details about what Breakthrough T1D employees receive:

Our employees love the convenience and flexibility of working remotely, so all positions are work from home (within Canada).
Health and Wellness Benefits:
Benefits to support your physical and mental health – this includes Manulife group benefits, Maple virtual health care, Not Myself Today to support mentally healthy workplaces and generous paid sick time.

We want employees to grow within their roles and have a career at Breakthrough T1D, so we practice Career Development Planning and have a budget for paid development opportunities for each employee.
Other benefits include:
Group RRSP Matching Program, winter holiday office closures, flex weeks in the summer and more!

Benefits listed above for regular full-time employees. Not all benefits may be available to part-time or temporary employees.

Breakthrough T1D strives to foster a workplace that reflects the diversity of the community it serves and welcomes applications from all qualified candidates. Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Brex’s AI-native automation and world-class service eliminate manual expense and accounting tasks for customers so they can focus on what matters most. Tens of thousands of the world's best companies run on Brex, including DoorDash, Coinbase, Robinhood, Zoom, Plaid, Reddit, and SeatGeek.

Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We’re committed to building a diverse team and inclusive culture and believe your potential should only be limited by how big you can dream. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career.

Product at Brex

The Product team is at the forefront of Brex's mission to empower employees anywhere to make better financial decisions. With a deep understanding of the business, we identify and scope out the most impactful opportunities for Brex to tackle. We are responsible for aligning cross-functional teams — such as Engineering, Legal, Compliance, and Design — on key decisions. We set strategy and drive products from inception to launch, enabling Brex to grow rapidly and help our customers reach their full potential.

What You’ll Do

As a Product Leader at Brex, you will be the driving force behind our Growth Product team — overseeing the thoughtful strategy and execution of team and technical systems to drive customer acquisition and onboarding. You will also collaborate closely with our Go-to-Market (GTM) teams to ensure seamless acquisition and onboarding for customers, particularly those with significant and complex spending needs. You will be instrumental in creating features, models, and tools that empower our GTM and Marketing teams to get maximal leverage out of their efforts. You will work closely with cross-functional teams across the organization, based in San Francisco, New York, Seattle, Vancouver, Brazil, and remote locations. Past examples of work in this domain include AI agents for GTM workflows, developing best-in-class GTM data and enrichment systems, ML models for account prioritization, prospect AI classification systems, and more.

Where you’ll work

This role will be based in either our San Francisco, Seattle, or New York City office. You must be willing to work in the office at least three days per week on Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. Employees will be able to work remotely for up to four weeks per year, for a minimum of one week at a time.

Responsibilities

Drive product and systems investments that improve GTM metrics such as CAC payback, pipeline conversion, and efficiency.
Define and execute a multi-quarter Growth strategy in partnership with Engineering, Design, GTM, Marketing, Ops, and Data to deliver high-impact, scalable products with measurable business impact.
Embed within Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success to identify workflow bottlenecks and lead automation and optimization initiatives.
Analyze GTM funnel and conversion metrics to uncover insights and guide product priorities and roadmap decisions.
Set clear goals, metrics, and success criteria for the Growth team, driving accountability to measurable outcomes.
Manage and develop a team of Product Managers, fostering clarity, ownership, and a culture of high performance.
Oversee core Growth Product and Engineering domains, including account scoring, TAM data, outbound automation, and GTM tooling.
Align stakeholders around an aspirational 6–12 month roadmap that advances GTM efficiency and business growth.
Ensure successful activation and implementation of customers initiatives by partnering with GTM and Customer Success to operationalize tooling and automations.
Continuously refine activation based on feedback and performance data to drive faster time-to-value and sustainable adoption.

Requirements

Relevant experience: 10+ years of experience in product management or management consulting, ideally with direct responsibility for or experience scaling B2B products and GTM systems, with a strong understanding of growth, GTM, and/or marketing pipelines.
Analytical sense: You demonstrate a strong aptitude for and actively use data to inform your decision-making. Basic SQL proficiency is strongly preferred.
Communication: You have proven experience working and communicating effectively with senior leaders and executives, and influencing stakeholders across departments and functions, including Engineering, Design, Marketing, Sales, CRMX/Business Systems, IT, Legal, and more. You excel at building trust and working relationships.
Systems-thinker: You are a systems thinker, capable of thinking holistically across product, technical, and people systems to identify bottlenecks and opportunities for efficiency, automation, fraud prevention, and product growth within the payables ecosystem.

Compensation

The expected salary range for this role is $340,000 - $425,000. However, the starting base pay will depend on a number of factors including the candidate’s location, skills, experience, market demands, and internal pay parity. Depending on the position offered, equity and other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package.

Please be aware, job-seekers may be at risk of targeting by malicious actors looking for personal data. Brex recruiters will only reach out via LinkedIn or email with a brex.com domain. Any outreach claiming to be from Brex via other sources should be ignored.

jobs.title: Director, Finance
jobs.description:
About RouteThis

RouteThis is on a mission to revolutionize technical support. We build AI-powered solutions that help Internet Service Providers and Smart Home companies solve connectivity and WiFi problems before the subscriber ever needs to call.

The Role

RouteThis is 10 years in and moving from a SaaS business to an AI-native one. That shift changes the shape of the P&L, the way revenue is recognized and the questions leadership needs Finance to answer. The Director, Finance leads the function through it.

This is an FP&A-led role. The priority is planning, forecasting and cash, with Finance acting as a partner in business decisions rather than a function that reports on them afterwards. The core planning model and reporting structure are being put in place now. The Director will come in as that work lands, understand how and why it was built, and own it from there. There is still plenty to shape, including finance rhythms, spending approvals and forecasting cadence.

This role reports to the Chief Operating Officer, who leads Finance for the company and presents to the board. The Director prepares the finance materials that go to the board and leads the Financial Controller day to day. It is a hands-on role in a lean, AI-enabled team.

What You'll Do

FP&A.
Build and maintain the live weekly forecast across ARR by product line, expense and cash, and lead the annual budgeting process.
Business partnership.
Act as a thought partner to the COO and CEO, bringing forward-looking analysis into strategy and business planning before decisions are made.
Reporting and close.
Own the monthly and quarterly close, including the SaaS versus AI revenue and P&L split, and prepare board and investor materials in partnership with the COO.
Cash and treasury.
Manage runway, covenants, AR and AP, collections and foreign exchange exposure.
Team and rhythms.
Lead the Financial Controller and design the internal finance rhythms the company runs on: collections, spending approvals and forecasting cadence.
Governance.
Support audit readiness, insurance review and internal controls as the company scales.
Cross-functional partnership.
Partner with Sales, Customer Success and Professional Services on unit economics and pricing model support.
AI and tooling.
Use AI and modern finance tools to keep a small team efficient, and keep improving how the function works.

What You Bring

CPA, CA or CMA designation.
Seven or more years of progressive finance experience, with meaningful time in FP&A rather than primarily a controllership or close-focused track.
Experience in a SaaS or subscription business. Exposure to more than one revenue model, or to usage-based revenue recognition, is a strong asset.
Experience preparing board and investor materials and cash forecasts in close partnership with a CEO, COO or CFO.
Fluency building live, rolling financial models.
Comfort operating without a CFO in place and taking ownership of a newly built model and process.
A hands-on, practical approach. You are as comfortable in the detail as you are in a leadership conversation.
Comfort with AI tools and an interest in using them more.
A clear, confident communicator with the CEO, COO and board.

Why RouteThis

Ownership.
Direct visibility to the CEO, COO and board, with real ownership of the finance function.
Timing.
A 10-year-old business with a product that works, moving from SaaS to AI-native. You will see the numbers change and help lead the company through it.
Team.
A close, highly motivated team that prefers to promote from within.
Time off.
Every long weekend, the Friday is off too. The company closes for a week between Christmas and New Year.

Package

CAD $180,000 to $200,000 Competitive benefits through Manulife: Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance Employee Assistance Program Equity: Stock Options 3 weeks vacation plus an additional 10 days around statutory holidays
Our downtown Kitchener office has an onsite gym and weekly team lunches. For remote team members we run other social activities.

Location

Headquartered in downtown Kitchener, Ontario, with hybrid work arrangements. Kitchener-based candidates are preferred. We will also consider strong candidates in the Toronto area who can be in Kitchener regularly.

How We Hire

We use AI tools to support our recruitment process, including helping us organize applications and identify early matches based on role criteria. That said, every rejection decision is made by a human. We encourage candidates to apply authentically and avoid relying solely on AI-generated responses, especially during interviews.

Do you feel like you're able to tackle this role? Show us what you got! We absolutely don't expect applicants to check off every box for any of our positions, and welcome you to apply if you feel like you are an excellent fit.

This opportunity is offered through HighlightTA, the on-demand talent team supporting RouteThis's growth.

Please let us know if you require an accommodation due to a disability, and RouteThis will work with you to address your needs.

Role Summary

The AVP Technology Lead – Digital is a strategic technology leader responsible for enabling, scaling, and modernizing Sun Life Canada’s shared digital platforms that support secure, connected, and frictionless Client and advisor experiences. This role provides technology leadership across core digital assets including Secure Web, Public Web, & Secure Mobile, and related enablement platforms such as client identity and access management, and an internal design system.

The role combines strategic leadership, technical oversight, people leadership, delivery execution, operational accountability, and vendor/financial management to drive technology excellence and measurable business value. The AVP partners closely with Product, Client Experience, Architecture, Cybersecurity, Operations, Engineering, and Business leaders to ensure digital assets are resilient, scalable, secure, reusable, and aligned to enterprise priorities.

This role operates in a complex, high-visibility environment where digital platform reliability, modernization, and cross-business enablement are critical to Client outcomes. The leader must be able to bring clarity to a broad mandate, make decisions in ambiguity, and build a high-performing technology organization that balances speed, stability, security, and long-term platform health.

What will you do?

Technology Strategy, Platform Enablement & Engineering
Shape, communicate, and align the digital technology strategy across business units, ensuring it supports near-term delivery commitments and longer-term modernization objectives.
Partner with Business Leads, Product, Client Experience, Architecture, Cybersecurity, Operations, and Enterprise Technology to define platform roadmaps, OKRs, sequencing, and investment priorities.
Provide thought leadership on the evolution of shared digital platforms, including identity, web, mobile, integration, data enablement, and reusable digital capabilities.
Promote technology stack standards, modern engineering practices, automation, and architectural discipline, balancing build vs. buy vs. partner decisions in a complex technology ecosystem.
Ensure design and engineering decisions account for reusability, scalability, security, maintainability, accessibility, and technical debt reduction.
Create the conditions for exceptional digital experiences by enabling business and product teams with reliable, scalable, secure, and reusable platforms.
Platform Delivery & Execution
Accountable for end-to-end delivery of digital platform capabilities, including oversight of internal delivery teams, vendors, system integrators, and total cost of ownership.
Drive delivery excellence by improving velocity, quality, reliability, predictability, and agile maturity across multiple squads.
Track delivery metrics, identify bottlenecks, and implement targeted productivity and delivery maturity improvements.
Serve as the primary escalation point for platform, delivery, vendor, and dependency-related issues, enabling rapid resolution in a complex environment.
Ensure delivery is integrated across product, architecture, engineering, operations, cybersecurity, and business priorities.
Embed test-and-learn, automation, and continuous improvement practices to improve speed, quality, and sustainability.
People Leadership & Capability Development
Lead, mentor, and develop technology leaders and teams, fostering a collaborative, inclusive, accountable, and execution-focused culture.
Design and optimize team structures to support clear ownership, delivery outcomes, modernization priorities, and clear accountabilities.
Partner with Chapter, Engineering, Product, and Business leaders on workforce planning, role clarity, succession planning, and capability development.
Build internal capability in digital engineering, enablement, agile delivery, vendor management, and operational excellence.
Coach leaders to manage performance effectively, clarify ownership, and build resilient teams through change and transformation.
Financial & Vendor Management
Lead budget management, including annual planning, cost tracking, capitalization, forecasting, and investment prioritization.
Manage strategic vendor and system integrator relationships, holding partners accountable for delivery quality, outcomes, knowledge transfer, and value realization.
Drive cost transparency and technology spend optimization across applications, infrastructure, security, vendor, and platform investments.
Identify opportunities to reduce long-term dependency on external partners while strengthening internal platform ownership and capability.
Operational Excellence, Risk & Security
Ensure stability, security, technology currency, resiliency, and end-of-life decommissioning for applications within scope.
Establish governance processes that balance speed of delivery with risk management, audit, regulatory, cybersecurity, and control requirements.
Partner with Application Operations to ensure effective incident management, change management, disaster recovery, and business continuity planning.
Proactively manage operational risk, application health, technical debt, and service reliability across shared digital capabilities.
Cross-Functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement
Act as a strategic technology partner to leaders across Product, Client Experience, Business, Operations, Architecture, Cybersecurity, and Enterprise Technology.
Communicate digital strategy, delivery status, risks, trade-offs, and dependencies with clarity and transparency.
Represent the Digital technology function in executive forums, bringing enterprise perspective, external insight, and pragmatic recommendations.
Strengthen alignment between technology investments, business priorities, Client experience outcomes, and enterprise digital strategy.

Accountabilities

Align digital strategy with business objectives, Client outcomes, enterprise standards, and shared technology priorities.
Define and monitor roadmaps, OKRs, modernization priorities, and delivery sequencing.
Oversee execution across delivery teams, vendors, system integrators, and enterprise partners.
Establish governance, track delivery metrics, and drive productivity, quality, and reliability improvements.
Manage budgets, vendor relationships, and cost optimization opportunities.
Build and sustain a high-performing, engaged, inclusive, and platform-oriented technology organization.
Ensure digital platforms are secure, scalable, resilient, reusable, and positioned to support future growth.

What you need to succeed?

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field; advanced degree or MBA is an asset.
10+ years of experience in senior technology leadership roles with demonstrated success delivering complex, mission-critical digital platforms.
Experience leading modernization and enablement of digital platforms such as identity, web, mobile, integration, or client/advisor experience platforms.

Strong financial acumen with experience managing sizable technology budgets, vendor portfolios, and total cost of ownership.
Strong stakeholder management, executive communication, and organizational leadership skills.
Experience in regulated financial services is valuable; depth in digital enablement, engineering excellence, and vendor-heavy delivery environments is prioritized.
As this position is posted in several locations, we specify that bilingualism (French, English, both oral and written) is required for Quebec only for the frequent interactions with English and French-speaking colleagues or internal partners across Canada or worldwide

Mindset & Behaviours

Decisive leader comfortable operating in ambiguity, complexity, and transformation.
Strong technical credibility with the ability to challenge architecture, delivery practices, platform decisions, and CI/CD approaches.
Builder mindset with equal focus on fixing, scaling, enabling, and simplifying.
Pragmatic, outcomes-driven decision-maker who balances speed, stability, risk, and long-term application health.

jobs.title: Director, Business Intelligence
jobs.description:
At Viral Nation,
we specialize in building social-first ecosystems for brands to connect with the modern consumer journey. Our integrated solutions align strategy, talent, media, and technology with culturally relevant creativity to scale the world’s fastest-growing digital brands. Viral Nation offers a fluid, creative, and growth-oriented environment that will support your ambitions to apply your talents in an open, collaborative, and fast-paced culture. Our ability to stay at the forefront of the industry has fuelled our success and will guide us in paving the path forward. We’re driven to push boundaries and think beyond today to deliver strategies, and we’re just getting started.

While we continuously exceed our goals, we need your help – our success is only as great as our people. Strong performance leads to high expectations, and we must keep raising the bar!

The Director, Business Intelligence will lead enterprise-wide analytics strategy and will be responsible for building and leading a high-performing team of analysts delivering actionable insights across sales forecasting, retail performance, campaign measurement, and influencer/paid/social strategy optimization.

This leader will serve as a strategic thought partner to Sales, Marketing, Brand, eCommerce, Finance, and Executive Leadership, translating data into commercial growth opportunities, driving ROI, and embedding analytics into core business decision-making. The role combines strategic vision, technical depth, cross-functional leadership, and team development.

Responsibilities:

Act as a senior analytics partner to client account, strategy, and service teams by translating client objectives into scalable, best-in-class measurement frameworks that support social-first marketing performance.
Serve as the senior analytics advisor to executive leadership, shaping marketing, retail, and social investment decisions through data-driven insights.
Elevate analytics from reporting to strategic advantage by synthesizing data into clear narratives that inform brand positioning, channel strategy, and enterprise decision-making.
Own end-to-end measurement strategy across paid media, influencer, social, and retail media, ensuring clear linkage between investment and revenue outcomes.
Forecast and quantify incremental revenue and retail lift across eCommerce and offline retail partners by developing predictive models that connect media spend, influencer engagement, and social performance to sales velocity and conversion.
Design and operationalize robust ROI frameworks, including brand lift studies, sales lift studies, incrementality testing, multi-touch attribution, and marketing mix modeling, translating insights into optimized channel mix and budget allocation.
Build scalable measurement systems to evaluate influencer effectiveness, content performance, audience growth, and conversion impact, informing creative strategy and platform optimization.
Identify emerging consumer and digital engagement trends to inform brand strategy, innovation, and go-to-market planning.
Build, lead, and mentor a high-performing analytics team, fostering a culture of analytical rigor, commercial acumen, and executive-ready storytelling.
Design and oversee scalable data collection and reporting infrastructure, including structured databases, automated reporting workflows, dashboards, and standardized presentations.

Qualifications:

Extensive experience in marketing, media, or agency environments, with demonstrated ability to apply analytics and research to drive client strategy and business outcomes.
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a relevant field (Social Sciences, Statistics, Data Science, Business Analytics, or related discipline), or equivalent practical experience.
12+ years of progressive experience in research, analytics, and measurement, with a proven track record of leading complex, high-impact initiatives.
Advanced expertise in primary and secondary research methodologies, including brand tracking, brand and communications strategy, brand lift studies, regression analysis, Market Mix Modeling, social listening, and digital and site analytics.
Deep technical proficiency in analytics and BI technologies, including Python and SQL for analysis and data modeling, Google Cloud Platform, BigQuery, and Snowflake for data infrastructure, and BI tools such as Sigma or comparable platforms for scalable reporting and dashboarding.
Demonstrated ability to architect and optimize analytics workflows, data pipelines, and reporting systems that support automation, scalability, and self-serve insights.
Strong executive-level communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to translate complex analytical findings into clear, actionable recommendations for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Proven ability to influence cross-functional teams and senior client stakeholders, providing strategic guidance grounded in data, research rigor, and business context.

This role has an annual salary range of $140,000 - $160,000.

This range reflects the full scope and progression of the role, from building capability to operating with sustained impact at a higher level. In addition to base salary, we offer a comprehensive benefits and total rewards package designed to support our team as they grow with us.

Where an offer falls within this range is determined through the interview process. Candidates are benchmarked by the hiring team based on role scope, relevant experience, skill alignment, and expected impact, using consistent and objective criteria.

Compensation Philosophy:

At Viral Nation, compensation is structured, performance-led, and market-aligned. Pay decisions are intentional, based on role requirements, performance, and market alignment by country, and are set to maintain internal pay equity across comparable roles and levels.

Compensation progression is tied to demonstrated performance, expanded scope, and sustained contribution over time, not tenure alone. Employee compensation is reviewed regularly through formal performance reviews and check-ins to ensure alignment with role expectations and impact.

AI in Recruitment:

Viral Nation does not use AI-enabled tools to screen, assess, rank, or select candidates – our hiring teams make all hiring decisions. AI note-taking tools may be used during interviews.

DEI Commitment:

Viral Nation is committed to diversity, equity and inclusion in our agency. Viral Nation welcomes applications from people with visible and non-visible disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the recruiting and selection process.

jobs.description:
Description And Requirements

The Director of Project Finance & M&A is responsible for leading financial analysis, structuring and financial due diligence for mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, and strategic investments in renewable energy assets and platforms across the United States and Canada.

Reporting to the Head of Finance & Insurance, this role plays a central role in evaluating transaction opportunities, structuring project financings, and supporting capital formation activities, including tax equity, tax credit transferability, and project debt.

The Director will work closely with the M&A, Business Development, Legal, Tax, and Asset Management teams, as well as external advisors and capital providers, to ensure robust financial evaluation and optimal financing structures for investments and operating assets.

The role requires strong expertise in renewable energy project finance, financial modeling, tax equity structures, transferability, and project-level debt financing.

To maximize collaboration and innovation, an essential function of this role is a regular onsite presence in an Enel office. 

The Instrument and Controls Specialist is responsible to support execute and provide configuration and maintenance services for the Process Control System and other automation systems at the Enel Green Power Facilities for Solar assets. Ensure facility controls automation and machinery function safely, efficiently, reliably and within budgetary limits, utilizing allocated resources, with the objective of meeting business goals for production while minimizing unscheduled equipment down time. Provide day-to-day maintenance activities and provide mentoring/coaching to less experienced employees.

What you will do Responsibilities, include, but not limited to:

M&A Financial Due Diligence and Transaction Support

Lead financial due diligence for acquisitions, divestitures, and joint venture transactions, including review of project financial models, assumptions, capital structures, and financing arrangements.

Evaluate project economics, financing structures, tax attributes, and key commercial contracts to identify financial risks and value drivers.

Coordinate with internal teams and external advisors on buy-side and sell-side transaction processes, including data room review, financial analysis, and diligence reporting.

Prepare investment committee materials, valuation analyses, and transaction recommendations for senior management.

Project Finance Structuring

Support the origination, negotiation, and closing of project financings including tax equity partnerships, transferability transactions, and term debt facilities.

Coordinate closely with lenders, tax equity investors, transferability buyers, and financial advisors during transaction execution.

Analyze and structure tax equity partnership transactions, including partnership flip structures and related financial modeling.

Conduct sensitivity analysis, valuation analysis, and financing optimization scenarios.

Ensure modeling assumptions are aligned with project contracts, tax structures, and financing agreements.

Provide financial input into investment committee materials and strategic decision processes.

Work closely with M&A, Development, Valuation, Legal, Tax, and Asset Management teams to support project execution and investment decision making.

What you will bring

Education

Master’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business Administration or related field

Experience

MBA, CFA or other professional designation preferred

Minimum 6–8 years of experience in project finance, investment banking, or renewable energy transactions

Direct experience with M&A financial due diligence and transaction execution

Demonstrated experience with tax equity structures, tax credit transferability transactions, and project debt financing

Experience In Renewable Energy Or Power Sector Required

Technical Skills

Advanced financial modeling and valuation skills

Strong understanding of project finance structures and capital markets

Experience reviewing and negotiating financing term sheets and transaction documentation

Professional Skills

Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities

Excellent written and verbal communication skills

Ability to present complex financial analysis to senior management

Strong negotiation and stakeholder management capabilities

Ability to manage multiple transaction processes simultaneously

Why join us?

Please see below for additional information on Enel North America rewards.

Enel North America offers its regular full-time employees affordable, quality healthcare for you and your family, life insurance and disability benefits to provide security, and retirement benefits to help you plan for your financial future. In addition, we offer an array of other benefits such as flexible spending accounts, tuition reimbursement and professional development allowance. 

Benefits are effective as of day one! 

Some additional perks to working with Enel North America include: 

401k with match fully vested as of day one. Enel-NA matches 100% of the first 4% that you contribute up to set IRS limits. 

Generous PTO that supports work/life balance including: 4 weeks annually of vacation as well as personal days, volunteer days, your birthday off, paid holidays, and sick time. Proration may apply during first year of employment. 

Paid leave programs 

The opportunity to grow and develop your career with the support and mentorship of senior leaders. 

The opportunity to work for one of the world’s most recognizable and respected brands in the energy industry that believes by working together we can create a new energy era in which the world can become more sustainable. 

An employee’s eligibility for these benefits shall be subject to the governing documents for such plans and programs and/or company policy. The benefits described above may be modified or eliminated with or without notice in accordance with the governing documents and applicable law.

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and the Selection Process

Enel North America is dedicated to providing equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender, national origin, citizenship, age, disability, sexual orientation, genetic information. We will not discriminate, in any employment decision, against any individual or group on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, gender, national origin, citizenship, age, disability, sexual orientation, genetic information, or veterans/national guard/military reserve status. This shall be done in compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws in every location in which Enel North America has facilities. Enel North America maintains a drug-free workplace and performs pre-employment substance abuse testing and background checks, where permitted by law. Accessibility – If you require accessibility assistance applying for open positions please contact EnelApplication@enel.com.

The selection process includes an initial introductory interview with the Recruiting team, followed by an interview with the relevant business line. If your profile matches the requirements of the role, we will contact you to share all the details of the next steps.

Enel North America is committed to providing a fair and transparent hiring process for all job seekers. We will never ask you to pay money or provide sensitive information, such as your social security number or bank account number, as part of the application process. We only hire through our official channels, which include our website and LinkedIn page. If you receive a job offer that did not come through one of those channels, it is likely a scam, and we suggest reporting it to the authorities.

We are looking for individuals who embody our values: trust, respect, innovation, proactivity, and flexibility.

Do you want to be a part of change? Apply now and join the Solar O&M team to help drive the energy transition with us!

Notice to Recruiters & Staffing Agencies

Enel North America has an internal talent acquisition department and designated career site for individuals looking to join our team. Enel North America will not accept unsolicited resumes from any external recruiters, staffing firms, search agencies or any fee-based referrals. Any unsolicited resumes sent to directly to Enel North America, in any capacity will be considered property of Enel North America. This policy is applicable to all Enel North America locations and will be the responsibility of third parties and vendors to understand this policy. Enel North America will not pay a fee for any placement resulting from the receipt of an unsolicited resume.

Who we are

Enel North America:

Enel North America is a proven renewables leader delivering clean, flexible and sustainable energy solutions.

As part of the Enel Group, we develop, build, own and operate renewable power plants and demand response solutions, with over 11 gigawatts (GW) of installed wind and solar capacity, over 1 GW of energy storage and nearly 5 GW of demand response in the US and Canada.

For nearly 25 years, we've reliably powered modern life and driven climate action with our people, partners and communities by putting sustainability at the center of everything we do. Enel is a top-five industry leader for clean power capacity in the US, demand response in North America and utility-scale battery storage in Texas.

We are a smart and passionate team working together to build the Enel North America that we want for the long-term – one that is founded on strong financial, social and environmental values. Being on our team means being part of lasting progress to create a thriving and more sustainable world for our climate and communities. It means valuing safety, trust, innovation, proactivity, flexibility and respect in all we do. Our vision is ambitious, and we'll get there together.

Enel Spa

Enel is a multinational power company and a leading integrated player in the global power and renewables markets, present in 27 countries worldwide.

At global level, it is the largest renewable player, the foremost electricity distribution network player by number of grid customers served and the biggest retail operator by customer base.

Enel generates electricity with approximately 93 GW of total capacity. Enel Green Power, the Group’s renewables arm, has a total capacity of approximately 68 GW and a generation mix that includes wind, solar, geothermal, and hydroelectric power, as well as energy storage facilities, installed in Europe, the Americas, Africa, Asia, and Oceania.

Enel Grids, the Group’s global business line dedicated to the management of the electricity distribution service worldwide, delivers electricity through a network of 1.9 million kilometers with more than 69 million end users connected to its distribution grids. Enel Commercial is the Group’s arm dedicated to customers around the world with the aim of effectively providing products and services based on their energy needs and encouraging them towards a more conscious and sustainable use of energy. It provides electricity, gas and integrated services to more than 29 million customers globally including households, enterprises, industries and public administrations. In addition, it offers flexibility services aggregating 10.2 GW and has over 34,000 owned public charging points for electric mobility.

Curious about us? Discover more at www.enel.com

.

jobs.description:
WHO ARE WE?

At Nexans our global vision is to electrify the future. For over a century, Nexans has played a crucial role in the electrification of the planet. With around 28,000 people in 42 countries, the Group is leading the charge to the new world of electrification: safer, sustainable, renewable, decarbonized and accessible to everyone Nexans recognizes the differences that make each employee valuable and unique.

WELCOMING YOU TO THE TEAM

Our story starts in 1911, manufacturing cables to support the distribution of power generated from Niagara Falls, Nexans has proudly contributed to Canada's growth. We have been involved in many of Canada's most ambitious projects; from dams, bridges, energy transmission and distribution to railroads and transportation. We are a vertically integrated manufacturer and our products are made at facilities located in Quebec, Ontario, and Saskatchewan.

As Finance Director, Canada, you will report directly to the VP Finance, North America. This role is being created as part of the North American transformation, establishing dedicated Canadian and US organizations under a new North American business group. The Finance Director will provide financial leadership for the Canadian business, partnering closely with the broader North American leadership team to drive financial performance and support the growth and development of the Canadian organization

GETTING TO KNOW THE POSITION

One of the strategic orientations that Nexans pursues consists in capturing growth and differentiating its offer by escalading the value chain from the production of cables towards the provision of innovative cable systems and services and solutions to better address the current and future needs of our partners and customers.

The Finance Director, Canada is responsible for driving the financial performance of the Canadian Business Unit in alignment with NAM objectives. The role oversees financial planning, budgeting, reporting, and controls, while ensuring compliance with Group policies and supporting sound business decisions. The Finance Director also leads and develops the Canadian finance team, partnering with the business to optimize financial performance and resources.

How You Make An Impact

Financial Strategy & Business Performance

Directs and oversees the financial activities of the Canadian organization, ensuring strong financial performance, sound governance, and alignment with Nexans Group and North American objectives.
Provides strategic financial leadership and insight to support business decisions, including investments, acquisitions, divestitures, capital allocation, pension matters, and other strategic initiatives.
Provides timely and accurate financial analysis, reporting, forecasts, and business indicators to support decision-making by Canadian and North American senior management, Nexans Corporate, and COMEX.
Acts as a strategic business partner to the leadership team and operational functions, providing financial expertise and challenging assumptions to support profitable and sustainable growth.
Monitors business and market trends, including relevant competitor and economic developments, and provides financial insights to support the organization's positioning and decision-making.
Provides financial advice and support in the negotiation and review of strategic commercial contracts and agreements, including contracts with significant financial, commodity, or foreign exchange exposure.

Planning, Budgeting & Forecasting

Leads the annual budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning processes, ensuring alignment with business objectives and Group requirements.
Continually improves the budgeting and forecasting process by strengthening financial discipline and developing the financial understanding of department and business leaders.
Oversees the monitoring of financial performance against budget, forecast, and business objectives, identifying risks, opportunities, and corrective actions.
Provides financial analysis and recommendations to support cost optimization and improve overall business performance.

Financial Reporting & Governance

Defines and oversees the monthly consolidated reporting process, including sales, P&L, MMR, and other key financial indicators for the Canadian organization and North American Business Group.
Ensures the timely and accurate preparation and consolidation of financial reports, management analysis, forecasts, and financial outlooks.
Ensures compliance with applicable accounting standards, Group policies, IFRS, and Canadian accounting and regulatory requirements.
Establishes, implements, and maintains appropriate financial policies, procedures, systems, and internal controls to safeguard company assets and ensure the integrity and reliability of financial information.
Represents Finance in internal and external audits and ensures timely follow-up and resolution of audit findings.

Cash, Treasury, Tax & Risk Management

Develops and implements strategies to optimize cash flow, working capital, liquidity, and overall financial performance.
Oversees treasury activities, banking relationships, credit policies, and other areas impacting the organization's cash position and financial resilience.
Ensures, in coordination with Nexans Corporate and relevant internal stakeholders, compliance with applicable Canadian tax requirements and monitors changes in legislation that may impact the business.
Identifies, assesses, and manages key financial and business risks, ensuring appropriate mitigation measures and controls are in place.
Provides financial guidance on matters involving foreign exchange, commodity exposure, financing, and other financial risks, as applicable.

Finance Transformation & Continuous Improvement

Leads initiatives to optimize financial processes, strengthen cost control, improve reporting efficiency, and increase the automation and digitalization of Finance activities.
Drives continuous improvement of Finance systems, processes, and controls to improve the overall efficiency, effectiveness, and quality of financial operations.
Ensures that Finance policies, procedures, and systems evolve in line with the organization's changing business needs and Group requirements.

Finance Leadership & Organizational Effectiveness

Leads and develops the Finance organization, ensuring appropriate capabilities, performance, succession, and professional development to support the organization's financial objectives.
Continuously assesses the effectiveness and organizational structure of the Finance function and implements improvements to enhance efficiency and business support.
Promotes a strong culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, compliance, and business partnership within the Finance organization.

North American & Group Collaboration

Supports and contributes to North American strategic initiatives and synergies, including cross-functional initiatives defined as NAM priorities.
Collaborates closely with Nexans Corporate, North American leadership, and other Finance leaders to ensure alignment of financial strategies, reporting, controls, and business priorities.
Provides financial support and analysis for major North American and Group initiatives, ensuring appropriate financial evaluation, risk assessment, and follow-up.
Ensures effective communication of financial performance, risks, opportunities, and recommendations to senior leadership and relevant stakeholders.

You will be expected to:

Maximize the Canadian BU profits through an adequate administration of expenses, costs, placement of funds and use of resources.
Deliver accurate and timely financial reporting, forecasts, and insights to support business decisions.
Improve financial performance through strong planning, cost control, and working capital management.
Ensure compliance with Nexans policies, accounting standards, internal controls, and Canadian regulations.
Build a strong and effective Finance team with the right capabilities to support the business.
Drive continuous improvement and strengthen Finance processes, systems, and business support.

WHAT YOU BRING TO THE ROLE ?

Professional degree in Accounting and/or related fields
Postgraduate degree / Master Finance or MBA
Minimum 7 years of experience directing financial areas, or developing financial processes
Knowledge of IFRS accounting standards
Knowledge in the SAP/BI System
Financial reporting/consolidation

About Kinaxis

Are you looking to join an innovative, market-leading company where you can truly elevate your career? At Kinaxis we are serious about culture, we are serious about technology, we are serious about customers, and we are serious about not taking ourselves too seriously. If you are looking to be part of an incredible growth story, then we might just be the place for you!

In 1984, we started out as a team of three engineers. Today, we have grown to become a global organization with over 2000 employees around the world, 6 global office and a best-in-class HQ in Ottawa, Canada. As winners of several Top Employer awards globally, we are proud to work with our customers and employees towards solving some of the biggest challenges facing supply chains today.

Kinaxis is a global leader in modern supply chain orchestration, powering complex global supply chains, and supporting the people who manage them. Our powerful, AI infused platform provides full transparency and visibility across end-to-end supply chains, enabling our customers to make faster, better decisions. We are trusted by renowned global brands to provide the agility and predictability needed to navigate today’s volatility and disruption. With more than 40,000 users in over 100 countries, we are expanding our team as we continue to innovate and revolutionize how we support our customers.

Location

Ottawa and Toronto, CA - Hybrid

Other Canadian locations - Remote

About The Team

Our Financial Planning and Analysis (FP&A) team partners with leaders across the company to help drive business decisions. They work with stakeholders to highlight insights and analysis needed to make data-driven decisions that help fuel growth and operational excellence. The Director, Financial Planning & Analysis, is a trusted advisor and subject matter expert who brings a depth and breadth of knowledge and expertise in leading, directing, and developing the overall operations and delivery of revenue forecasting, consolidated forecasts and reporting, external metrics, and evolving financial planning strategies within Kinaxis.

This role is ideal for a forward-thinking finance leader who combines deep financial expertise with strong business acumen, operational excellence, and a passion for transforming finance through data, automation, and AI-enabled insights.

Partnering closely with the VP, Financial Planning & Analysis the Director, Financial Planning & Analysis is responsible for effective management and continuous improvement of budgeting and forecasting cycles and provides strategic financial consultation and support to the business.

Vacancy Status

This is an existing job vacancy

What you will do

Business Performance & FP&A Excellence

Build an integrated, enterprise-wide planning process across business units and regions to drive business objectives and long-term growth.
Develop key financial models and scenarios to evaluate strategic initiatives and investments, with a view to multi-year projections.
Lead scenario planning, sensitivity analysis, and financial modeling to support strategic decisions.
Manage and drive management reporting – analyze financial results, distill and synthesize issues and communicate key messages (including business risks) to the senior leadership team.
Support Board reporting, executive presentations, and investor reporting and communications.
Deliver actionable financial insights that influence investment priorities, resource allocation, pricing, and growth initiatives.
Demonstrated outstanding communication and executive presentation skills, with the ability to translate complex financial information into clear business insights.
Develop KPIs and performance dashboards that provide timely visibility into business health.
Foster strong partnerships across the organization including Product, Sales, Corporate Functions and other teams.

Finance Transformation & Technology

Through personalized, preventative, and whole person approaches to health and wellness, we help residents and members better understand their health, take ownership of their wellbeing, and live healthier, more connected lives.

We are seeking a National Director of Wellness Strategy
to lead the development and evolution of our national wellness strategy, with an immediate focus on Allbright, functional health and wellness clinics, and Lifestyle Residences. jobs.description:

8:30am to 4:30pm / Monday to Friday

 This position is currently under consideration for an internal candidate. However, we welcome all applications and will review submissions in accordance with university hiring policies.

ABOUT EMILY CARR UNIVERSITY OF ART + DESIGN

Situated on unceded, traditional and ancestral xʷməθkʷəy̓əm (Musqueam), Sḵwx̱wú7mesh Úxwumixw (Squamish), and səl̓ilw̓ətaʔɬ (Tsleil-Waututh) territories in Vancouver, Canada, Emily Carr University of Art + Design (ECU) is where creativity meets practice. Ranked among the world’s top 30 universities for art and design (QS 2024), ECU is recognized globally for its hands-on, practice-based teaching and learning environment that equips students to experiment, take risks and drive innovation.

Since 1925, ECU has championed bold ideas and emerging talent through a close-knit, studio-intensive setting that connects students with award-winning faculty, cutting-edge facilities, and real-world opportunities. Today, ECU serves more than 2,400 undergraduate and graduate students, along with thousands more through continuing studies, contributing to Canada’s cultural and creative sectors and shaping the future of art, media, design and research.

Having marked our centennial in 2025, ECU continues to ask what art and design can make possible.100 years in the making, we are shaping what comes next.

About The Role

Reporting to the Vice-President, Finance + Administration, the Director, Financial Services is responsible for leading the University in the ongoing process of continuous improvement in business and accounting practices. This position is responsible for the administration of financial policy, the overall management of accounting operations, financial report systems, and the monitoring of financial performance in accordance with University policy. The Director provides leadership and direction to the Finance Department and ensures the integrity of data in a complex integrated database (Colleague). A key function of the Director is to translate unstructured ideas into coherent presentations suitable for implementation according to the University’s needs.

Benefits Of Joining The Emily Carr Community

Enrollment in a comprehensive benefits package, including Dental Coverage, Extended Health, Disability Coverage and Life Insurance.
Membership in the College Pension Plan.
Competitive vacation and Professional Development benefits.

AS THE SUCCESSFUL APPLICANT, YOU SHOULD POSSESS

Professional designation in accounting from a recognized educational institution (CPA).
Minimum ten years of progressively responsible experience in financial and administrative management.
Expertise in budget planning, financial management and control, as well as administration of budget and financial resources.
Extensive experience with computer based accounting systems and large database.
Demonstrated knowledge in area of expertise, along with supervisory and leadership experience.
Expert communication, interpersonal and presentation skills with the ability to build relationships and cooperation on a University-wide level.
Ability to set and communicate high standards for group performance within the Financial Services department and to facilitate and motivate teamwork.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to apply sound judgement in problem solving and evaluate courses of action.
Ability to advise on and make complex financial decisions.
Strong computer skills with advanced proficiency in Word, Excel and PowerPoint.

Typical Duties

Develops, administers, and ensures compliance with guidelines, policies and procedures for effective financial management of the University’s resources leading to continuous improvement in business and accounting practices.
Reviews and prepares analyses of financial information and ensures the completion of both internal and external financial reports by communicated deadlines, including all provincial and federal reporting requirements.
Responds to requests for ad hoc information from the VP, Finance + Administration, the President + Vice-Chancellor, administrative management, and external agencies, and provides effective counsel and assistance.
Participates as required in short and long range strategic planning, collaborating with administrative management and producing coherent implementation plans from unstructured proposals.
Designs and maintains an internal control framework for the Financial Services area such that business loss is mitigated.
Manages cash flow requirements and invests surplus funds in line with established investment policy.
Responsible for the year-end audit processes and reviews preparation of annual working papers and financial statements for external auditors. Manages the preparation of analysis and supporting documents for review by the VP, Finance + Administration and the Ministry of Post-Secondary Education and Future Skills.
Directly supervises the management positions within Financial Services and ensures all responsibilities are carried out effectively. Maintains oversight of the Financial Services department staff including recruitment and selection, orientation, performance planning and review and ongoing training and development.
Collaborates with the Associate Vice-President, Human Resources in hiring, discipline, dismissal and grievance procedures and collective agreement administration relating to support staff. Produces labour costing for collective bargaining and participates directly in collective agreement negotiations.
Arranges for tenders of University banking services and external audits, establishing criteria to make decisions and providing reports and recommendations to the VP, Finance + Administration and the Board.
Responsible for the preparation of the annual budget. Assists the VP, Finance + Administration in financial planning, forecasting, development and consolidation of budgets and in the development of presentations to the Board. Prepares, analyses and adjusts University budget based on long term plans; divisional submissions and established priorities for review by the VP, Finance + Administration.
Reviews and interprets month-end financial results. Advises VP, Finance + Administration of results through management reports, highlighting potential issues or problems.
Participates on University committees as assigned.
Responsible for ensuring the completion of weekly cheque runs, ensuring appropriate audit and authorization is performed before processing.
Maintains currency in legislation and regulations and in area of professional expertise. Maintains an active role in professional activities relating to the area of responsibility by participating in associations and committee’s external to the University.
Manages the department budget and is responsible for expenditures and allocations within that budget.
Collaborates with the Executive Director, University Advancement + Events to maintain detailed financial records and provides advice on the management of endowed funds.
Acts for the VP, Finance + Administration in his/her absence.
Performs other related duties as required.
