jobs.description:
Organization: Cambridge Memorial Hospital
Position: Director, Finance
Location: Cambridge, ON (on-site)
Salary: $155,000 - $185,000

THE ORGANIZATION
Cambridge Memorial Hospital (CMH) is more than a hospital: they are a cornerstone of a vibrant, rapidly growing community and an organization in transformation. Following a major redevelopment and expansion, CMH is redefining what exceptional community healthcare looks like, delivering high-quality, patient-centred care while building for the future. CMH is building healthier communities together . As a thriving acute care hospital serving the Waterloo Wellington Region and beyond, CMH provides comprehensive services including Emergency, Surgery, Medicine, Women’s and Children’s Health, Intensive Care, and Mental Health.

As healthcare continues to evolve, CMH is seeking an accomplished and forward-thinking Director, Finance to join our senior leadership team. This is a rare opportunity to influence strategy at an organization that combines the complexity of a large healthcare environment with the agility, collegiality, and impact of a community hospital.

As healthcare funding models evolve and system pressures increase, CMH is seeking a strategic and forward-thinking Director, Finance to play a critical leadership role in ensuring the organization’s long-term financial sustainability and operational excellence. This is a high-impact opportunity to serve as a trusted financial advisor to the Executive Team and Board Committees while leading a dedicated finance team in delivering robust financial stewardship in a complex healthcare environment

THE OPPORTUNITY
Reporting to the Vice President, Corporate Services & Chief Financial Officer the Director, Finance provides enterprise-wide leadership and oversight of the hospital’s financial operations, planning, reporting, treasury, and internal control environment.
Working at the intersection of finance, operations, and strategy, the Director will help guide the organization through evolving funding models, growth opportunities, capital investments, and system transformation initiatives.

The Director is responsible for advancing financial strategy, strengthening fiscal stewardship, optimizing funding opportunities, and ensuring regulatory compliance, while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. As a key leader, the Director partners closely with clinical and operational leaders to align financial planning with organizational priorities. This role extends far beyond traditional financial oversight.

The Director is a trusted advisor and business partner who helps shape organizational strategy, supports critical decision-making, identifies opportunities for innovation and efficiency, and ensures CMH remains well-positioned to thrive in an increasingly complex healthcare environment.

As Director, Finance, you will drive strategic decision-making through:
Providing financial leadership and insight to the Executive Team, Directors' Council, and Board Committees, ensuring leaders have the information and analysis needed to make confident, informed decisions.
Leading long-range financial planning, capital planning, and sustainability strategies that support CMH's vision for growth and excellence.
Navigating evolving provincial funding models and healthcare priorities while identifying opportunities to optimize resources and strengthen organizational performance.
Developing and mentoring an engaged, talented finance team while fostering a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning.
Collaborating closely with clinical and operational leaders, the CMH Foundation, and community partners to support strategic initiatives, business cases, capital investments, and service enhancements.

IDEAL CANDIDATE
A senior leader with passion for healthcare and community impact.
Strong experience in hospitals with a minimum of 7–10 years of progressive financial experience navigating complexity and driving meaningful change.
Experience working within a publicly funded environment and familiarity with Ministry of Health reporting requirements.
Proven success leading budgeting, forecasting, audit, and financial reporting functions.
Experience presenting financial information to senior leadership and/or Board Committees.
The ability to think strategically with strong business and financial acumen while maintaining operational excellence.
Strong relationship-building and influencing skills and a collaborative leadership style that inspires confidence and trust and an ability to engage across disciplines.
Clear, confident communicator capable of translating complex financial information for diverse audiences.
Ability to lead effectively in a dynamic and evolving healthcare environment and a commitment to developing people and building high-performing teams.
Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills.
Advanced knowledge of MIS guidelines, systems implementations, financial systems, financial modelling and advanced spreadsheet applications.
Familiarity with procurement practices and the Broader Public Sector Procurement Directive is an asset.
Bachelor’s degree in Commerce, Business, Finance, or related field.
Professional accounting designation (CPA or equivalent).

The Director, Finance role is a current existing vacancy. LHH Knightsbridge does not use artificial intelligence (AI) to screen, assess, or select applicants for a position.

At Cambridge Memorial Hospital (CMH), community matters to us. We acknowledge and are grateful for the opportunity to meet, work and offer healthcare on what is the traditional territories for the Anishinaabe, the Haudenosaunee and the Chinnonton.

We are committed to providing and fostering a respectful, caring, and inclusive workplace; one that generates belonging. We want a work culture where people are free to express their authentic selves and are able to bring their best daily. That includes a workplace that is free from violence, harassment and discrimination of any kind.

We welcome all applicants and encourage members of equity-deserving groups including Indigenous and LGBTQ2SIA+ communities regardless of race, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, lifestyle, age, educational background, national origin, religion, neurodiversity or physical ability. We promise to ask if needed, and to provide reasonable accommodation to you during the recruitment and selection process to ensure an equitable experience.

To support all of us in this journey, Cambridge Memorial Hospital is an employee partner with the Canadian Centre for Diversity & Inclusion (CCDI) and provides access to all CMH members to CCDI resources and education. We encourage you to reflect upon our inclusive commitment to you as we welcome and encourage you to explore a promising future career at CMH.

Significant investments in systems, reporting capabilities, process improvement, and business growth are planned over the coming years, and this role will play a central leadership role in guiding that transformation.

· Director of Finance & Business Leadership: Lead the organization’s overall finance strategy and financial operations. · Systems & Organizational Transformation: Lead major finance systems, reporting, automation, and process improvement initiatives. Champion modernization of the finance function through technology, data, and scalable business processes that support future growth.

· Compliance & Governance: Maintain strong accounting policies, internal controls, compliance processes, and audit readiness while supporting increasingly sophisticated operational and financial requirements.

· CPA designation preferred; equivalent experience will be considered.
· 8–10+ years of progressive accounting and finance experience, including leadership responsibility.
· Strong Controller-level technical accounting capabilities combined with strategic business acumen.
· Construction, contracting, field service, or other project-based industry experience strongly preferred.

· Experience operating within a multi-entity or operationally complex environment.

· Strong leadership, communication, analytical, and problem-solving abilities.

Liteline Corporation is a privately held Canadian lighting manufacturer with more than 160 employees across multiple facilities in the Greater Toronto Area. We are adding a Director of Information Technology to our leadership team — a senior role with full ownership of the IT function and a direct hand in how this business operates and grows.

The scope is deliberately broad. Liteline is investing in artificial intelligence, automation, data infrastructure and connected business systems across the organization, and the Director of Information Technology will lead that work from the front.

This is an operating role as much as a technical one. The person in this position will work closely with leadership and with departments across the business, including Operations, Customer Service, Sales, Finance, Product Development, Manufacturing, Warehousing and Distribution.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise AI Strategy & Transformation
jobs.description:
Job Purpose

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Director, Enterprise AI Strategy & Transformation leads the development and execution of the organization’s enterprise AI strategy and transformation agenda to drive measurable business value, productivity, operational efficiency, innovation, and informed decision-making. The role serves as the organization’s AI subject matter expert and enterprise coordinating point, providing strategic guidance on AI opportunities, investments, governance, risk, technology, adoption, and value realization.

The Director partners with business and functional leaders to identify, prioritize, and implement AI and intelligent automation opportunities aligned with organizational objectives and financial goals. The role initially focuses on leveraging AI to enhance financial and operational performance, including forecasting, reporting, analysis, productivity, workflow efficiency, cost management, and decision-making, with successful capabilities and practices progressively expanded across other functions. The Director oversees the enterprise AI portfolio and lifecycle from opportunity assessment and business case development through solution selection, implementation, adoption, benefits realization, ongoing monitoring, and retirement.

Key Duties And Responsibilities

AI Strategy, Portfolio & Value Management

Develop and maintain the enterprise AI strategy, operating model, portfolio, and roadmap aligned with corporate objectives and financial goals.
Identify, evaluate, and prioritize AI opportunities based on strategic alignment, business value, cost, complexity, data readiness, risk, and organizational readiness.
Develop business cases, investment recommendations, and implementation roadmaps, including build, buy, configure, or partner options.
Establish performance measures, baseline metrics, and value-realization frameworks to track AI adoption, ROI, productivity, cost savings, revenue impact, and other business outcomes.
Provide executive leadership with visibility into AI investments, performance, realized benefits, opportunities, and risks.

AI Solution Development & Implementation

Lead the evaluation, design, development, and deployment of AI solutions across enterprise productivity, function-specific applications, intelligent automation, advanced AI, and emerging agentic capabilities.
Partner with business units and end users to identify opportunities, develop practical AI-enabled solutions, and improve processes and ways of working.
Oversee AI pilots, proofs of concept, and enterprise implementations through the full lifecycle—from opportunity identification and feasibility through deployment, adoption, benefits realization, monitoring, and retirement.
Coordinate with Cybersecurity, Human Resources and other stakeholders to ensure solutions are appropriately designed, implemented, adopted, and measured.
Assess solution performance and recommend whether initiatives should be scaled, enhanced, consolidated, paused, or retired based on business value, adoption, cost, and risk.

AI Governance, Risk & Responsible Adoption

Establish and maintain enterprise AI governance frameworks, policies, standards, controls, and risk-based processes to support responsible AI adoption.
Ensure AI initiatives are appropriately assessed for cybersecurity, privacy, data, intellectual property, legal, ethical, third-party, model, and business continuity risks.
Maintain an enterprise inventory of approved AI technologies, platforms, models, agents, and material use cases, with appropriate review, approval, testing, human oversight, monitoring, and escalation requirements.
Ensure data quality, classification, access, security, information governance, and regulatory requirements are addressed before AI solutions are deployed.
Monitor the evolving AI landscape, regulatory expectations, and associated risks, and update governance practices as required.

Enterprise AI Adoption & Change Management

Lead enterprise AI literacy, adoption, and change-management initiatives across executives, leaders, employees, technical teams, and advanced AI users.
Develop and deliver role- and function-specific training, guidance, and resources to promote effective and responsible use of AI.
Serve as the enterprise resource for AI strategy, best practices, use-case guidance, and adoption support.
Measure AI utilization, adoption, training effectiveness, employee feedback, and business outcomes to continuously improve AI enablement.
Coordinate internal subject matter experts, technology teams, business stakeholders, and external partners to support successful AI adoption

Vendor, Technology & Partner Management

Evaluate AI technologies, vendors, consultants, platforms, and implementation partners against business requirements, value, security, architecture, scalability, risk, and total cost of ownership.
Manage AI technology and vendor relationships to ensure service quality, effective implementation, and value realization.
Maintain oversight of the enterprise AI technology portfolio to identify duplicate capabilities, unnecessary licensing, overlapping solutions, and opportunities for consolidation.
Monitor emerging AI technologies—including generative AI, large language models, predictive AI, intelligent automation, computer vision, and agentic AI—and assess their practical business applicability and potential value.

Qualifications, Skills, And Educational Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred.
Minimum seven (7) years of progressive experience in AI, data analytics, digital transformation, automation, technology, or related fields, including significant experience leading enterprise AI or generative AI adoption.
Proven experience leading complex, enterprise-wide AI or business transformation initiatives from strategy and business case development through implementation, adoption, scaling, and measurable value realization.
Strong business and financial acumen, including experience with budgeting, forecasting, reporting, business case development, technology investment evaluation, performance measurement, and ROI.
Strong knowledge of AI technologies, including generative AI, machine learning, predictive analytics, intelligent automation, large language models, AI agents, and emerging AI capabilities, with an understanding of data, cybersecurity, privacy, and AI governance.
Strong strategic thinking, analytical, communication, stakeholder management, project management, and change management skills, with the ability to translate complex technology into practical business solutions and influence cross-functional decisions.
Strong technical and business judgment to evaluate AI solutions, vendors, risks, data and technology dependencies, and investment decisions. Professional certifications in AI, analytics, project management, responsible AI, or AI governance are considered an asset.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORKING CONDITIONS

Standard office setting - hybrid arrangement (4 days in-office)
Fast paced office environment
Travel expectations between facilities in Mississauga and North York

 The Enterprise Chief Controls Office (ECCO) is a centralized first line of defense group (1LOD) with the goal of embedding a culture of risk ownership and operational excellence by elevating the control environment and driving consistency and quality of risk practices to minimize loss and regulatory sanction, drive cost efficiencies, and accelerate execution to enable growth. The Operational Resilience and Business Continuity Management (BCM) team provide leadership in designing and implementing strategic vision, long-term operational model, roadmap and program governance across our platforms in the 1LOD. Working in partnership with platform and business unit Operational Resilience, BCM and Incident Management teams, this central team drives an enterprise-wide strategy to strengthen first line capabilities by driving consistent risk and control practices, embedding resilience into the way we lead, operate and respond to disruption while enabling critical business outcomes. The team is integral in evolving the operating model, governance, and relationship to other resilience risk areas, serving as a single first-line voice to unify, standardize and elevate Resilience capabilities in alignment with ECCO's mandate to embed risk ownership and operational excellence across the organization

jobs.title: Director of Data
jobs.description:
**Purpose in Every Position**


Pebl puts a world of talent at your fingertips. With our AI\-powered Global Work Platform, companies can hire, pay, and manage employees in 185\+ countries—removing risk, red tape, and guesswork from global growth. Backed by more than a decade of compliance leadership and local expertise, Pebl helps businesses move fast, stay compliant, and scale with confidence. With Pebl, companies everywhere can hire great talent anywhere.

**Where Your Work Moves the Needle.**


At Pebl, every team member drives our success. Joining us means more than filling a role—you’re accountable for results and impact. Our values guide how we operate, execute, and collaborate across borders. By putting them into action, you’ll help us scale faster, compete harder, and lead the future of global work.

**What Makes You a Great Fit**


We are seeking a highly technical, deeply analytical, and aggressively innovative Director of Data to lead our data strategy, infrastructure, and AI integration. You will not just be managing a team; you will be the chief storyteller for our data and the evangelist for our "AI Everywhere" initiative.


Based out of our Palo Alto office, you will sit at the intersection of R\&D and our core business functions—specifically Marketing, Sales, Operations, Finance, and Legal—ensuring that Pebl’s vast repository of global employment and compliance data is secure, accessible, and actionable.

***In\-office collaboration is required at our Toronto office Monday through Wednesday.***

**How You'll Make An Impact:**

**1\. Architect the Future (Technical \& Hands\-On Data Engineering)**

* Own the vision and execution of Pebl’s modern data infrastructure.
* Serve as the ultimate technical authority on data engineering, ensuring highly scalable, performant, and reliable data pipelines.
* Champion strict data security, privacy, and governance protocols to protect our global payroll, HR, and compliance data.

**2\. Drive Actionable Business Insights (Analytical Powerhouse)**

* Transform complex datasets into clear, actionable strategies across all departments.
* Partner with Marketing and Sales to optimize our growth funnel, CAC, and conversion rates.
* Collaborate with Operations, Finance, and Legal to improve billing accuracy, payroll speed, and compliance tracking.

**3\. Champion "AI Everywhere" (AI Native Operations)**

* Lead the charge to make Pebl a truly AI\-native company.
* Bring AI capabilities to our R\&D offerings, such as enhancing our compliance assistant, Alfie.
* Engage directly with Marketing, Sales, Operations, Finance, and Legal to embed AI into their daily workflows, driving massive internal efficiency.

**4\. Bridge the Gap (Communication \& Storytelling)**

* Act as the ultimate translator between deep technical R\&D work and overarching business objectives.
* Master the art of data storytelling to present complex insights to the executive team and the board in a compelling way.

**5\. Build and Foster the Team (Leadership)**

* **Lead the Charge:** Be a hands\-on, execution\-oriented leader who ensures delivery of strong business results.
* **Be the NBA Coach:** Recruit top\-tier talent and assemble a high\-performing team of data engineers, analysts, and AI specialists.
* **Be the Gardener:** Foster a culture of continuous learning and psychological safety to cultivate a data\-driven mindset across the entire company.

**Let's Connect If You Have:**

* **Extensive Technical Background:** 15\+ years of experience in data engineering, data science, or analytics, with at least 5 years in a senior leadership role.
* **Modern Stack Mastery:** Deep, hands\-on expertise orchestrating our specific modern data infrastructure stack: **Snowflake, Fivetran, Atlan, Looker, and Monte Carlo**.
* **AI/ML Track Record:** Proven experience deploying LLMs, machine learning models, and AI tools for both production products and internal operational workflows.
* **Cross\-Functional Business Acumen:** Demonstrated ability to collaborate with Marketing, Sales, Operations, Finance, and Legal to tie data initiatives directly to top\-line growth and bottom\-line efficiency.
* **Exceptional Communication:** A track record of weaving data into compelling business narratives for non\-technical stakeholders.
* **Work Style:** Ability to work from our Palo Alto office Monday through Wednesday to collaborate directly with the executive and R\&D teams.

**Our Commitment to You**


At Pebl, we’re committed to supporting our team with comprehensive rewards and benefits designed to meet diverse needs across roles and locations. Our core offerings include:

* **Flexible Time Off** – Take the time you need to recharge.
* **Parental Leave** – Support for growing families.
* **Health and Dental Insurance** – Where applicable, to cover you and your loved ones.
* **Retirement Savings \+ Employee Incentive Plan** – Plan for the future while sharing our success.


Please visit our career page for more information.

**Pebl is an Equal Opportunity Employer.**


We power global teams and believe diverse perspectives drive innovation and impact. Employment decisions at Pebl are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law. We’re committed to fostering an inclusive culture where every teammate can thrive and do the best work of their career—anywhere in the world.

Organization: Securian Canada

Position Title: Head of Total Rewards & Talent Intelligence

Reports to: Chief Human Experience Officer

Location: Toronto (hybrid)

THE COMPANY

Securian Canada is a technology-enabled insurance organization with more than 70 years of experience serving Canadians through financial institutions, associations, affinity organizations, and other strategic distribution partners. As an independent subsidiary of Securian Financial Group, the company combines deep local market expertise with the resources and scale of a leading North American insurance organization. Focused on helping Canadians build greater financial security, Securian Canada offers a range of life, creditor, and specialty insurance solutions designed to meet evolving consumer needs. The organization has established a strong reputation for customer-focused innovation, leveraging technology, data, and digital capabilities to enhance both product offerings and client experiences.

In recent years, Securian Canada has experienced significant growth and transformation through strategic investments, business expansion, and acquisition activity, further strengthening its market position. Despite its increased scale and sophistication, the organization continues to foster a culture characterized by agility, collaboration, inclusion, and an entrepreneurial approach to innovation and continuous improvement.

THE ROLE

Reporting to the Chief Human Experience Officer, the Head of Total Rewards & Talent Intelligence is a critical leadership role responsible for shaping and executing a holistic total rewards and talent analytics strategy.

This role integrates deep functional leadership in compensation and rewards with the forward-looking use of data and insights to inform talent and business decisions. The mandate spans strategy, design, governance, and execution, while serving as a trusted advisor to senior leadership and the Board on compensation matters.
The Head of Total Rewards & Talent Intelligence leads a team and plays a central role in ensuring that reward strategies, talent insights, and workforce decisions are scalable, financially sustainable, and aligned with business priorities.

This is a build-and-shape role, requiring a leader who can operate both strategically and hands-on, establishing frameworks, elevating capabilities, and delivering impact to the business in a high-growth environment.

Total Rewards Strategy & Design

Lead the design and evolution of an integrated total rewards strategy aligned with business objectives, culture, and growth ambitions

Evaluate market competitiveness and effectiveness of programs, recommending adjustments as needed

Executive Compensation & Governance

Prepare materials and provide insights for Board and Committee reporting, including compensation analysis and recommendations
Ensure strong governance, internal controls, and compliance with applicable standards

People Analytics & Workforce Insights

Develop insights related to workforce trends, capability gaps, performance, engagement, and retention
Translate data into clear, actionable recommendations for senior leadership
Advance the use of systems, analytics, and dashboards across the organization

Enterprise Partnership & Advisory

Partner across HR and the business to align rewards, talent priorities, and enterprise goals

M&A and Strategic Initiatives

Lead Total Rewards and People Analytics support for M&A due diligence and post acquisition integration
Provide guidance on compensation harmonization, workforce alignment, and organizational implications
Support broader strategic initiatives, including growth, restructuring, and expansion efforts

Operational Excellence & Risk Management

Ensure accuracy and integrity of critical processes including compensation cycles and executive reporting
Drive operational efficiency, process improvement, and automation based on modern AI tools
Identify and mitigate financial, compliance, and operational risks

Team Leadership

Lead and develop a small, high-impact team across Total Rewards and People Analytics
Build a strong consultative capability within the team
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement

CANDIDATE PROFILE

Experience & Expertise

Deep expertise in total rewards, including compensation design and executive compensation
Experience in growth-oriented, evolving, or transformation environments
Strong capability in data and talent analytics
Exposure to M&A, integration, or large-scale organizational change initiatives
Experience preparing materials and insights for senior executives and Boards

Enterprise mindset with the ability to align people strategies with business priorities
Credible advisor to senior leaders, with strong influencing skills
Ability to balance strategy and execution in a resource-conscious environment
Proven experience building and leading high-performing teams

Personal Characteristics

Collaborative, relationship-oriented, and effective across diverse stakeholder groups

jobs.title: Associate Director of Finance
jobs.description:
This is an exciting opportunity to shape the future of one of McMaster's most dynamic and entrepreneurial portfolios. As the Associate Director, Finance, Ancillary Operations
, you will provide strategic financial leadership across five diverse and revenue-generating businesses, including Housing & Conference Services, Hospitality Services, The Campus Store, Media Production Services, and Parking Services
, overseeing a portfolio of approximately $112 million in annual operations
. In this newly created role, you will play a pivotal part in designing and leading a shared-services finance model, driving operational excellence, strengthening financial sustainability, and influencing key business decisions that enhance the experience of students, employees, and campus visitors. Working closely with senior leaders across the University, you will have a unique opportunity to build something new, modernize financial practices, and help position McMaster's ancillary enterprises for long-term success and growth.

Job Description

Job Summary:

The Associate Director, Finance – Ancillary Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for the full range of financial activities across the Ancillary Operations portfolio, including Housing and Conference Services Hospitality Services, Campus Store, Parking Services, Media Production Services, and other assigned operations. The role is accountable for integrating financial planning and analysis, accounting and financial operations, financial reporting, controls, revenue and pricing analysis, and business performance management to support the financial sustainability and effective operation of the portfolio.

The Associate Director provides strategic financial advice to support business planning, investment, resource allocation, revenue generation, pricing, and operational decision-making. The role provides oversight of portfolio financial activities and establishes effective financial management practices, controls, and evaluate and improve processes across diverse operations.

Through a functional reporting relationship to the Controller, the Associate Director ensures Ancillary Operations financial activities are aligned with institutional accounting requirements, financial policies, controls, systems, and reporting standards, while representing the financial and business requirements of Ancillary Operations within the broader University finance function.

Accountabilities:

1. Financial & Business Leadership

Provide financial leadership across the Ancillary Operations portfolio, integrating financial priorities and activities across diverse revenue-generating operations.
Lead the development and execution of annual budgets, forecasts, multi-year financial plans, and longer-term financial strategies aligned with portfolio and institutional objectives.
Serve as the senior financial advisor to the Executive Director and Ancillary leadership team on financial sustainability, resource allocation, investment, and financial performance.
Establish financial priorities and plans for the portfolio and provide direction on how financial objectives and targets will be achieved.

2. Financial Planning, Revenue & Business Performance

Provide leadership and financial advice related to revenue generation, revenue diversification, pricing strategies, capital and deferred maintenance planning and strategies, cost-recovery models, margins, and financial sustainability.
Partner with business leaders to evaluate and shape new services, business opportunities, service delivery models, building and space refresh planning, and revenue-generating initiatives.
Establish approaches for assessing profitability, margins, return on investment, break-even points, and other measures of financial and business performance.
Monitor market, demand, volume, revenue, cost, and other business drivers and assess their implications for portfolio financial performance in collaboration with campus business partners.
Identify significant financial risks and opportunities and lead the development of strategies to improve business and financial outcomes.

3. Accounting, Financial Operations & Reporting

Provide oversight of accounting, financial reporting, and transactional financial activities across Ancillary Operations, ensuring accurate, timely, efficient, and appropriately controlled financial operations.
Ensure appropriate oversight of revenue and expenditure transactions, accounts receivable and payable activities, internal and external billings, reconciliations, journal entries, and other portfolio financial processes.
Ensure appropriate accounting treatment, internal controls, documentation, approvals, reconciliations, and financial controls are consistently applied across operations.
Oversee portfolio financial reporting, including financial results, forecasts, variance analysis, revenue, expenses, margins, and other key financial measures.
Establish clear roles, responsibilities, service expectations, internal controls and processes for financial activities undertaken within Ancillary Operations.
Resolve complex accounting and financial management issues in collaboration with the Controller and other areas of central Finance.
Lead opportunities to standardize, streamline, and automate financial processes while maintaining appropriate financial controls and service levels.
Lead and manage all internal and external financial audit processes; including the year-end process in collaboration with central Finance.

4. Financial Governance, Controls & Stewardship

Establish and maintain effective financial management practices, processes, and controls across the Ancillary Operations portfolio.
Ensure portfolio financial activities comply with University policies, accounting requirements, financial controls, and applicable regulatory requirements.
Interpret institutional financial requirements and determine appropriate approaches for implementation across the portfolio.
Assess the effectiveness of portfolio financial controls and lead corrective action in response to identified risks, deficiencies, or compliance issues.
Support internal and external audit activities and ensure appropriate resolution of findings related to portfolio financial operations.
Promote and advance financial accountability, stewardship, and consistent application of financial practices across Ancillary Operations.
Recommend improvements to financial policies, practices, and controls based on changing business requirements and identified risks.

5. Partnership & Institutional Alignment

Serve as the primary financial partner to the Executive Director, Ancillary Operations and provide financial leadership to the broader Ancillary leadership team.
Translate complex financial, operational, and business information into clear insights and recommendations for senior decision-makers.
Present financial performance, forecasts, business cases, risks, opportunities, and recommendations to senior leadership and other decision-making forums.
Build effective relationships with the Controller, central Finance functions to ensure alignment between portfolio and institutional financial requirements.
Represent Ancillary Operations in institutional financial planning, budgeting, reporting, accounting, and financial process discussions.
Ensure portfolio financial plans, accounting practices, reporting, systems, and controls align with institutional frameworks and standards.
Contribute to University-wide financial initiatives and provide input into institutional practices and processes based on the needs and complexity of revenue-generating operations.

6. People Leadership

Lead, develop, and provide direction to financial professionals supporting the Ancillary Services portfolio.
Establish annual objectives, priorities, accountabilities, and performance expectations aligned with portfolio and institutional financial objectives.
Delegate operational financial activities appropriately to enable effective oversight of the broader finance function and focus on portfolio-level priorities and longer-term planning.
Coach and develop financial staff and provide guidance on complex financial, accounting, analytical, and business issues.
Ensure appropriate quality assurance and review of financial planning, analysis, reporting, accounting, and transactional activities.
Build financial management capability and strengthen financial literacy and accountability across Ancillary Services.
Foster a culture of collaboration, continuous improvement, service excellence, sound financial stewardship, and accountability.

jobs.title: Director, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A)
jobs.description:
With millions of diners, 70,000+ restaurant partners and 25+ years of experience, OpenTable, part of Booking Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: BKNG), is an industry leader with a passion for helping restaurants thrive. Our world-class technology empowers restaurants to focus on what matters most – their team, their guests, and their bottom line – while enabling diners to discover and book the perfect restaurant for every occasion.

Every employee at OpenTable has a tangible impact on what we do and how we do it. You’ll also be part of a global team and its portfolio of metasearch brands. Hospitality is all about taking care of others, and it defines our culture.

About The Job

OpenTable is seeking a strategic and operationally-minded Director of FP&A to lead financial planning, forecasting, and analysis for our core operational investments. Located in our Toronto office, this role will have primary ownership over the company’s Operating Expenses (OpEx), Capital Expenditures (CapEx), and Commissions modeling and structures. Reporting to the VP, FP&A, you will act as a key business partner to departmental heads, ensuring disciplined resource allocation, optimization of capital investments, and the implementation of commission plans that align with corporate growth objectives. This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Responsibilities

OpEx Management & Forecasting: Lead the annual budgeting and monthly forecasting processes for global operating expenses. Partner with department heads ( tech, sales, marketing, G&A) to track spend, analyze variances, and identify cost-efficiency opportunities.
CapEx Planning & Governance: Oversee the evaluation, tracking, and prioritization of capital expenditures. Develop robust ROI models for major technology, infrastructure, and facilities investments to guide executive decision-making.
Commissions Oversight: Own the financial oversight of the commission program. Partner with Sales Operations to ensure commission plans are accurate and effective.
Business Partnership: Serve as a trusted financial advisor to operational leadership, translating complex financial data into actionable insights that drive strategic initiatives.
Management Reporting: Deliver clear monthly and quarterly financial review packages focusing on spend efficiency, capital deployment, and incentive plan effectiveness for senior leadership.
Process & Systems Improvement: Continuously scale and automate FP&A processes, particularly around expense tracking and commission calculations, to support organizational growth.

Qualifications

Experience: 7–10 years of progressive experience in corporate finance, FP&A, or strategic finance, with a strong emphasis on expense management, capital budgeting, and sales compensation finance.
Leadership: Demonstrated experience managing professional finance team members and leading cross-functional projects.
Analytical Skills: Advanced financial modeling skills (Excel/Google Sheets) and experience handling large datasets. Proficiency with financial planning tools, ERP software, and commission management platforms (e.g., CaptivateIQ).
Communication: Strong ability to influence and build partnerships with non-finance executives by presenting financial concepts clearly and concisely.
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related quantitative field.

Benefits and Perks

Work from (almost) anywhere for up to 20 days per year
Focus on mental health and well-being:
Company-paid therapy sessions through SpringHealth
Company-paid subscription to Headspace
Annual company-wide week off a year - the whole team fully recharges (and returns without a pile-up of work!)

Paid parental leave
Generous paid vacation + time off for your birthday
Paid volunteer time
Focus on your career growth:
Development Dollars
Leadership development
Access to thousands of on-demand e-learnings

Travel Discounts
Employee Resource Groups
20 days of paid time off
Private health and dental insurance
Life and Disability insurance

The best connections happen face-to-face, whether you’re sitting down to dinner or having coffee with a coworker. That’s why OpenTable has adopted a hybrid workplace model. This role aligns with that approach, with an expectation of coming into the office two days a week—giving employees the best of both worlds: in-person collaboration and flexibility.

We offer a competitive base salary and benefits including: health benefits; flexible spending account; retirement benefits; life insurance; paid time off (including PTO, paid sick leave, medical leave, bereavement leave, floating holidays and paid holidays); and parental leave benefits. jobs.description:
Who We Are

For more than 130 years, The Salvation Army has served people in need in communities across Canada and Bermuda. Building on our roots as a world-wide Christian church, each year we help more than 2 million people, providing necessities such as food, clothing and shelter. In addition, we support people experiencing unemployment, addiction and family challenges. We continually adapt and innovate to meet emerging needs and live out our mission, vision and values of hope, service, dignity and stewardship. As a faith- and values-based organization, we hire and serve people of all backgrounds and walks of life - there is a place for everyone to belong here.

Mission Statement

The Salvation Army exists to share the love of Jesus Christ, meet human needs and be a transforming influence in the communities of our world.

Job Description

Position Summary

The Director of Finance manages one of the regional financial accounting and advisory services groups of The Salvation Army for Canada and Bermuda and has responsibility for relationship management and for providing financial and strategic advice to the various mission partner leadership teams within the related region. The Director of Finance conducts financial reviews as required, monitors overall financial health for various operating units in Canada and Bermuda and through a collaborative approach with the appropriate divisional or territorial leadership teams, develops action plans to address concerns when needed. The Director of Finance recommends and administers policies and procedures pertaining to such matters and is responsible for ensuring the integrity of the accounting records in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles.

Key Accountabilities

Lead the delivery of financial accounting and advisory services across multiple operating entities, ensuring sound financial management, compliance, and alignment with organizational objectives.
Develop, implement, and maintain accounting policies, procedures, financial controls, and chart of accounts standards to support accuracy, consistency, and regulatory compliance.
Monitor and assess the financial health, performance, and long-term sustainability of operating units, identifying risks and recommending corrective actions to strengthen financial outcomes.
Conduct financial reviews, analyze key performance indicators, and collaborate with leadership to develop and implement action plans that address financial and operational concerns.
Partner with mission leaders and stakeholders to provide strategic financial advice, interpret policies, and support informed decision-making on operational and organizational priorities.
Lead the budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning processes, including annual operating and capital budgets, long-term forecasts, variance analysis, and performance monitoring.
Oversee financial reporting, account reconciliations, and month-end and year-end processes to ensure the accuracy, completeness, and integrity of financial information.
Manage internal and external audit activities, regulatory filings, charitable and tax returns, and financial statement preparation to meet all compliance and reporting requirements.
Support cash flow management, capital projects, government funding initiatives, and stakeholder reporting by providing financial analysis, forecasts, budgets, and funding-related guidance.
Supervise, mentor, and develop finance staff while fostering strong stakeholder relationships, building financial management capacity, and promoting continuous improvement across finance operations.

Education And Experience Qualifications

Completion of an undergraduate degree in Accounting or a related discipline.
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation required.
Five to seven (5-7) years of progressive accounting, finance, or business management experience, including leadership responsibility for budgeting, financial management, and operational oversight.
Demonstrated supervisory and leadership experience, with the ability to coach, mentor, and develop high-performing teams.
Extensive knowledge of accounting principles, financial management practices, and financial reporting requirements, including regulatory compliance and audit processes.
Experience developing solutions to complex business and financial challenges, managing large-scale initiatives, and exercising sound judgment with a high degree of independence.
Strong understanding of integrated business systems, automated workflows, and accounting technologies, including cloud-based and web-enabled applications.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and financial analysis tools, with the ability to interpret, analyze, and present complex financial information.
Excellent written and verbal communication, stakeholder engagement, and customer service skills, with the ability to convey complex information clearly and effectively.
Non-profit sector experience, including reporting to government agencies and external funders, is considered an asset.

Compensation

The target hiring range for this position is $105,518.40 to $131,913.60 with a maximum of $158,288.00.

Placement in the salary range will be based on factors such as market conditions, internal equity, and candidate experience, skills, and qualifications relevant to the role.

if you have a need for any accommodation and we will be pleased to discuss this with you.

jobs.description:
The Opportunity

The Pharmacy Examining Board of Canada (PEBC), a national not-for-profit certification and assessment body for the pharmacy profession, is seeking an Interim Vice-President, Psychometrics and Data Analytics.

This is a highly strategic executive mandate. PEBC is looking for a strong, proven leader who can redefine its psychometric and data strategies and provide senior leadership across psychometrics, enterprise data strategy, analytics, governance and business intelligence.

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer and serving on the Senior Management Team, the Interim Vice-President holds overall accountability for psychometrics and related data analysis, and leads PEBC’s enterprise data strategy, data analytics and business intelligence, data governance, and reporting. The role ensures the validity, reliability, fairness and defensibility of high-stakes national certification examinations, and positions data as a strategic asset informing decision-making across the organization.

Combining strategic leadership with deep technical authority, the Interim Vice-President advances psychometric and analytic practice through established and emerging methodologies, research and evidence-informed decision-making.

Key Responsibilities

Oversee the psychometric quality of all assessments, validity, reliability, fairness and defensibility, through test design and administration support, standard setting, equating, scaling, scoring and results reporting.
Ensure consistent application of psychometric methodologies across assessments, in line with professional standards and best practices.
Direct statistical and forensic analyses of examination outcomes, candidate performance and testing incidents (including remote proctoring) to support fair, evidence-based decisions.
Lead the initial development and implementation of an enterprise data governance framework, data quality, integrity, security, privacy, retention, definitions and stewardship, alongside metadata management, a data catalogue, and master and reference data management.
Govern analytical and AI/machine-learning models used in or affecting assessments, including model validation, bias and fairness testing, performance monitoring, drift detection and documentation.
Own the reporting, dashboard and data-visualization environment, including self-serve business intelligence for senior leadership, the Board and stakeholders, underpinned by a governed single source of truth and semantic layer.
Champion a data strategy that treats assessment and operational data as a strategic asset, and advance analytics from descriptive and diagnostic reporting toward predictive and prescriptive capability.
Steward the multi-year data strategy and analytics roadmap aligned to the strategic plan, in collaboration with technology leadership, which owns the underlying data platform and engineering.
Chair the data governance operating model, with named data owners and stewards in each function, reporting through the Senior Management Team to the CEO.
Advise on psychometric and standard-setting decisions with high-stakes or policy-level impact, and on statistical and forensic findings related to testing irregularities.
Partner closely with executive peers in Assessments, Technology and Operations, and present psychometric results, validity evidence and recommendations to the Board's examinations committee.
Lead all HR matters for the Psychometrics and Data Analytics department, including recruitment, training, retention and performance management, along with annual business priorities, projects and budget.

Qualifications

PhD required, ideally in psychometrics or educational measurement, or in a closely related quantitative discipline such as statistics.
Significant progressive senior leadership and management experience, including leading technical teams or functions.
Substantial experience as a psychometrician in educational or psychological testing (typically eight or more years), including high-stakes assessment.
Strong expertise in psychometric methodologies, including standard setting, equating and scaling.
Experience leading or overseeing enterprise data strategy, data governance, data analytics and business intelligence/reporting.
Proven ability to design, conduct, interpret and present psychometric analyses and studies in high-stakes assessment contexts.
Strong data analysis and scientific-computing skills, and familiarity with business-intelligence and data-visualization tools.
Experience leveraging data science, machine learning or emerging AI tools to support measurement and analytics.
Assets: exposure to predictive/prescriptive analytics and AI/ML model governance; professional certification and licensure experience; proficiency in French.

The Ideal Candidate

You are a strong, seasoned leader with a track record of setting direction, someone who has redefined strategy for a technical function, not just managed one. You bring high professional standards and a strong commitment to assessment quality, fairness and defensibility, with sound analytical judgment on complex, high-impact psychometric and data issues. You balance strategic leadership with technical rigour, hands-on where needed and treat data integrity, security and privacy as paramount. You are a credible, confident and collaborative communicator, able to translate complex psychometric and data concepts for non-technical audiences, inspire and develop a technical team, and operate independently in a high-stakes assessment environment.

Working Conditions

This is a fully remote position open to candidates located in Canada or the United States. Occasional travel may be required.

How to Apply

This is an interim executive engagement; the anticipated term will be confirmed with shortlisted candidates.

To express interest, please submit a cover letter and résumé to Vanessa at Peak Performance HR at vanessa@peakperformancehr.com. Please reference “Interim VP, Psychometrics and Data Analytics” in the subject line.

All inquiries and applications will be treated in confidence.

PEBC is an equal opportunity employer committed to an inclusive, barrier-free recruitment process. Accommodations are available on request at all stages of the selection process.

This role is a replacement, and AI will not be used during the recruitment process.

jobs.description:
Position Overview

Genome Atlantic
brings businesses, governments, and researchers together to focus expertise and investment on Atlantic Canada’s priorities. We help partners turn insights from DNA into practical solutions that improve health, increase productivity, and drive business growth and job creation. The team at Genome Atlantic is connected by a collaborative way of working and a shared commitment to making an impact across Atlantic Canada. 

We are looking for an experienced finance leader who, working as part of a skilled team, appreciates seeing the impact of what they do.

As our Director, Finance & Administration
, you will be the senior financial leader in the organization and a trusted partner to our President & CEO. This is both a leadership role and a hands-on one. You will provide financial insight and advice, while also being directly involved in the accounting, reporting, budgeting, audit, funding and administrative work that keeps the organization aligned with its commitments and vision.

One day you may be preparing financial information for the Board or advising the CEO on an important decision. The next, you may be collaborating on a project with other Genome Center Finance leads , reconciling financial information, working through a funding claim, coordinating an audit requirement, reviewing a contract or solving an operational issue.

For the right person, that combination of collaborative leadership, variety and hands-on involvement is part of what makes the opportunity interesting.

If you are a CPA who enjoys meaningful work, fostering strong relationships and being part of an experienced team where people know and support one another, we would love to hear from you!

The Opportunity

Reporting to the President & CEO, the Director, Finance & Administration
is responsible for the financial stewardship of Genome Atlantic and the effective administration of across important internal business functions, including:

• accounting, financial management and reporting
• budgeting, forecasting and financial analysis
• funder and project financial management
• external audit and financial controls
• Board and Finance & Audit Committee reporting
• contracts and agreements
• payroll and benefits administration
• selected HR and policy administration
• technology and vendor coordination
• organizational systems and administration

This position has one direct report, the Senior Coordinator, Projects and Finance, and is responsible for providing direction, support and appropriate oversight. The role also works closely with the President & CEO, colleagues, Board members, funders, auditors, project partners and external advisors and contractors.

This role combines strategic financial leadership with hands-on involvement in the day-to-day work. You will contribute directly to Genome Atlantic’s financial and administrative operations, provide trusted advice to the CEO and Board, and help ensure the systems and processes that support the organization are reliable, well managed and effective.

Areas of Responsibility

Financial Leadership & Stewardship

Oversee and work directly within Genome Atlantic’s financial management systems, accounting records, controls and policies; lead budgeting; monitor financial performance; prepare quarterly and annual financial reporting; coordinate the annual audit; and provide financial analysis and advice to support decision-making.

Funding & Project Financial Management

Prepare and oversee financial claims and reporting for funding partners, support project budgeting and financial administration, monitor project financial performance and maintain strong relationships with funders, institutional partners and other Genome Centres.

Board & Governance Support

Prepare and present financial information to the Finance & Audit Committee and Board of Directors and support the President & CEO with the financial and administrative aspects of governance.

Contracts, People & Administration

Work directly with contracts, agreements, payroll and benefits administration, employee documentation, policies, technology and other organizational processes, while coordinating with external professional partners as needed.

Team & Organizational Support

Work collaboratively with an experienced team, share knowledge, strengthen processes and contribute beyond a narrow functional boundary when needed. You will provide direction and support while also valuing the expertise and organizational knowledge of the people around you.

Experience and Qualifications

We are looking for someone who combines strong technical finance expertise with practical business judgement and an approachable, collaborative working style. This includes:

A CPA designation in good standing
A minimum of five years of progressively responsible accounting and financial management experience, including senior-level responsibility for a finance function.
Broad experience across the full financial cycle, including accounting operations, budgeting and forecasting, financial reporting, cash management, financial controls, year-end activities and external audit.
Experience preparing and presenting financial information to senior leaders, Boards and/or Finance and Audit Committees, with the ability to translate financial information into clear, practical advice that supports good decisions.
Experience managing externally funded programs, projects or contribution agreements, including budgets, financial claims, reporting and reconciliation.
Experience building effective relationships with funders, government agencies, institutional partners, auditors and other professional advisors.
Experience supporting, supervising or developing others, with a collaborative approach that respects the knowledge and expertise colleagues bring.
A high level of attention to detail and accuracy, with the discipline to ensure financial information, reporting, records and follow-through are complete, reliable and well managed, while still keeping sight of the bigger picture. 
Experience working effectively with external service providers and professional partners, including accounting and IT support.
Experience with payroll, benefits and confidential employee and compensation information.
Clear communication skills and the ability to build trusted working relationships through responsiveness, dependability and follow-through.
Comfort taking ownership, working independently and knowing when to seek input or involve others.
Comfort moving between strategic advice and hands-on execution, sometimes within the same day.
A practical mindset and an interest in strengthening systems, simplifying processes and helping the organization work effectively.
Flexibility, good humour and a willingness to contribute where needed as part of a small, collaborative team.
Experience with not-for-profit accounting and governance is not required but would be highly valued.
Experience in contract administration, policy or HR administration, research, innovation, academic, government-funded or project-based environments would be an asset.
Strong Microsoft Excel and Microsoft 365 skills are important; experience with QuickBooks would be an asset.

Work Environment

This is a full-time hybrid position based in Halifax, Nova Scotia
.

Genome Atlantic’s current hybrid model includes working in the Halifax office on Tuesday
, Wednesday
and Thursday
, with flexibility to work remotely on Monday and Friday.

Periodic travel within Atlantic Canada and elsewhere in Canada may be required. The role also includes predictable periods of increased activity associated with quarter-end and year-end reporting, audits, funding requirements, Board meetings and project milestones.

Physical Requirements

Ability to sit at a desk or workstation for extended periods of time while performing computer-based work.
Ability to communicate effectively in English with team members, stakeholders, and clients through verbal and written communication.
Ability to travel to other Genome Canada/Genome Centre offices, partner sites, and out-of-province conferences as needed.

How To Apply 

If this role speaks to you, we’d love to hear from you! 

Please share your cover letter and resume as a single PDF (with your full name in the file name) to recruitment@genomeatlantic.ca
with the subject line: Director, Finance and Accounting
.

The application deadline is Monday, October 19th, 2026. 

Individual accommodations due to a disability are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, religion, ethnicity, gender, disability, citizenship status, marital status, or actual or perceived sexual orientation. 

Genome Atlantic is committed to creating an inclusive environment and building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We value diversity and recognize that experience comes in many forms and skills are transferable. If you feel enthusiastic about our efforts and believe you have the skills to contribute and excel in this role, apply! 

We thank all interested parties; however, only those applicants under consideration will be contacted. 

About Genome Atlantic 

Genome Atlantic connects ideas and people across public and private sectors to fuel innovation and translate discoveries into solutions across key sectors including energy; mining; aquaculture; agriculture and agri-food; forestry; health; and the environment. Together with our many partners, we have enabled over $170 million in strategic R&D since our inception in 2000, driving sustainable economic development in Atlantic Canada’s natural resources, improving health outcomes, enhancing environmental stewardship, and helping our regional industries adapt to climate change. genomeatlantic.ca

Eruditus and its sister company Emeritus provide Small Private Online Courses (SPOCs) to students all over the world. EMERITUS enables working professionals who cannot enroll in full-time courses to access a top-tier, affordable education that will give them the skills needed to be the business leaders of tomorrow. The Emeritus and Eruditus global team include 1,000+ employees located in the US, Dubai, Mexico, India, China, and Singapore.

Information about the Program Leader role:

Emeritus is seeking a Program Leader
for the Kellogg Executive Education Program AI-First Marketing Strategy: Executing Intelligent Systems for Growth Live Online Program .
The Program Leader is a subject matter expert that serves as the front-line academic support for learners in the course, supporting the delivery of a high-impact, 8-weeks online program. The Program Leader will be working closely with the Emeritus Academic Delivery Team. Candidates must have industry experience and demonstrated knowledge of the course subject area. They will guide learners through complex topics like AI-driven strategies, frameworks, and challenges in real-world contexts.
This is a great role for someone who wants work flexibility and the chance to diversify their resume with consultancy and teaching experience. This is an independent contractor position in a remote setting.

Responsibilities of the Program Leader role:

Facilitate weekly live sessions and moderate required discussion boards
Moderate and guide learner engagement during faculty live sessions
Support learners in synthesizing live session content delivered by the faculty
Assist with capstone assignment challenges
Grade specific assignments while aligning with the suggested rubric
Collaborate with instructional designers to improve engagement and comprehension
Monitor learner progress and provide support or escalation as needed

Qualifications for the Program Leader role:

Bachelor’s degree in marketing, business, communications or a related field plus MBA from a top university.
10+ years of progressive marketing leadership experience including ownership of brand, growth demand generation and digital strategy.
Proven experience integrating AI technologies into marketing operations, campaign execution, analytics and customer engagement.
Deep understanding of modern AI -driven marketing tools and platforms, including generative AI, predictive analytics, marketing automation, CRM systems and personalization engines.
Demonstrated ability to build and scale AI-first marketing workflows that improve efficiency, campaign performance and customer acquisition.
Proven experience leading multi-channel campaigns across paid media, content marketing, SEO, email, social media and lifecycle marketing.
Strong understanding of prompt engineering, AI assisted content generation, workflow automation, and responsible AI usage in marketing.
Proven experience managing transformation projects from initiation to closure.
Experience providing guidance and recommendations to management to ensure marketing strategy or innovation plans align with company goals.
Experience supporting executive or mid-career professionals
in continuing education is highly preferred.
Excellent communication, facilitation, and interpersonal skills with an ability to listen effectively, respond appropriately, and maintain a mutual comfort level while working with a diverse population.
Ability to translate content into actionable insights.
Empathetic and learner-centered approach.
Comfortable in an online environment, navigating LMS platforms (Canvas), Zoom, Slack, or similar environments.
Strong organizational and time-management skills to manage weekly cycles of engagement and support.

Program Description and Context:

The AI
‑ First Marketing Strategy: Executing Intelligent Systems for Growth
program from Kellogg Executive Education is an eight-week online experience that prepares leaders to navigate a pivotal shift: AI is redefining how organizations grow and compete. Many organizations continue to operate between experimentation and execution, using AI tools in isolation rather than integrating them into a connected system. As generative AI (gen AI) expands marketers’ ability to create, personalize and act at scale, participants will learn to build marketing systems that operate continuously, adapt in real time and drive measurable growth. This program will enable participants to architect this shift through the Intelligent Marketing Operating System (I-MOS) framework, developed by Professor Mohanbir Sawhney, a globally recognized authority in AI, marketing and business innovation. I-MOS defines what to do and shows how to apply AI across your marketing system. By learning to apply AI across connected workflows and align intelligence, decisioning, execution and governance, participants will build the capability to design high-performing marketing systems that continuously evolve.
Duration: 8-weeks (estimated learner commitment: 4–5 hours/week).
Structure: Blend of asynchronous Canvas activities and live Zoom sessions.

 HOOPP is seeking an accomplished institutional investment leader to help shape portfolio construction, investment strategy and risk-informed decision-making across one of Canada's leading pension funds.

 Reporting to the Vice President, Total Portfolio Risk & Analytics, this role operates at the intersection of investment strategy, portfolio construction, total fund analytics and risk insight. The successful candidate will partner closely with senior investment leaders to evaluate strategic opportunities, assess portfolio resilience and provide forward-looking insights that support decisions across public and private markets.

 As a senior leader within the Risk Division, the Senior Director will influence how investment risks and opportunities are understood at the total portfolio level. The role will help advance HOOPP's Total Portfolio Approach through innovative analytics, rigorous research, constructive challenge and strategic thought leadership.

 This is an opportunity to contribute to investment decisions spanning equities, fixed income, derivatives, real estate, infrastructure, private equity and private credit, while helping shape the continued evolution of total portfolio strategy, analytics and risk management at HOOPP.

 What you will do: 

 Strategic Portfolio Leadership
 Partner with Investment Management and the Total Portfolio Group to provide insights that support portfolio construction, strategic asset allocation and investment decision-making across HOOPP’s total fund.
 Act as a trusted advisor to senior leaders on portfolio design, investment strategy, risk-return trade-offs and portfolio resilience.
 Assess the interaction of public and private market exposures, providing an integrated view of portfolio opportunities, concentrations and vulnerabilities.
 Provide constructive challenge and independent assessment of strategic allocations, portfolio construction choices and material investment transactions.

 Total Portfolio Analytics & Risk Insight
 Lead enterprise-wide oversight of total portfolio risk across public and private markets, including equities, fixed income, derivatives, real estate, infrastructure, private equity and private credit.
 Monitor macroeconomic conditions, market developments and structural investment themes to assess their potential impact on total portfolio outcomes.
 Lead benchmark governance across asset classes, ensuring benchmarks appropriately reflect mandate objectives, risk exposures and return drivers.
 Oversee stress testing and scenario analysis frameworks, partnering with Investment Management and Actuarial teams to evaluate portfolio and funded-status outcomes across a range of market environments.
 Evaluate portfolio vulnerabilities, diversification benefits, liquidity dynamics and cross-asset interactions through a total fund lens.

 Research & Innovation
 Drive research and thought leadership in portfolio construction, asset allocation, risk factor modelling, diversification and advanced portfolio analytics.
 Advance analytical capabilities related to emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and data-driven investment insights, and assess their implications for portfolios, markets and investment processes.
 Lead innovation in cross-asset correlation, tail-risk analysis, scenario design and forward-looking portfolio assessment methodologies.
 Collaborate with technology partners, external experts and industry peers to strengthen analytical capabilities and investment decision-support frameworks.

 Leadership & Influence
 Lead, develop and mentor a high-performing team of portfolio risk and analytics professionals.
 Build trusted partnerships across Investment Management, Finance, Actuarial, Technology, Legal, Human Resources and other key stakeholder groups.
 Translate complex analysis into clear, actionable insights for senior leaders and governance forums.
 Represent HOOPP externally through industry forums, peer collaboration, research initiatives and thought leadership.
 Contribute to the long-term evolution of HOOPP’s Total Portfolio Approach and broader investment risk framework.

 What you bring: 

 A graduate degree in Finance, Economics, Mathematics, Engineering, Computer Science, Business Administration or a related discipline. A CFA, FRM, MBA or equivalent professional designation is considered an asset.
 12+ years of experience in institutional investing, portfolio construction, investment strategy, total fund management, multi-asset investing, OCIO, capital markets or investment risk leadership.
 Deep understanding of portfolio construction, asset allocation, investment decision-making and risk management across public and private markets.
 Experience evaluating complex multi-asset portfolios, including alternative investments and derivatives.
 Strong knowledge of total fund investing, stress testing, scenario analysis and quantitative portfolio analytics.
 Demonstrated ability to provide strategic insights that inform senior-level investment decisions and to exercise sound judgement when constructively challenging established views.
 Proven people leadership experience, including building, coaching and developing high-performing teams.
 Executive presence and exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex analytical concepts into actionable investment insights.
 Experience within a pension fund, sovereign wealth fund, endowment, insurance asset manager, OCIO platform or other sophisticated institutional investor is preferred. Canadian or international pension experience is considered an asset.
 Experience with Aladdin Risk, Ortec or comparable portfolio and risk management systems is considered an asset.
 Coding, software development, data science or advanced quantitative research experience is advantageous.
