jobs.description:
McKesson, l’une des 10 premières entreprises du classement Fortune Global 500, touche à pratiquement tous les aspects des soins de santé et s’emploie à faire une réelle différence. Nous sommes reconnus pour notre capacité à offrir un savoir, des produits et des services qui rendent les soins de qualité plus accessibles et plus abordables. Chez nous, la santé, le bonheur et le bien-être de nos gens et des personnes que nous desservons sont prioritaires—et nous tiennent à cœur.

Ce que tu fais chez McKesson a de l’importance. Nous favorisons une culture où tu peux t’épanouir et avoir un impact, et où tu es encouragé à proposer de nouvelles idées. Ensemble, nous façonnons l’avenir de la santé pour nos patients, nos communautés et nos équipes. Si tu souhaites dès aujourd’hui contribuer à la santé de demain, nous aimerions avoir de tes nouvelles.

McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

Directeur(trice) principal(e) de l’architecture de solutions/Senior Director, Solution Architecture

À propos du poste

McKesson recherche un(e) Directeur(trice) Principal(e), Architecture d’Entreprise et Expérience Numérique
pour diriger la stratégie d’architecture couvrant l’architecture de solutions, l’architecture applicative, la modernisation des solutions héritées (legacy) et la gestion de l’expérience numérique. Ce leader définira la vision de solutions technologiques modernes, évolutives, sécurisées et centrées sur le client afin de soutenir les priorités de l’entreprise et d’améliorer les résultats opérationnels.

Dans ce rôle, vous dirigerez les pratiques d’architecture qui relient la stratégie d’affaires à l’exécution technologique. Vous collaborerez avec les dirigeants, les équipes produits, ingénierie, sécurité, opérations et les parties prenantes métier afin de moderniser les plateformes, simplifier les environnements hérités, orienter la stratégie d’expérience numérique et renforcer la gouvernance architecturale. Vous développerez également les talents, influencerez les décisions à l’échelle de l’entreprise et aiderez les équipes à livrer des solutions technologiques à fort impact dans un environnement complexe et réglementé.

Ce que vous ferez

Diriger la pratique d’architecture d’entreprise couvrant l’architecture de solutions, l’architecture applicative, la modernisation et la gestion de l’expérience numérique.
Définir les normes d’architecture, les feuilles de route, les modèles de gouvernance et les cadres décisionnels permettant une livraison technologique sécurisée et évolutive.
Collaborer avec les dirigeants et les responsables métier afin d’aligner la stratégie d’architecture sur les objectifs d’affaires, les besoins des clients et les priorités de l’entreprise.
Diriger les stratégies de modernisation des applications et plateformes héritées, y compris la rationalisation applicative, la migration vers le cloud, l’intégration, l’automatisation et la réduction de la dette technique.
Orienter l’architecture de l’expérience numérique afin d’améliorer l’utilisabilité, l’accessibilité, la performance, la fiabilité ainsi que les parcours clients et employés de bout en bout.
Conseiller les équipes sur les modèles d’architecture modernes, notamment les API, les microservices, les plateformes cloud natives, l’intégration de données, la gestion des identités, la sécurité et l’observabilité.
Superviser la planification du portefeuille d’architecture, la stratégie fournisseurs, les recommandations d’investissement et la création de valeur mesurable.
Développer les responsables et les équipes d’architecture grâce au mentorat, à la gestion des talents, à l’évaluation de la performance et à un leadership inclusif.

Exigences de base

13 ans ou plus d’expérience professionnelle en technologie, dont au moins 6 ans dans des fonctions de leadership en architecture, ingénierie, livraison d’applications, plateformes numériques ou transformation technologique.
Diplôme universitaire en informatique, systèmes d’information, ingénierie ou domaine connexe, ou expérience équivalente.
Expérience dans la direction d’architectures d’entreprise, de solutions ou applicatives dans des environnements technologiques de grande envergure.
Expérience de la conception et de la modernisation d’architectures de solutions d’entreprise en s’appuyant sur des plateformes intégrant l’intelligence artificielle et des technologies émergentes afin de stimuler l’innovation, l’évolutivité et la création de valeur.
Expérience dans l’élaboration de stratégies d’architecture, de feuilles de route, de normes, de modèles de gouvernance et de recommandations destinées aux dirigeants.
Expérience dans la modernisation d’applications, de plateformes ou de capacités numériques héritées.
Expérience en gestion de responsables, d’équipes d’architecture ou d’équipes technologiques multidisciplinaires.
Expérience de collaboration avec des parties prenantes métier et technologiques de haut niveau pour influencer la stratégie et l’exécution.
Expérience en planification budgétaire, gestion des fournisseurs, priorisation de portefeuille ou prise de décisions d’investissement technologique.

Compétences et expériences privilégiées

Expérience avec les plateformes cloud, les stratégies API, les microservices, l’architecture événementielle (event-driven), le DevSecOps ou l’ingénierie de plateformes.
Expérience en gestion de l’expérience numérique, plateformes d’expérience client, portails, applications mobiles/web ou solutions omnicanales.
Expérience dans les secteurs de la santé, de la distribution pharmaceutique, de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, du commerce de détail ou d’autres environnements d’entreprise réglementés.
Expérience des cadres d’architecture d’entreprise, des comités de revue d’architecture, de la modélisation des capacités ou de la gestion de portefeuille applicatif.
Expérience de direction de programmes de transformation à grande échelle impliquant plusieurs équipes, fonctions ou unités d’affaires.
Excellentes compétences en communication avec les dirigeants et capacité à simplifier des décisions technologiques complexes pour des audiences métier.
Capacité démontrée à améliorer la performance opérationnelle, réduire la dette technique et accélérer la mise sur le marché.
Style de leadership axé sur la collaboration, la vision stratégique, la conduite du changement, l’orientation client et le développement des talents.

Déplacements, présence au bureau et exigences physiques

Le modèle de travail peut être à distance, hybride ou en présentiel selon les besoins de l’entreprise et de l’équipe.
Des déplacements occasionnels peuvent être requis pour des réunions de leadership, des sessions de planification, des rencontres avec des fournisseurs ou des activités de collaboration d’équipe.
Le poste requiert une utilisation régulière de l’ordinateur ainsi qu’une participation à des réunions virtuelles et en personne.

About The Role

McKesson is seeking a Senior Director, Enterprise Architecture & Digital Experience
to lead architecture strategy across solution architecture, application architecture, legacy solution modernization, and digital experience management. This leader will set the vision for modern, scalable, secure, and customer-centered technology solutions that support enterprise priorities and improve business outcomes.

In this role, you will lead architecture practices that connect business strategy to technology execution. You will partner with senior leaders, product, engineering, security, operations, and business stakeholders to modernize platforms, simplify legacy environments, guide digital experience strategy, and strengthen architecture governance. You will also develop leaders, influence enterprise decisions, and help teams deliver high-impact technology solutions in a complex, regulated environment.

What You’ll Do

Lead the enterprise architecture practice across solution architecture, application architecture, modernization, and digital experience management.
Define architecture standards, roadmaps, governance models, and decision frameworks that enable scalable and secure technology delivery.
Partner with executive and senior business leaders to align architecture strategy with business objectives, customer needs, and enterprise priorities.
Lead legacy application and platform modernization strategies, including rationalization, cloud migration, integration, automation, and technical debt reduction.
Guide digital experience architecture to improve usability, accessibility, performance, reliability, and end-to-end customer and employee journeys.
Advise teams on modern architecture patterns, including APIs, microservices, cloud-native platforms, data integration, identity, security, and observability.
Oversee architecture portfolio planning, vendor strategy, investment recommendations, and measurable value delivery.
Build and develop architecture leaders and teams through coaching, talent planning, performance management, and inclusive leadership practices.

Basic Requirements

13+ years of professional technology experience, including 6+ years of leadership experience in architecture, engineering, application delivery, digital platforms, or technology transformation.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or related field, or equivalent experience.
Experience leading enterprise, solution, or application architecture across large-scale technology environments.
Lead the design and modernization of enterprise solution architectures, leveraging AI-enabled platforms and emerging technologies to drive innovation, scalability, and business value.
Experience developing architecture strategy, roadmaps, standards, governance, and executive-level recommendations.
Experience leading modernization of legacy applications, platforms, or digital capabilities.
Experience managing leaders, architecture teams, or cross-functional technology teams.
Experience partnering with senior business and technology stakeholders to influence strategy and delivery.
Experience with budget planning, vendor management, portfolio prioritization, or technology investment decisions.

Preferred Skills/Experience

Experience with cloud platforms, API strategy, microservices, event-driven architecture, DevSecOps, or platform engineering.
Experience with digital experience management, customer experience platforms, portals, mobile/web applications, or omnichannel solutions.
Experience in healthcare, pharmaceutical distribution, supply chain, retail, or other regulated enterprise environments.
Experience with enterprise architecture frameworks, architecture review boards, capability modeling, or application portfolio management.
Experience leading large-scale transformation programs across multiple teams, functions, or business units.
Strong executive communication skills with the ability to simplify complex technology decisions for business audiences.
Demonstrated ability to improve operational performance, reduce technical debt, and increase speed-to-market.
Leadership approach aligned to collaboration, strategic insight, change leadership, customer focus, and talent development.

Description Of Travel Or In-Office And Physical Requirements

Work model may be remote, hybrid, or office-based depending on business and team needs.
Occasional travel may be required for leadership meetings, planning sessions, vendor engagements, or team collaboration.

As Director of Deal Desk & Pricing, you will lead and scale Varicent's Deal Desk function, serving as the central authority for deal governance, pricing operations, quote-to-booking processes, and commercial execution. You'll work closely with Sales, Customer Success, Renewals, Finance, Legal, Product, and Revenue Operations to drive pricing accuracy, data integrity, operational efficiency, and compliance throughout the customer lifecycle. This role combines strategic leadership with hands-on execution — you'll establish the processes, governance frameworks, systems alignment, and team structure that enable scalable growth. This is a people leadership role: you'll manage and grow Deal Desk professionals while improving deal velocity, profitability, forecasting accuracy, and operational excellence.

What You Will Be Doing

Lead and develop the Deal Desk team, including coaching, performance management, capacity planning, and workload prioritization.
Establish and run Deal Desk operating processes: deal intake, approvals, escalations, service-level expectations, and stakeholder communications.
Own quote-to-booking governance for new business, renewals, expansions, and cross-sell opportunities, ensuring pricing accuracy and policy compliance.
Work with Sales and Customer Success on deal structuring, pricing decisions, exception management, and commercial approvals.
Maintain data integrity and system alignment across Salesforce, CPQ platforms, pricing tools, and related commercial systems.
Partner with Finance on forecasting activities, revenue recognition requirements, commercial risk assessments, and audit readiness.
Build and maintain governance frameworks, policies, documentation, and enablement resources that drive consistent business practices.
Lead process improvement and change management initiatives to reduce deal cycle times and improve scalability and reporting quality.

What You Bring

Demonstrated expertise in Deal Desk, Pricing, Revenue Operations, Commercial Operations, FP&A, Commercial Finance, or related business functions (typically gained over 10–12+ years)
Experience leading teams, programs, or cross-functional operational functions (typically 5+ years)
Experience with complex B2B sales motions, including new business, renewals, expansions, and cross-sell transactions
Expertise in Deal Desk operations, pricing governance, quote-to-booking workflows, commercial approvals, and process design
Experience working with Salesforce, DealHub CPQ, or comparable CPQ/CRM platforms
Solid grasp of how pricing structures, commercial terms, ACV, and contract structures impact forecasting and revenue recognition
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a track record of using operational data to improve business processes and decisions
Ability to influence senior stakeholders across Sales, Finance, Legal, Customer Success, Product, and Revenue Operations

Success Outcomes

First 90 Days

Build a working understanding of Varicent's pricing structure, commercial processes, systems landscape, and quote-to-booking workflows.
Establish strong relationships with Sales, Customer Success, Finance, Legal, Product, and Revenue Operations stakeholders.
Assess current Deal Desk processes, governance controls, approval workflows, and reporting capabilities.
Identify opportunities to improve deal execution efficiency, data quality, and process consistency.

Within 6 Months

Roll out clear governance frameworks, approval structures, and operational standards across the Deal Desk function.
Raise quote quality, pricing accuracy, and first-pass approval rates while cutting rework and processing delays.
Set up consistent forecasting workflows with Finance using Deal Desk insights and commercial data.
Strengthen data integrity and alignment across Salesforce, CPQ platforms, pricing tools, and related systems.
Develop scalable team operating rhythms and performance metrics aligned to business objectives.

Within 12 Months

Position Deal Desk as a go-to strategic partner across Go-To-Market, Finance, and Executive teams.
Show measurable gains in deal cycle times, pricing governance, compliance, and forecasting accuracy.
Deliver scalable quote-to-booking processes that support growth while maintaining strong controls and audit readiness.
Build a high-performing Deal Desk organization with clear accountability and operational excellence.
Create a sustainable operating model that supports revenue growth, profitability objectives, and commercial scalability.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Solutions Architecture — Americas
jobs.description:
Who are we?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

As the Senior Director of Solutions Architecture for the Americas at Cohere, you will own the US and Canada commercial Solutions Architecture function. You will lead the team that turns enterprise interest in agentic AI into deployed, production systems, and you will be accountable for the technical win in the most competitive AI market in the world. The United States and Canada are our largest commercial opportunity, and this seat owns how we win them.

You will take an established, distributed team of strong technical people and raise what it can do — setting the bar and establishing the operating rhythm that lets a team of generalists run consistent, industry-fluent plays at enterprise scale. You will set direction for the function, sit on the Solution Architecture leadership team alongside the regional leaders for EMEA and Asia Pacific, and contribute to company-wide decisions with your peers across Sales, Product and Engineering.

In This Role, You Will

Lead and Scale the Organization: Build, coach and develop a high-performing Solutions Architecture organization across the US and Canada, and grow the senior technical talent within it.
Own the Technical Win: Be personally accountable for the technical outcome of the region’s most strategic pursuits, and be in the room for the ones that decide the year.
Own the US Market: Lead how Cohere positions, proves and sells into US enterprises — our largest commercial opportunity, and the market this seat is measured on.
Extend Our Reach: Grow the share of the region’s pipeline the team is technically leading, and make sure we are engaged early on the opportunities that matter most.
Own the Number with Sales: Partner with regional Sales leadership as a co-owner of the region’s number, not as a support function to it.
Set Direction for the Function: Define the vision, strategy and operating model for Americas Solutions Architecture, and hold your leaders accountable for delivery and execution against it.
Build Repeatable Solution Practices: Establish scalable solution-selling methodologies, industry playbooks, executive narratives, business cases and technical delivery frameworks that improve consistency and win rates.
Architect Enterprise AI Solutions: Guide customers in designing secure, scalable, production-ready agentic AI solutions across cloud, hybrid, VPC and on-premises environments.
Shape Product Direction: Partner closely with Product and Engineering to translate customer feedback and market needs into platform improvements and roadmap priorities.
Attract Talent to Cohere: Bring senior technical field talent with you and continue to attract it. Building the bench is part of the job, not a consequence of it.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and develop the Americas commercial Solutions Architecture team through coaching, hiring, performance management and career development.
Partner with regional Sales leadership to pursue and close strategic enterprise opportunities across financial services, healthcare, energy, technology and other key verticals.
Own the region’s technical coverage model, and ensure the team is engaged early and consistently on the opportunities that matter most.
Lead executive workshops, discovery sessions, solution presentations and technical deep dives with C-suite and senior customer stakeholders.
Develop business cases, solution architectures, implementation roadmaps and technical proposals that align customer objectives with Cohere’s platform.
Guide customers through the deployment of enterprise AI solutions, ensuring scalability, security, governance and operational readiness.
Create repeatable solution assets, industry playbooks and best practices that enable the team to consistently deliver high-quality customer engagements.
Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Sales and Customer Success to ensure alignment between customer needs and platform evolution, and contribute to decisions that reach beyond your own function.
Serve as the voice of the field by capturing customer feedback and competitive insights that influence product strategy.
Own and report on the region’s operational and commercial metrics, including technical win rates, pipeline health, coverage and team performance.

What We’re Looking For

Leadership Experience: 15+ years in Solutions Architecture, Solutions Engineering, Technical Consulting or Enterprise Architecture, including 7+ years leading customer-facing technical teams, and a record of developing people into senior and leadership roles.
People Leadership: A proven record of hiring, coaching and developing high-performing Solutions Architecture or Solutions Engineering teams, and of building or transforming an organization rather than inheriting a healthy one.
Executive Presence: You command a room. You are credible in front of a CEO and their business leaders, the people who own the problem and the budget, and equally credible in front of a Chief Information Officer, a Chief AI Officer or a Chief Information Security Officer. You can move between the business case and the architecture without losing either audience.
Hands-On Technical Credibility: You are technical enough to be believed by a strong engineering bench. You work with models and agents yourself, you can pressure-test your team’s architecture, and you can be the most useful person in a design conversation when it matters. This is a player-coach seat, not an overlay.
Commercial Acumen: A demonstrated ability to partner with enterprise Sales leadership, influence strategic deals, and articulate business value to executive stakeholders. You have carried a number and can point to deals you personally moved.
Consulting Mindset: Experience leading complex enterprise solution engagements, developing business cases, implementation plans and executive-ready recommendations.
Technical Expertise: A strong understanding of modern AI architectures, including large language models, agentic systems, retrieval, enterprise integrations, cloud platforms, hybrid and on-premises deployments, security and governance.
Enterprise Experience: Experience designing and delivering enterprise technology solutions in complex, regulated or large-scale environments.
Cross-Functional Influence: A record of contributing to decisions beyond your own function, and of working effectively with Product and Engineering leadership.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience building or turning around a regional technical field organization, and evidence of what changed as a result.
Background in enterprise AI, cloud, or data platform companies, or applied AI consulting organizations.
Experience supporting customers in regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare, energy, or the public sector.
Experience building repeatable solution-selling methodologies and helping generalist technical teams operate at a consistently high level.
A network of senior technical field talent you can attract to Cohere.
Experience operating in high-growth environments where speed, ownership and cross-functional collaboration are critical.

Full-Time Employees At Cohere Enjoy These Perks

A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.
Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.
RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.
100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.
Annual enrichment benefits:

Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.

Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)
Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.

How And Where We Work

Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.
For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.
For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.
Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.

We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form, and we will work together to meet your needs.

We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider.

Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers page.

This role is open to Manager-level or Director-level depending on candidate’s experience and qualifications

We are looking for an Enterprise Application Support Lead to oversee the configuration, maintenance and ongoing support of Berkley Canada’s core insurance business systems, including underwriting, policy administration and claims platforms. This role serves as a key bridge between insurance business stakeholders, system vendors, and internal technology teams, ensuring core systems continue to meet operational, data and control requirements. The successful candidate will bring strong commercial insurance domain knowledge, experience working with third-party system vendors, and a disciplined approach to system support, change and release management.

Develop and maintain a deep understanding of Berkley Canada’s core insurance systems, including features, configuration, integration points and operational dependencies.
Engage closely with underwriting, claims and operations stakeholders to understand business needs and map these to system functionality and configuration options.
Work with system vendors and implementation partners to interpret requirements, develop implementation approaches, oversee delivery and hold vendors accountable for outcomes.
Track and manage system defects; facilitate prioritization, analysis and development of workarounds; oversee vendor resolution of defects, user acceptance testing and release.
Plan and oversee version upgrade cycles, staying informed of new system features and functionality and determining when and how upgrades should be adopted.
Serve as a subject matter expert for system testing, including development of test plans for new features, defect fixes, regression and integration testing; oversee test execution and sign-off.
Collaborate with the Data Engineering team to ensure changes to core systems appropriately consider downstream data, analytics and reporting requirements.
Establish and promote frameworks, standards and best practices for system super users who manage business configuration and insurance policy issuance.
Establish, document and periodically test controls related to third-party application release management and vendor management.
Own and maintain key vendor relationships related to core insurance applications.

You will also have the chance to...

Make a noticeable impact on a small but growing team where the benefits of your contributions will be highly visible to the rest of the organization.
Draw from resources and expertise available in the wider Berkley Group of companies.
Enjoy a competitive benefits package including a personal budget for professional development.
Join a supportive and empowering company culture that recognizes and values the diversity of our people.
Work flexibly in a hybrid remote/on-site environment.

Experience working with third-party system vendors, including requirements interpretation, delivery oversight and vendor relationship management.
Solid understanding of system testing disciplines, release management and change control in a regulated environment.
Ability to understand and articulate how system changes impact downstream data, reporting and analytics.
Strong communication skills with the ability to work effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Highly organized, detail-oriented and comfortable operating in a control-conscious environment.
Collaborative, pragmatic and solution-focused approach.
Post-secondary educational qualification in computer information systems, computer science or business management preferred but not required with relevant work experience.

jobs.description:
Position Description

Health Technology & Transformation

CGI is seeking a Director Consulting, Health Technology & Transformation to provide senior technical and health industry leadership across the Atlantic Business Unit.

As one of Canada's largest IT and business consulting services firms, CGI combines strong local client relationships with the scale, industry expertise, delivery capabilities, and intellectual property of a global organization. In this role, you will help connect the needs of Atlantic Canadian health organizations with CGI's national and global health, technology, and delivery capabilities.

Shape Health Solutions. Provide Technical Leadership. Enable Successful Transformation.

As a Director Consulting Expert Health Technology & Transformation, you will serve as a senior technical and solution advisory leader for CGI's health clients and strategic health initiatives across Atlantic Canada.

Working with Directors of Consulting Services, account leaders, architects, delivery leaders, and technology specialists, you will bring deep health sector and technical expertise to strategic client opportunities and complex transformation initiatives.

You will lead technical discovery, solution shaping, technology strategy, architecture alignment, and senior technical assurance, helping CGI convert client priorities into credible, secure, and executable solutions.

You will help clients understand how digital health platforms, enterprise applications, integration, interoperability, data, AI, cloud, cybersecurity, and automation can be applied to address their clinical, administrative, and operational priorities.

You will also help CGI develop a more cohesive health technology capability across Atlantic Canada by connecting local client needs with CGI's broader health expertise, reusable assets, delivery capabilities, intellectual property, and alliance partner solutions.

What You'll Bring

Your future duties and responsibilities

Health Technology Advisory

Serve as a senior health technology advisor to client technology leaders, digital health executives, operational leaders, clinical stakeholders, architects, and transformation teams.
Bring the appropriate technical expertise into strategic client discussions and opportunities by collaborating across CGI's account, consulting, architecture, and delivery teams.
Lead technical discovery sessions, current state assessments, architecture reviews, option analyses, and technology roadmap development.
Translate clinical, operational, administrative, and business requirements into practical technology strategies and solution approaches.
Advise clients on digital health modernization, enterprise architecture, interoperability, integration, data platforms, AI adoption, cloud transformation, cybersecurity, automation, and application modernization.
Help clients evaluate technology alternatives, dependencies, risks, implementation considerations, and total cost of ownership.
Ensure recommendations reflect healthcare delivery realities, privacy, security, clinical workflow, data governance, regulatory requirements, and organizational readiness.
Communicate complex technology considerations clearly to technical and non technical stakeholders.

Technical Opportunity Shaping

Partner with account and industry leaders to assess and shape strategic health opportunities.
Provide technical leadership during early opportunity qualification by assessing feasibility, complexity, capability requirements, delivery risks, and potential solution approaches.
Lead or support technical discovery workshops, solutioning sessions, demonstrations, proofs of concept, and architecture discussions.
Develop high level solution architectures, technology roadmaps, implementation approaches, estimates, assumptions, dependencies, and risk assessments.
Coordinate input from CGI specialists across digital health, cloud, data and AI, cybersecurity, application services, managed services, enterprise platforms, and systems integration.
Connect Atlantic Canadian opportunities with CGI capabilities, accelerators, intellectual property, case studies, delivery centres, and alliance partner technologies.
Ensure proposed solutions are technically credible, differentiated, scalable, secure, and aligned with the client environment.
Provide senior technical input into proposals, presentations, statements of work, business cases, and competitive procurements.
Participate in client presentations and procurement processes as CGI's senior health technology subject matter expert.
Help create a clear transition from opportunity shaping into detailed design, mobilization, and delivery.

Health Architecture and Solution Leadership

Provide architecture and solution leadership across complex health transformation initiatives.
Assess how individual technologies and initiatives fit within a client's enterprise architecture, digital health strategy, and long term operating model.
Guide solution teams in developing integrated architectures spanning applications, data, integration, cloud, cybersecurity, infrastructure, and user experience.
Promote interoperability, reuse, scalability, security, maintainability, and alignment with relevant health sector standards.
Provide expertise in health data exchange, integration patterns, APIs, interoperability frameworks, and standards such as HL7 and FHIR where applicable.
Support the modernization and integration of electronic medical record, electronic health record, claims, benefits, case management, scheduling, patient engagement, clinical, and administrative platforms.
Identify technical risks, architecture gaps, capability constraints, and dependencies before they affect implementation.
Help clients avoid isolated technology investments by promoting enterprise level roadmaps and sustainable architecture decisions.

Delivery Assurance and Technical Governance

Provide senior technical oversight for strategic or high risk health engagements.
Support engagement mobilization by validating solution scope, architecture, resource requirements, delivery assumptions, and technical dependencies.
Participate in architecture governance, design reviews, technical risk reviews, and executive steering discussions where appropriate.
Work with delivery leaders to ensure implementation remains aligned with the agreed solution strategy and client outcomes.
Provide escalation support for complex technical, architectural, integration, or health domain issues.
Help delivery teams navigate client technology environments, governance processes, privacy requirements, and health sector constraints.
Review significant solution changes to assess their effect on scope, risk, cost, architecture, and long term maintainability.
Capture lessons learned and reusable technical assets from health engagements.

Capability Development

Help define the health technology capabilities required to support CGI's Atlantic health strategy.
Collaborate with CGI's account, industry, and technology leaders to identify market needs, emerging technology trends, capability gaps, and areas in which CGI can differentiate.
Develop reusable health technology assets, reference architectures, assessment methods, solution patterns, demonstrations, and points of view.
Connect Atlantic teams with CGI health experts, architects, delivery centres, and technology practices across Canada and globally.
Mentor architects, consultants, and technical team members working within the health portfolio.
Help improve health industry fluency among CGI's technical teams and technology fluency among CGI's health consulting and account teams.
Support the identification and development of technical talent required for current and future health opportunities.
Represent CGI in health technology forums, industry working groups, technical conferences, and partner discussions as appropriate.
Maintain current knowledge of health technology developments, emerging standards, cybersecurity threats, platform capabilities, and industry leading practices.

Required Qualifications To Be Successful In This Role

jobs.title: Director, Security Architecture & Engineering, Information & Corporate Security
jobs.description:
Purpose. Performance. People. 

 Joining CPP Investments means joining one of the world’s most admired and respected institutional investors to drive a single mandate: to deliver strong, sustainable returns for generations of Canadians.   

 With a long-term horizon and global reach, we deploy capital at scale across public and private markets. Our size, stability, and disciplined investment philosophy allow us to pursue complex opportunities and build enduring partnerships worldwide.  

 For our people, this means meaningful work with tangible impact, real opportunity, and collaboration with exceptional colleagues who value partnership and performance. Here, you’ll contribute to outcomes that matter alongside team members committed to excellence and shared success.   

 The Role 

The Director, Security Architecture & Engineering will provide strategic and technical leadership for CPP Investments' security architecture and engineering function. Reporting to the Managing Director, Security Architecture & Engineering, you will lead the development of enterprise security architecture, cloud security strategy, and security engineering capabilities while partnering across the organization to embed security into technology delivery and operations. You will build and mentor a high-performing team, drive innovation, and help strengthen CPP Investments' overall cybersecurity posture 

 The Team 

 Technology & Operations enables CPP Investments to deliver on its global investment mandate through secure, resilient, and innovative technology capabilities. The department partners across the organization to provide scalable platforms, modern infrastructure, and cybersecurity capabilities that protect the organization while supporting business growth.

 The Security Architecture & Engineering team is responsible for establishing enterprise security architecture standards, advancing security engineering capabilities, and embedding security by design across technology platforms. The team works closely with technology and business partners to deliver secure, resilient solutions that effectively manage cyber risk.

 Accountabilities 
 Provide strategic leadership, direction, and mentorship to the Security Architecture & Engineering team while helping shape and execute the organization's long-term cybersecurity strategy.

 Lead the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of enterprise security architecture, ensuring alignment with business objectives, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices.

 Develop and execute the organization's cloud security strategy, strengthening the security, scalability, and resilience of cloud environments.

 Evaluate emerging cybersecurity technologies, trends, and standards, driving the adoption of innovative solutions that align with the organization's risk appetite.

 Lead security architecture reviews and risk assessments, providing expert guidance and actionable recommendations to stakeholders.

 Partner with technology, operations, and business teams to embed security-by-design principles throughout the technology lifecycle and effectively communicate security strategies and risks to diverse audiences.

 Oversee the design and implementation of security platforms, automation capabilities, and engineering solutions that enhance operational effectiveness and strengthen the organization's security posture.

 What You Bring 
 Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related discipline.

 CISSP, CISM, CCSP, or an equivalent industry certification.

 Minimum of 15 years of experience in security architecture, security engineering, or a related cybersecurity discipline.

 Minimum of 4 years of people leadership experience leading security architecture or security engineering teams.

 Demonstrated expertise in enterprise security architecture, cloud security, security engineering, risk assessment, and security technologies within complex organizations; experience in Canadian financial services is considered an asset.

 Strong leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence technical and business audiences.

 Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and collaboration skills, with a commitment to continuous learning and staying current with evolving cybersecurity trends.

 You are motivated to contribute to something larger than yourself, approach complex challenges with rigor, and hold yourself to  high standards in a collaborative, performance-driven environment.   

 We provide colleagues with cutting-edge AI tools, dedicated learning time, and practical support to help them deliver with greater impact.

 Inclusion & Accessibility 
 CPP Investments is committed to  equitable access to employment and building a workforce that reflects diverse talent and perspectives. If you require accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.   

 Attention: Protect Yourself from Fraud 
 CPP Investments is committed to a secure and transparent recruitment process. We will never ask candidates for payment or financial information at any stage of hiring. All legitimate opportunities are posted on our careers page, and communications will come from our applicant tracking system, Workday.  

 CPP Investments may use AI tools to help screen and assess applicants by analyzing resumes and applications for relevant skills and experience. These tools support, but do not replace, human decision-making.

 #LI-ONSITE

jobs.title: Directeur, Planification de la chaîne d’approvisionnement et transport/Director, Supply Chain Planning & Transportation
jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

 What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

 Directeur, Planification de la chaîne d’approvisionnement et transport 
 Aperçu du poste 
 Le directeur ou la directrice, Planification de la chaîne d’approvisionnement et transport, est responsable de diriger la stratégie technologique, la prestation de services et l’habilitation opérationnelle des plateformes et des capacités soutenant l’écosystème de planification de la chaîne d’approvisionnement et de transport de bout en bout de McKesson Canada.
 Ce rôle collabore étroitement avec les équipes de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, de la distribution pharmaceutique et des opérations, des approvisionnements, des opérations des centres de distribution, du transport, de l’analytique ainsi qu’avec des partenaires technologiques externes afin de garantir que les solutions de planification et de transport sont stables, sécurisées, évolutives et alignées sur les priorités de l’entreprise.
 Le poste fournit un leadership dans les domaines de la prévision de la demande, de la planification de l’approvisionnement, du réapprovisionnement, de l’optimisation des stocks, de l’exécution du transport, de la visibilité, de l’intégration des transporteurs et des flottes, de la qualité des données, de l’analytique et de l’intégration entre les systèmes.
 Le directeur ou la directrice est responsable d’assurer la fiabilité des services, de faire évoluer le modèle opérationnel, de réduire les frictions opérationnelles, d’améliorer la réalisation de la valeur d’affaires et de soutenir la modernisation technologique tout en gérant les risques, la conformité, la performance des fournisseurs et la discipline financière.

 Principales responsabilités 
 Leadership stratégique 
 Élaborer et exécuter la stratégie technologique et de services pour les solutions de planification de la chaîne d’approvisionnement et de transport, en assurant l’alignement avec les objectifs d’affaires de McKesson Canada, les priorités de croissance, les attentes en matière de niveaux de service et les besoins de résilience opérationnelle.
 Collaborer avec les dirigeants des secteurs d’affaires et de la technologie afin de définir des feuilles de route pluriannuelles pour la planification, le réapprovisionnement, la visibilité du transport, l’optimisation, l’automatisation, l’exploitation des données et la modernisation des plateformes de base.
 Fournir un leadership éclairé sur les tendances technologiques de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, y compris la planification avancée, l’optimisation, la prévision alimentée par l’IA et l’apprentissage automatique, l’évolution des plateformes SaaS, l’intégration fondée sur les API, l’analytique du transport et les capacités de visibilité numérique.
 Traduire les priorités d’affaires en plans technologiques exploitables, recommandations d’investissement, séquencement de la livraison et résultats mesurables en matière de valeur.
 Prestation des services et modèle opérationnel 
 Assurer la responsabilité et la maturité du modèle opérationnel de prestation des services pour les technologies de planification de la chaîne d’approvisionnement et de transport, y compris la définition claire des responsabilités, la gestion des demandes, la priorisation, la gestion des incidents et des problèmes, la gouvernance des mises en production, le contrôle des changements et l’amélioration continue.
 Définir et gérer les indicateurs clés de performance (KPI), les ententes de niveau de service (SLA/SLO), les mesures de consommation, la transparence des coûts et les rapports destinés à la direction relativement aux services de planification et de transport.
 Assurer un soutien fiable aux processus d’affaires complexes à volume élevé, notamment la prévision, la planification de l’approvisionnement, le réapprovisionnement, l’optimisation des stocks, la gestion des stocks par les fournisseurs, l’acheminement du transport, la visibilité des expéditions, l’intégration des centres de distribution, la visibilité des commandes ainsi que les interfaces avec les transporteurs et les flottes.
 Collaborer avec les responsables de produits d’affaires, les dirigeants opérationnels, le PMO, les équipes d’architecture, de données, de cybersécurité, d’infrastructure et les fournisseurs afin de coordonner les dépendances interservices et de réduire les transferts.
 Gestion d’équipe 
 Diriger, encadrer et développer une équipe multidisciplinaire composée de gestionnaires, d’analystes, d’ingénieurs, de responsables de services et de ressources fournisseurs soutenant les capacités de planification et de transport.
 Établir des objectifs et des attentes clairs, offrir du coaching et de la rétroaction, et favoriser une culture de responsabilisation, de collaboration, d’orientation client, de rigueur opérationnelle et d’apprentissage continu.
 Élaborer des plans de ressources et de capacités visant à répondre aux besoins en matière de connaissances du domaine, d’expertise des systèmes, de compétences d’intégration, d’analyse d’affaires, de qualité des données, de gestion des fournisseurs et de couverture du soutien.
 Promouvoir une planification efficace de la relève, la documentation, la formation croisée et la réduction des points de défaillance uniques.
 Développement et mise en œuvre de solutions 
 Superviser la conception, la mise en œuvre, l’amélioration et la gestion du cycle de vie des solutions technologiques de planification et de transport, en veillant à ce qu’elles soient évolutives, résilientes, sécurisées, faciles à soutenir et adaptées aux besoins de l’entreprise.
 Guider les équipes de livraison dans les activités liées aux exigences, à l’architecture, à la conception de l’intégration, au mappage des données, aux essais, au déploiement, à l’hypercare et à la préparation à la production.
 Assurer une intégration efficace entre les principales plateformes et les flux de données, notamment les systèmes de planification, les outils de transport, MBA/AS400 le cas échéant, l’EDI, les API, les plateformes analytiques, les données de référence, les tableaux de bord ainsi que les capacités de visibilité destinées aux clients en aval.
 Favoriser l’excellence de la livraison de projets, la saine gestion financière et la réalisation de la valeur dans le cadre des initiatives d’amélioration, de modernisation et de soutien opérationnel.
 Gestion des fournisseurs et des partenaires 
 Gérer les relations avec les fournisseurs externes, les partenaires technologiques et les prestataires de services soutenant les capacités de planification de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, de transport, d’analytique, d’intégration et de services gérés.
 Évaluer la performance des fournisseurs en fonction de leurs engagements, des SLA, des livrables, des modalités commerciales et des résultats d’affaires attendus.
 Soutenir la gestion du cycle de vie des contrats, les évaluations de renouvellement, les feuilles de route des fournisseurs, l’escalade des problèmes et les occasions de partenariats stratégiques.
 Veiller à ce que les fournisseurs assurent un transfert de connaissances efficace, une documentation adéquate, la maintenabilité des solutions et des pratiques opérationnelles durables.
 Gestion des risques et conformité 
 Veiller à ce que les solutions soient conformes aux politiques de McKesson, aux exigences de cybersécurité, aux normes de protection des renseignements personnels, aux attentes réglementaires, aux exigences d’audit et aux contrôles des risques technologiques.
 Maintenir les plans de résilience, de reprise après sinistre, de gestion des accès et de continuité des activités pour les services technologiques de planification et de transport.
 Identifier et atténuer de façon proactive les risques liés à la qualité des données, à la stabilité des plateformes, aux défaillances d’intégration, à la dépendance envers les fournisseurs, à la dette technique, à la préparation opérationnelle, à la sécurité et aux lacunes des processus.
 Mettre en place une gouvernance des changements en production, des interventions en cas d’incident, de l’analyse des causes profondes et des mesures correctives et préventives.
 Excellence opérationnelle et création de valeur 
 Favoriser l’excellence opérationnelle grâce à la normalisation des processus, à l’automatisation, à l’optimisation des coûts, à la simplification des plateformes, à la documentation et à l’amélioration continue des services.
 Collaborer avec les parties prenantes de l’entreprise afin d’améliorer les capacités de précision des prévisions, l’efficacité de la planification, le soutien à la prise de décisions relatives aux stocks, la visibilité du transport, les perspectives sur la performance des livraisons et la réactivité de la chaîne d’approvisionnement de bout en bout.
 Soutenir les discussions sur la priorisation en fournissant une information transparente sur les impacts d’affaires, la capacité, les risques, les coûts et les dépendances.
 Générer une valeur mesurable grâce à une meilleure fiabilité des services, à la réduction des efforts manuels, à une résolution plus rapide des problèmes, à une meilleure qualité des données, à une diminution des risques de conformité et à un meilleur alignement avec les besoins de l’entreprise.
 Indicateurs de succès 
 Réussite des livraisons mesurée selon les délais, la portée, le budget, la qualité, la préparation à la production et l’adoption par les utilisateurs.
 Réduction du volume d’incidents, de leur récurrence et du délai moyen de résolution; amélioration du respect des SLA/SLO pour les services critiques de planification et de transport.
 Amélioration de la transparence concernant la consommation des services, les facteurs de coûts, la performance des fournisseurs et les contraintes de capacité.
 Renforcement de la confiance des utilisateurs envers les plateformes de planification et de transport grâce à des opérations stables, à une meilleure qualité des données et à des intégrations fiables.
 Respect constant des exigences en matière de sécurité, de conformité, d’accès, de résilience et d’audit.
 Démonstration d’une valeur d’affaires grâce à des gains d’efficacité, à la réduction du travail manuel, à une meilleure aide à la décision, à une visibilité accrue et au soutien des résultats liés aux revenus, aux marges, au service et à l’expérience client.

 Qualifications minimales (connaissances, compétences et aptitudes) 
 Baccalauréat en technologies de l’information, en informatique, en chaîne d’approvisionnement, en génie, en administration des affaires ou expérience pratique équivalente; diplôme d’études supérieures ou certifications pertinentes considérés comme un atout.
 Minimum de 10 à 12 années d’expérience progressive en leadership technologique, incluant une expérience significative en gestion d’applications d’entreprise, prestation de services, transformation ou livraison de solutions dans les domaines de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, de la logistique, du transport, de la distribution ou des secteurs connexes.
 Expérience des technologies de planification de la chaîne d’approvisionnement et/ou de transport, notamment la prévision de la demande, la planification de l’approvisionnement, le réapprovisionnement, l’optimisation des stocks, les systèmes TMS/exécution du transport, l’intégration des itinéraires, des flottes et des transporteurs, la visibilité des expéditions, les intégrations EDI/API, les plateformes de données et l’analytique.
 Solide compréhension de la gestion des services TI, des modèles opérationnels de produits et de plateformes, des pratiques de livraison de projets, du cycle de développement logiciel (SDLC), des méthodologies Agile et Waterfall, du soutien à la production, de la gestion des incidents et des problèmes ainsi que de la gouvernance des mises en production.
 Capacité démontrée à collaborer avec des intervenants d’affaires de niveau supérieur, à traduire les besoins de l’entreprise en feuilles de route technologiques et à exercer une influence dans un environnement matriciel sans dépendre uniquement de l’autorité hiérarchique directe.
 Solides compétences en gestion des fournisseurs, supervision contractuelle, gestion financière et établissement des priorités.
 Expérience démontrée en leadership, incluant la création d’équipes engagées, le développement des talents, l’établissement d’orientations et l’amélioration de la responsabilisation.
 Excellentes compétences analytiques, en communication, en présentation à la direction, en résolution de problèmes et en prise de décision; le bilinguisme français-anglais est préféré pour interagir avec les parties prenantes canadiennes.
 Personne organisée, méthodique et attentive aux détails, capable de gérer plusieurs priorités, de travailler sous pression et de diriger efficacement en situation d’incident, d’ambiguïté et de changement.
 Orienté(e) vers le client et les résultats, avec un engagement envers une prestation de services de haute qualité et la création d’une valeur d’affaires mesurable.

 Conditions de travail 
 Présence au bureau requise. Nous appliquons un modèle Flex & Connect avec une présence au bureau de deux jours par semaine.
 ____________________________________________________________________

 Director, Supply Chain Planning & Transportation  
 Position Overview  
 The Director, Supply Chain Planning & Transportation is responsible for leading the technology strategy, service delivery, and operational enablement for platforms and capabilities supporting McKesson Canada’s end-to-end supply chain planning and transportation ecosystem. This role partners closely with Supply Chain, Pharmaceutical Distribution & Operations, Procurement, DC Operations, Transportation, Analytics, and external technology partners to ensure planning and transportation solutions are stable, secure, scalable, and aligned to business priorities. 
 The role provides leadership across demand forecasting, supply planning, replenishment, inventory optimization, transportation execution, visibility, carrier/fleet integration, data quality, analytics, and cross-system integration. The Director is accountable for delivering reliable services, maturing the operating model, reducing operational friction, improving business value realization, and enabling technology modernization while managing risk, compliance, vendor performance, and financial discipline. 

 Key Responsibilities  
 Strategic Leadership  
 Develop and execute the technology and service strategy for Supply Chain Planning and Transportation solutions, ensuring alignment with McKesson Canada business objectives, growth priorities, service-level expectations, and operational resilience needs. 
 Partner with senior business and technology leadership to define multi-year roadmaps for planning, replenishment, transportation visibility, optimization, automation, data enablement, and modernization of core platforms. 
 Provide thought leadership on supply chain technology trends, including advanced planning, optimization, AI/ML-enabled forecasting, SaaS platform evolution, API-based integration, transportation analytics, and digital visibility capabilities. 
 Translate business priorities into actionable technology plans, investment recommendations, delivery sequencing, and measurable value outcomes. 
 Service Delivery & Operating Model  
 Own and mature the Service Delivery Operating Model for Supply Chain Planning and Transportation technology services, including clear accountability, demand intake, prioritization, incident/problem management, release governance, change control, and continuous improvement. 
 Define and manage service KPIs, SLAs/SLOs, consumption metrics, cost transparency, and executive reporting for planning and transportation services. 
 Ensure reliable support for complex, high-volume business processes including forecasting, supply planning, replenishment, inventory optimization, vendor-managed inventory enablement, transportation routing, shipment visibility, DC integration, order visibility, and carrier/fleet interfaces. 
 Partner with business product owners, operations leaders, PMO, architecture, data, cybersecurity, infrastructure, and vendor teams to coordinate cross-service dependencies and reduce handoffs. 
 Team Management  
 Lead, coach, and develop a multidisciplinary team of managers, analysts, engineers, service leads, and vendor resources supporting planning and transportation capabilities. 
 Set clear goals and expectations, provide coaching and feedback, and foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, customer focus, operational discipline, and continuous learning. 
 Build resource and capability plans that address domain knowledge, system expertise, integration skills, business analysis, data quality, vendor management, and support coverage needs. 
 Promote effective succession planning, documentation, cross-training, and reduction of single points of failure. 
 Solution Development & Implementation  
 Oversee design, implementation, enhancement, and lifecycle management of planning and transportation technology solutions, ensuring they are scalable, resilient, secure, supportable, and fit for business purpose. 
 Guide delivery teams through requirements, architecture, integration design, data mapping, testing, deployment, hypercare, and production readiness activities. 
 Ensure effective integration across key platforms and data flows, including planning systems, transportation tools, MBA/AS400 where applicable, EDI, APIs, analytics platforms, master data, dashboards, and downstream customer-facing visibility capabilities. 
 Drive project delivery excellence, financial stewardship, and value realization across enhancement, modernization, and operational support initiatives. 
 Vendor & Partner Management  
 Manage relationships with external vendors, technology partners, and service providers supporting supply chain planning, transportation, analytics, integration, and managed services capabilities. 
 Evaluate vendor performance against commitments, SLAs, deliverables, commercial terms, and expected business outcomes. 
 Support contract lifecycle management, renewal assessments, vendor roadmaps, issue escalation, and strategic partnership opportunities. 
 Ensure vendors provide effective knowledge transfer, documentation, supportability, and sustainable operating practices. 
 Risk Management & Compliance  
 Ensure solutions comply with McKesson policies, cybersecurity requirements, privacy standards, regulatory expectations, audit requirements, and technology risk controls. 
 Maintain resiliency, disaster recovery, access management, and business continuity plans for planning and transportation technology services. 
 Proactively identify and mitigate risks related to data quality, platform stability, integration failures, vendor dependency, technical debt, operational readiness, security, and process gaps. 
 Establish governance around production changes, incident response, root-cause analysis, and corrective/preventive actions. 
 Operational Excellence & Value Delivery  
 Drive operational excellence through process standardization, automation, cost optimization, platform simplification, documentation, and continuous service improvement. 
 Partner with business stakeholders to improve forecast accuracy enablement, planning efficiency, inventory decision support, transportation visibility, delivery performance insight, and end-to-end supply chain responsiveness. 
 Support prioritization discussions by providing transparent business impact, capacity, risk, cost, and dependency information. 
 Deliver measurable value through improved service reliability, reduced manual effort, faster issue resolution, better data quality, reduced compliance risk, and stronger business alignment. 
 Success Metrics  
 Delivery success measured by time, scope, budget, quality, production readiness, and business adoption. 
 Reduction in incident volume, recurrence, and mean time to resolution; improved SLA/SLO adherence for critical planning and transportation services. 
 Improved transparency of service consumption, cost drivers, vendor performance, and capacity constraints. 
 Improved business confidence in planning and transportation platforms through stable operations, data quality, and reliable integrations. 
 Security, compliance, access, resiliency, and audit expectations met consistently. 
 Demonstrated business value through efficiency gains, reduced manual work, improved decision support, enhanced visibility, and support for revenue, margin, service, and customer outcomes. 

 Minimum Job Qualifications (Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities):  
 Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Supply Chain, Engineering, Business, or equivalent practical experience; advanced degree or relevant certifications are an asset. 
 Minimum 10–12 years of progressive technology leadership experience, including significant experience leading enterprise applications, service delivery, transformation, or solution delivery in supply chain, logistics, transportation, distribution, or related domains. 
 Experience with supply chain planning and/or transportation technology capabilities such as demand forecasting, supply planning, replenishment, inventory optimization, TMS/transportation execution, route/fleet/carrier integration, shipment visibility, EDI/API integrations, data platforms, and analytics. 
 Strong understanding of IT service management, product/platform operating models, project delivery practices, SDLC, Agile/Waterfall delivery, production support, incident/problem management, and release governance. 
 Demonstrated ability to partner with senior business stakeholders, translate business needs into technology roadmaps, and influence across matrixed teams without relying solely on direct authority. 
 Strong vendor management, contract oversight, financial management, and prioritization skills. 
 Proven leadership capability with experience building engaged teams, developing talent, setting direction, and improving accountability. 
 Strong analytical, communication, executive presentation, problem-solving, and decision-making skills; bilingual French/English preferred for Canadian stakeholder engagement. 
 Organized, methodical, and detail-oriented; able to manage multiple priorities, operate under pressure, and lead effectively through incidents, ambiguity, and change. 
 Customer-focused and outcome-oriented, with a commitment to high-quality service delivery and measurable business value.

 Ready to lead the financial future of a brand with heart and purpose? 
 At Hadley Designs, we believe every product should fill homes with beauty, learning, and inspiration. We design screen-free learning tools that help children fall in love with learning and help parents feel proud of how they nurture that growth.

 Your Core Focus
 You’ll own the full finance function, building scalable systems, managing cash flow, driving profitability, and leading financial strategy to support Hadley Designs’ next era of growth.

 ≤10% variance between forecasted and actual EBITDA
 12-month rolling cash forecast maintained weekly
 SOPs for all finance processes documented within 3 months

You’re not just reporting numbers, you’re building the foundation for smart, sustainable expansion.

jobs.description:
🚨 Urgent Hiring — Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. The selection process may take up to 4 weeks, but early applicants are strongly encouraged.
 Ready to Empower a Growing Team and Shape Our Future? 
 At Hadley Designs, we believe that learning should be enjoyable, engaging, and screen-free. Millions of parents and teachers trust our beautifully designed, developmentally aligned educational tools to help children grow and thrive. As a fast-growing brand, we are on a mission to make learning meaningful for families around the world.
 We are seeking a  Director of Recruiting & People Strategy  to join our team and build the systems that will drive our next phase of growth. If you are passionate about creating scalable people systems, empowering teams, and cultivating a culture that supports both personal and professional growth, this role offers a unique opportunity to make a significant impact.

 About Hadley Designs 
 Hadley Designs is redefining early education with creativity and purpose. Every product we create is hand-drawn and teacher-designed, crafted with care to build confidence and connection. Our screen-free tools help families and teachers make learning fun and meaningful, nurturing curiosity and creativity in children.
 Our Mission: 
We design screen-free products that parents can trust to help their children learn, grow, and reach their full potential. We create beautifully designed, developmentally sound tools that replace noise and distraction with connection, curiosity, and real learning.
 Our Vision: 
We aim to build the most trusted children’s brand in the world, present in millions of homes, reshaping how families learn, connect, and grow. Our products will be so widely used and passed down that generations of children will grow up learning from them and choose them again for their own families.

 Role Overview 
 As the   Director of Recruiting & People Strategy, you will own how Hadley Designs sources, vets, and closes top global talent, and you will own the broader people system that talent steps into. You will partner with leadership to design the recruiting engine that consistently delivers strong top-of-funnel for every open role, and you will scale the people systems that hold a remote, contractor-centric organization together as it grows toward $100M and beyond.

 This is a leadership-tier role with 1 direct report (the People Operations Specialist) and end-to-end ownership of the talent and people functions. Your weeks will be heavier on recruiting in the near term, live pipelines, structured interviews, test projects, employer brand, and steady on People Operations throughout (onboarding, performance frameworks, contractor renewal, leadership enablement).

 Key Responsibilities 

 Talent Acquisition (the #1 outcome of this role): 
 • Recruiting Pipeline Management: Source candidates across LinkedIn, job boards, freelancer platforms, and referrals; filter applicants for red flags, competency match, and scorecard alignment.
 • Test Project & Interview Operations: Run test projects, review submissions, conduct first-round group interviews, and manage candidate experience end-to-end.
 • Sourcing Channel Optimization: Manage and optimize sourcing channels based on performance; build "always hiring" shortlists for recurring high-leverage roles.
 • Employer Brand & Glassdoor Defense: Monitor and manage Glassdoor reviews, organize team review drives, ask for feedback, flag issues, protect brand rating.
 • Hiring Metrics & Funnel Reporting: Deliver weekly hiring pipeline reports broken down by channel and role; track funnel performance against KPIs.

 People Operations: 
 • People Systems Leadership: Design and implement systems for engaging, onboarding, and retaining talent, align
 ed with the company's growth objectives.
 • Organizational Design and Capacity Planning: Collaborate with leadership to ensure that the organizational structure and workforce planning meet the evolving needs of the business.
 • Performance and Development Frameworks: Establish performance expectations, evaluation frameworks, and development pathways that drive accountability and growth across the organization.
 • Talent Experience and Retention: Build a consistent and professional experience for talent that reinforces employee engagement, satisfaction, and retention.
 • Workforce Insights and Reporting: Provide insights and data-driven recommendations to leadership to guide decision-making and improve workforce effectiveness.
 • External Partnerships: Partner with external service providers to enhance and support people operations as necessary.

 How Success Is Measured (two bold sub-headers, each with bullets):

 Talent Acquisition KPIs: 
 • Average time to fill open roles: under 45 days.
 • Weekly applicant volume per active role: 250+ qualified applicants.
 • Weekly hiring pipeline report by sourcing channel: 100% completion, on time.
 • Completed candidate case studies available for review per role per week: 15+.
 • Glassdoor company rating: maintain 4.5+ average across the year.

 People Operations KPIs: 
 • Successful implementation of people systems that directly support the business's ability to scale.
 • Strong employee retention rates, with high performance and engagement.
 • Improved leadership confidence in people systems, talent readiness, and organizational alignment.
 • Predictable, scalable people operations that contribute to the company's growth and success.
