Reporting to the CFO, we are hiring a Vice President, Finance to play a key leadership role across Kilmer Group's finance function. As our new Vice President, Finance, you will combine financial stewardship with strategic partnership, helping guide decisions that support the continued growth and evolution of a diversified investment platform. Working closely with the CFO, senior leaders, and investment teams, you will oversee financial reporting, treasury, budgeting, investment portfolio reporting, and governance while providing the financial insight that supports investment decisions, business performance, and long-term value creation. You will lead a finance team and contribute across a broad range of initiatives, from evaluating acquisitions and investments to strengthening reporting, improving processes, and building the financial capabilities and infrastructure needed to support the organization's continued growth.

This is an existing, full-time opportunity based in the Toronto office, working onsite five days per week.

What’s in it for you?

Strategic influence. Reporting directly to the CFO, you will act as a trusted partner to the executive leadership team, contributing financial insight that informs investment decisions, capital allocation, and the long-term direction of Kilmer Group.

Breadth and exposure. This is an opportunity to apply your expertise across a diverse investment portfolio rather than within a single operating business. You will work on initiatives spanning financial reporting, tax, budgeting, long-term forecasting, governance, and business performance.

Build what's next. Technology and AI are transforming the finance function, and Kilmer Group is evolving with it - strengthening reporting, deepening financial analysis, and modernizing our processes to harness these new tools. You will help build new capabilities, grow a high-performing team, and shape a financial foundation built for long-term success.

As our new VP Finance, you will

Lead the finance function.
You will oversee accounting, treasury, financial reporting, and cash management across a complex, multi-entity organization, ensuring strong controls, effective budgeting, and timely, accurate reporting. As a trusted partner to the CFO, you will provide the financial leadership and operational oversight that enables the team to deliver with confidence while supporting the organization's growth objectives.
Provide strategic financial insight.
You will translate financial information into meaningful analysis that supports executive decision-making. Working closely with the CFO and senior leaders, you will develop reporting and insights that strengthen planning, support investment decisions, and provide a clearer understanding of business performance across the organization.
Support investments and corporate growth.
You will partner with the investment team on acquisitions, portfolio reporting, valuations, due diligence, and other strategic initiatives. You will work closely with leaders across Kilmer Group and its portfolio companies, providing financial guidance and building trusted relationships that support long-term value creation.
Lead and develop the team.
You will mentor, coach, and support the continued growth of the finance team while fostering a collaborative, accountable, and low-ego environment. You will build capability and create opportunities for continuous learning amongst the team.

You bring

The leadership.
You have experience leading high-performing finance teams and fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. You are a trusted advisor who can balance strategic priorities with operational execution while building strong relationships across the organization.
The foundation.
You are a CPA, CA with experience gained in both public accounting and industry, ideally including a Big 4 audit environment. You bring strong technical knowledge of ASPE and IFRS, investment holding company accounting, including asset valuations and investee reporting. You have experience with compliance and risk to ensure adherence with tax laws, accounting standards and internal controls. You know how to apply this technical foundation in a commercial environment, combining accounting expertise with sound strategic and business judgment.
The financial expertise.
You bring experience across financial reporting, treasury, budgeting, cash management, tax and corporate governance within complex organizations. You have worked with investment portfolios, valuations, transactions, or corporate development activities and are comfortable partnering with senior leaders to support investment decisions and long-term value creation.
The analytical mindset.
You are naturally curious and continuously look for ways to improve how work gets done. You leverage data and technology to strengthen reporting and decision-making, and you are excited by the opportunity to modernize finance through automation and the thoughtful application of AI.
The communication skills.
You can translate complex financial information into clear recommendations that support decision-making. Whether working with executives, portfolio company leaders, auditors, or external advisors, you build credibility through sound judgment, strong communication, and a collaborative approach.

Why join Kilmer Group?

Today, Kilmer Group continues to build on decades of successful investment and business leadership offering a dynamic and supportive environment with opportunities for growth and development. Beyond our investments, we are committed to strengthening the communities where we live and work through initiatives that support sport, health, research, and community development. Joining Kilmer Group means becoming part of an organization that thinks for the long term, values partnership, and is committed to building a lasting legacy.

Join us

We recognize that no candidate brings every qualification to a role. If your experience is closely aligned with what we are looking for and you are excited by the opportunity to contribute to Kilmer Group, we encourage you to apply. We look forward to learning more about your experience and the perspective you would bring to our team.

What you can expect from our interview process

A virtual interview with a Talent Advisor to discuss your interest in joining Kilmer Group and your experience. The conversation will be recorded using BrightHire, an AI-powered video interview tool. More details will be shared when you are invited to interview.
An in-person conversation with the Chief Financial Officer to discuss your leadership experience, your approach to building high-performing finance functions, and how you partner with executives to support investment decisions and long-term growth.
An in-person presentation and discussion with the Vice President, Talent and Special Projects and a senior member of the finance team. You will be asked to prepare and present a case study, followed by a conversation about your thinking, priorities, and leadership approach.
A final in-person conversation with the Chief Financial Officer to explore mutual fit, discuss your vision for the role, and answer any remaining questions. Finalists may also have the opportunity to meet additional members of the leadership team.

Kilmer Group is committed to creating a workplace where people are treated with respect, supported in their development, and empowered to contribute their best work. We recognize that diverse perspectives strengthen our business and help us make better decisions for our organization, our partners, and the communities in which we operate.

We welcome applications from all qualified candidates and are committed to providing an accessible recruitment process. If you require accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

jobs.title: Director of Data Management and Business Intelligence
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director of Data Management and Business Intelligence based in Canada.

This is a senior leadership opportunity to shape enterprise-wide data strategy, governance, architecture, and business intelligence in a complex, safety-critical environment.

You will establish trusted data foundations that help leaders and operational teams make better, faster decisions.

The role spans aviation operations, MRO, engineering, supply chain, finance, safety, quality, HR, commercial programs, and executive management.

You will lead the evolution of enterprise data platforms, with a strong focus on data quality, integration, security, and scalable BI.

You will also guide advanced analytics and AI initiatives, ensuring they are governed, measurable, and aligned with operational needs.

Working closely with senior stakeholders and multidisciplinary teams, you will build capabilities, develop talent, and drive enterprise adoption.

The role offers broad ownership and the opportunity to directly influence operational readiness, performance, compliance, and long-term growth.

Accountabilities

Define enterprise data strategy: Partner with the CIO and senior leaders to establish a multi-year data management and BI strategy aligned with business priorities, technology roadmaps, investment plans, and operational requirements.
Build the data operating model: Establish clear ownership, stewardship, decision rights, architecture standards, delivery practices, and support responsibilities across corporate and regional teams.
Lead data governance: Develop policies and standards covering data ownership, classification, quality, lineage, retention, residency, access, archival, and acceptable use.
Improve data quality: Establish authoritative data sources, common business definitions, quality controls, issue-management processes, and scorecards across critical operational and corporate data domains.
Protect sensitive information: Work with cybersecurity, legal, privacy, export compliance, quality, and security teams to ensure data is appropriately classified, protected, accessed, and shared.
Shape enterprise data architecture: Define architecture for ingestion, integration, master and reference data, lakehouse or warehouse platforms, semantic models, metadata, reporting, monitoring, and reusable data products.
Modernize data integration: Establish secure integration patterns for ERP, MRO, finance, supply chain, engineering, and other enterprise systems using APIs, event-based interfaces, ETL/ELT pipelines, and controlled data exchange.
Strengthen aviation and MRO data: Lead data remediation and governance for maintenance and ERP environments, improving the integrity of aircraft configuration, component history, maintenance plans, technical records, work orders, defects, and inventory information.
Develop performance intelligence: Lead executive, operational, and functional dashboards and establish consistent performance measures covering fleet readiness, maintenance, supply chain, safety, customers, workforce, programs, and financial performance.
Enable self-service analytics: Build governed data products and semantic models that allow business users to access reliable insights without creating uncontrolled copies of sensitive information.
Advance analytics and AI: Identify and govern use cases including predictive maintenance, component reliability, inventory optimization, demand forecasting, anomaly detection, and program risk monitoring, with appropriate ownership, data quality, human oversight, and security controls.
Lead and develop teams: Build a multidisciplinary organization across data governance, architecture, engineering, BI, and analytics while developing talent, succession plans, and critical capabilities.
Manage vendors and investments: Oversee external partners, technology platforms, budgets, licensing, service levels, risks, and total cost of ownership.
Communicate with leadership: Present data risks, investment priorities, architectural decisions, progress, tradeoffs, and measurable business value clearly to executives and non-technical stakeholders.

Requirements

Education: Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information systems, data engineering, analytics, business, engineering, or a related discipline; a graduate degree or relevant professional certification is an asset.
Leadership experience: At least 10 years of progressive experience across data management, analytics, BI, enterprise applications, or data architecture, including at least five years leading teams or major cross-functional programs.
Industry experience: Experience in aerospace, defense, aviation, MRO, or another highly regulated and asset-intensive industry is strongly preferred.
ERP/MRO expertise: Demonstrated experience improving data quality and reporting within complex ERP or MRO environments; experience with Ramco is a significant asset, while comparable aviation or enterprise platforms are also relevant.
International experience: Experience operating across multiple countries, legal entities, or security domains, particularly Canada and the United States, is preferred.
Data expertise: Strong knowledge of enterprise data architecture, dimensional and semantic modeling, master data management, metadata, data quality, lineage, SQL, APIs, and ETL/ELT integration.
Cloud and BI technologies: Hands-on understanding of modern cloud data platforms and BI solutions; experience with Microsoft Fabric, Azure, Power BI, and related Microsoft data services is preferred.
Aviation data knowledge: Familiarity with maintenance and supply-chain data, including serialized components, aircraft configuration, maintenance planning, technical records, reliability, and inventory transactions.
Regulatory knowledge: Familiarity with aviation regulatory and quality environments such as Transport Canada, FAA, EASA, safety management systems, and AS9100 is an asset.
Security and compliance: Working knowledge of information classification, access control, auditability, privacy, data residency, the Canadian Controlled Goods Program, ITAR/EAR, CUI safeguards, CMMC, and NIST SP 800-171 as applicable.
Security eligibility: Ability to obtain and maintain the security clearances, controlled-goods eligibility, and customer or program authorizations required for the position.
Business leadership: Strong judgment connecting data investments to safety, operational readiness, contract delivery, customer commitments, and financial performance.
Communication: Ability to explain data limitations, security requirements, architectural decisions, and complex technical concepts to executives, operational leaders, technical specialists, and front-line users.
Program management: Proven ability to manage priorities, budgets, vendors, dependencies, risks, and organizational change in complex environments.
Collaboration: Strong influencing and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work effectively across multidisciplinary teams without relying solely on formal authority.
Languages: Professional fluency in English is required; French and additional languages are considered assets.

Benefits

Full-time, remote position based in Canada.
Flexible work schedule.
Attractive benefits package.
Opportunities for professional development and career growth.
Multidisciplinary and multicultural collaboration across local and international teams.
Opportunity to work on enterprise-level data, BI, analytics, and AI initiatives with significant operational impact.
A collaborative environment emphasizing service, integrity, excellence, and teamwork.
Role requiring Level II Canadian government security clearance and eligibility for the Canadian Controlled Goods Program.

jobs.title: Chief Transformation Officer
jobs.description:
Chief Transformation Officer (CTO)Job Description Position:         Chief Transformation Officer (CTO) Reports to:  Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
Status:            Senior Leadership Position
Scope:            National transformation, digital platforms, innovation and modernisation

Position Purpose The Chief Transformation Officer (CTO) is a senior leadership role responsible for leading Lifesaving Society Canada’s transformation agenda and converting strategic priorities into sustainable national operating capabilities. The CTO will oversee VITA (CRM), artificial intelligence, the digital landscape and training manuals, virtual training, and related transformation initiatives. The position reports to the CEO, operates with significant delegated authority, manages related budgets and vendors, and works across the Board of Directors, Management Team, Branches, committees and external partners.
Leadership Mandate • Provide enterprise-wide leadership for LSC transformation initiatives, ensuring projects are coordinated, prioritized, resourced and aligned with LSC’s strategic direction, programs and delivery models.
•  Act independently within approved authority, escalating matters to the CEO or Board when they involve material strategic, financial, policy, privacy, security or reputational implications.
• Translate transformation strategy into clear roadmaps, implementation plans, governance structures, budgets, milestones, accountabilities and measurable outcomes.
•  Serve as a bridge between national strategy and practical implementation across the National Office and provincial Branches.

Key Accountabilities 1.  Transformation Strategy and Portfolio Leadership • Lead and coordinate LSC’s transformation portfolio, including VITA, AI, development, digital-resource modernization and virtual training.
• Establish integrated roadmaps, priorities, dependencies, milestones, risk controls and performance measures across transformation initiatives to include the subscription model.
• Identify opportunities to improve service delivery, operational efficiency, user experience, scalability, national consistency and revenue sustainability.
• Prepare recommendations, business cases and decision materials for the CEO, Management Team, Board and committees.
• Ensure transformation work reflects LSC’s national structure, Branch realities, program standards and delivery model.
2.  VITA (CRM) Platform Leadership • Provide national operational ownership and product coordination for VITA through implementation, stabilization and ongoing evolution.
• Manage the VITA scope baseline, roadmap, backlog, release calendar, gap register and national decision log.
• Lead the relationship with the platform developer/vendor and other service providers, including requirements clarification, delivery coordination, issue escalation, defect management, testing, acceptance criteria, service performance and documentation.
• Coordinate Branch readiness, migration, launch planning, hyper-care, training, issue triage, adoption monitoring and communication with Branch VITA Leads and Data Stewards.
• Maintain disciplined national change management for requests affecting shared data, workflows, permissions, reporting, integrations, configuration, scope and cross-Branch operations.
• Coordinate data governance and reporting, including data definitions, controlled values, data-quality measures, duplicate-management rules, reporting definitions and dashboard-access governance.
• Oversee VITA policies, business rules, user guides, role-based training materials, Branch toolkits, job aids, FAQs, release communications and other adoption resources.
• Ensure access and permissions are governed through an approved role-permission model, appropriate authorization, periodic review and segregation-of-duties controls; the CTO is accountable for business governance of access, not unrestricted technical control by a single individual.
• Coordinate privacy, security and compliance processes with the designated privacy/compliance resource and ensure risks are appropriately identified and escalated.
• Develop costed recommendations for post-implementation enhancements, support, staffing, funding and the long-term role of VITA in LSC’s digital architecture.
3.  Artificial Intelligence • Develop and lead an LSC approach to responsible AI adoption that supports operations, program delivery, service quality and organizational capacity.
• Identify, assess and prioritize practical AI use cases, including opportunities to streamline work, improve knowledge access and support decision-making.
• Establish appropriate governance, risk, privacy, security, human oversight and change-management practices for AI use.
• Build organizational AI literacy through guidance, training and practical support for staff and volunteers.
• Monitor emerging AI capabilities and recommend investments, pilots and policies appropriate to LSC.
5.  Digital Landscape and Training Resources • Lead the development of an integrated digital landscape for access to LSC resources and manuals.
• Oversee approaches to digital access, permissions, security, fees, version control and distribution of training and operational resources.
• Work with program leaders and Branches to ensure digital resources are current, accessible, practical and aligned with national standards.
• Identify opportunities to reduce duplication and improve the discoverability and management of national digital content.
6.  Virtual Training and Online Learning • Lead the development and expansion of virtual training and future online course offerings.
• Coordinate platform requirements, online registration, fee models, learner experience, training resources and operational support.
7.  Governance, Stakeholder and Change Leadership • Work   directly   with    the   CEO,  Board   of    Directors,   Management  Team,  Branches, commissions/committees and project groups on transformation priorities.
• Prepare clear reports, recommendations, dashboards, risk updates and decision materials for governance and management audiences.
• Maintain appropriate governance artifacts, including RACI/accountability frameworks, risk and issue registers, change logs, decision logs, policies, SOPs and project records.
• Lead organizational change, communications, training and adoption activities so that new systems and operating models are understood and used effectively.
• Build strong working relationships across LSC while respecting Branch operational responsibilities and national standards.
8.  Financial, Vendor and Resource Management • Develop and manage budgets for the transformation portfolio and its component initiatives.
• Monitor expenditures, forecasts, contracts and financial performance; identify variances and recommend corrective action.
• Lead procurement and vendor/service-provider relationships within delegated authority, with clear deliverables, service expectations and accountability.
• Assess resource and staffing requirements and recommend sustainable operating models for transformation functions.
• Ensure projects have realistic costs, timelines, ownership, risk controls and measures of success.

Qualifications and Experience • Progressive leadership experience in organizational transformation, digital modernization, technology-enabled service delivery, operations or a related field.
• Experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives involving multiple stakeholders, competing priorities and organizational change.
• Experience with CRM or enterprise platforms, vendor management, implementation, stabilization and continuous improvement.
• Experience developing and managing budgets, business cases, contracts and multi-year investment plans.
• Working knowledge of AI opportunities, governance and responsible adoption in an organizational setting.
• Experience working with senior management, boards, committees and governance processes.
• A relevant post-secondary credential or an equivalent combination of education and senior-level experience.
• Demonstrated knowledge of Lifesaving Society Canada, its programs, national/Branch delivery model and stakeholder environment is preferred.
• Knowledge of French, both written and spoken, is an asset.

Core Competencies • Strategic leadership: connects long-term direction to practical execution and measurable outcomes.
• Independent judgement: makes sound decisions within delegated authority and knows when escalation is required.
• Transformation leadership: leads people, process and technology change across complex stakeholder environments.
• Program and project leadership: manages interdependent initiatives, risks, timelines, resources and decisions.
• Relationship management: builds trust with the Board, Management Team, Branches, committees, vendors and partners.
• Financial acumen: develop budgets, evaluates investments and manages resources responsibly.
• Digital and data literacy: understands CRM, digital platforms, data governance, AI and online service delivery.
• Communication and change leadership: explains complex issues clearly and builds readiness, training and adoption.

Key Relationships • Internal: CEO; Board of Directors; Management Team; National Office staff; provincial Branches; commissions, committees and project teams.
• External: technology vendors and developers; consultants; service providers; training and digital partners; other stakeholders as assigned.

Initial Priorities • Assume leadership of the remaining VITA implementation, transition and stabilization work, with a structured handover from current project leadership.
• Confirm an integrated transformation roadmap, governance framework, budget and reporting cadence across VITA, AI, digital resources and virtual training.
• Establish clear decision rights, risk controls, vendor accountability and Branch engagement mechanisms for transformation initiatives.
• Develop practical recommendations for the long-term operating model and resource requirements
for LSC’s transformation portfolio.

 Negotiates loan structures and terms and conditions that align client requirements with the bank risk appetite and policies.

 Evaluates portfolio performance and recommends capital allocation strategies that optimize returns with investment objectives.
 Leads proposal development and delivers presentations to capture new business and expand client relationships.
 Networks with industry contacts to gather competitive insights and best practices.
 Develops and executes business development plans focused on enhancing client relationships and growth opportunities within the portfolio.
 Builds and maintains client relationships to ensure long-term financial performance in collaboration with Relationship Manager and business partners.

jobs.description:
**Discover your future at Citi**
--------------------------------


Working at Citi is far more than just a job. A career with us means joining a team of approximately 219,000 dedicated people from around the globe. At Citi, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your career, give back to your community and make a real impact.


**Job Overview**
----------------


Citi is looking for a Senior Java Developer to take technical ownership of business\-critical Credit Risk and Capital Markets platforms, driving the modernization of large\-scale systems into resilient, cloud\-native architectures. In this Vice President\-level role, you will operate as a senior individual contributor and technical leader — shaping engineering standards, guiding platform evolution, and delivering high\-impact solutions across a globally distributed team. If you bring deep Java expertise, Capital Markets domain knowledge, and a drive to solve complex engineering challenges at scale, this role offers the scope and influence to make a real difference**.**


**Responsibilities**
--------------------


* Design and deliver high\-performance, enterprise\-scale Credit Risk and Capital Markets systems across the full software development lifecycle, from architecture through production deployment.
* Lead the re\-engineering of complex, monolithic applications into modern, cloud\-native microservices, ensuring scalability, resilience, and regulatory compliance at every stage.
* Define and drive architectural decisions for platform modernization initiatives, including cloud migration and the adoption of distributed data processing technologies.
* Build and sustain low\-latency, highly available systems that meet enterprise\-grade standards for security, performance, and operational stability.
* Partner with a global team of software engineers, business analysts, DevOps, and support functions to deliver quality solutions across Capital Markets and Risk domains.
* Mentor and develop mid\-level and junior engineers, raising engineering standards and enabling the team to consistently deliver production\-grade solutions.
* Evaluate and integrate emerging technologies — including AI\-assisted development tooling — to improve engineering efficiency and delivery quality.

**Required Qualifications \& Skills**
-------------------------------------


* 6\+ years of experience in application development or systems analysis, with a track record of delivering large\-scale, complex technology initiatives.
* Deep expertise in Core Java, including object\-oriented design principles, concurrent and multi\-threaded programming, JVM memory management, and performance tuning.
* Hands\-on experience re\-engineering monolithic applications into microservices architectures, and deploying containerised workloads using Docker and Kubernetes.
* Practical knowledge of distributed systems and data processing frameworks such as Apache Flink, alongside distributed caching technologies such as Redis, Oracle Coherence, or GridGain.
* Database experience spanning relational platforms (preferably Oracle) and NoSQL technologies (preferably MongoDB), with the ability to design for scale and reliability.
* Proven domain knowledge in Capital Markets, including Derivatives, Credit Risk, and Risk Management, with experience supporting risk\-sensitive, business\-critical platforms.
* Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related STEM discipline, or equivalent practical experience in a comparable role.

**Beneficial Skills \& Qualifications**
---------------------------------------


* Experience with SDLC and DevOps tooling including Git, Bitbucket, Jenkins, SonarQube, and JIRA, with familiarity in secure coding practices.
* Familiarity with Linux and Unix environments, including scripting for automation and operational tasks.
* Experience using AI\-assisted development tools such as GitHub Copilot or Devin to accelerate engineering delivery.
* Recognised subject matter expertise in one or more areas of application development, with a demonstrated ability to influence architectural and strategic decisions at a senior level.

**What We Offer**
-----------------


At Citi, you will work at the intersection of technology and financial markets, contributing to platforms that directly support global Capital Markets operations. This is a senior role with real ownership, strategic influence, and the opportunity to shape how critical systems are built and modernised across a high\-performing global engineering team.


* Hybrid working model with 3 days in the office and 2 days working remotely, giving you flexibility alongside meaningful in\-person collaboration.
* Opportunity to lead technically significant, franchise\-critical initiatives with direct impact on Credit Risk and Capital Markets infrastructure at global scale.
* Access to continuous learning and professional development resources to deepen both technical and domain expertise.
* A performance\-driven environment where senior engineers have genuine influence over architectural direction and technology strategy.
* Competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your financial wellbeing and long\-term career growth.
* Wellbeing support and work\-life balance initiatives, backed by programmes tailored to the needs of experienced technology professionals.

Apply now to bring your Java engineering expertise to one of the world's leading financial institutions and take technical ownership of platforms that matter**.**

jobs.description:
About the AGCO

Established in 1998, the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO) is an Ontario provincial regulatory agency reporting to the Ministry of the Attorney General (MAG). The AGCO is responsible for regulating the alcohol, gaming and horse racing sectors and cannabis retail in accordance with the principles of honesty and integrity, and in the public interest. In so doing, the AGCO administers a range of Acts including Liquor Licence , Gaming Control, Horse Racing and Cannabis Licence.

The vision of the AGCO is to be a world-class regulator that is innovative, proactive, and socially responsible and regulate in accordance with the principles of honesty and integrity, and in the public interest.

Over the years, the AGCO under the spotlight of an expanding regulatory role has reinforced its commitment to ensure a framework of critical regulatory controls, digital data and corresponding reports are in place to ensure both public interest and the economic viability of the alcohol, gaming, horse racing, and cannabis industries. It is expected that the need for digital data as a business enabler is expected to intensify to align with AGCO’s expanded regulatory role.

Define the Future

As a result of this commitment to a digital business environment the AGCO has enhanced the mandate for the Director of Enterprise Data and Analytics
. This position will report directly to the CIO, be a key member of the information technology leadership team and will be responsiblefor building and leading a small and high-performing team responsible for an enterprise-wide program for data governance, data management and data analytics.

In this key role you will not only lead the design and oversee the adoption of the data governance framework but, you will also use your expertise across the data lifecycle to champion the view of data as an asset and a source of insights for critical decisions. You and your team will be responsible for data governance, data operations, data quality through advanced and explorative analytics that will improve trust in our data and increase speed to insight and business decision making.

Key Accountabilities include five key domains as follows:

Data Strategy and Governance

Develop a strategic vision and roadmap for implementing data and analytics governance standards, data management process and advanced data analytics across the enterprise that encourages innovation and enables business outcomes and opportunities while managing risk.
Development of policies around security, privacy, life cycle, quality and definitions and models
Define an approach for data governance, including KPIs and reporting, to ensure that data used across the enterprise is appropriately managed and supports business outcomes.
Identify potential areas where existing policies, processes, controls, and tools require change or need to be developed to ensure data objectives are met and to support evolving business needs

Relationship Management & Business Strategy Infused with Data

Work with Lines of Business to define what matters to the enterprise and the business outcomes that is important to them.
Develop and execute a communication plan to build awareness and adoption of the data governance and data management standards across the enterprise.
Build partnerships across all levels of the organization and affect change through leadership.
Provide subject matter expertise related to data governance, data management including the creation and management of data pipelines as well as advanced analytics to all business lines across the enterprise.
Build a team to support the notion of data as a business enabler, while building relationship with business, advocating data and finding a mandate for data.

Data Operations

Provide subject matter expertise related to data management including the creation and management of data pipelines as well as advanced analytics to all business lines across the enterprise.
Manage the data operations and data quality functions to ensure data is properly governed with appropriate policies, processes and standards including supporting documentation.
Identify potential areas where existing policies, processes, controls, and tools require change or need to be developed to ensure data objectives are met and to support evolving business needs.

Analytics and Insights

Work directly with client stakeholders to translate business problems into high level analytics solution designs using the latest data science techniques.
Build a team to support the notion of data as a business enable, while building relationship with business, advocating data and finding a mandate for data.
Lead and participate in discussions with your team to select and apply relevant analytic techniques and create actionable business insights.
Present analytic solutions to business audiences highlighting robustness of the solution and how it could help generate business value.
Make presentations to senior management, business teams, and develop plans to help operationalize analytic solutions.

People Leadership

Manage a small high-performing team of data professionals including establishing performance targets, developing their skills and capabilities to meet the needs of the organization, as well as building on existing recruiting capabilities to address new needs and skills gaps.

Ideal Experience

Management Experience:
ten (10) or more years of experience in an information technology leadership capacity, with at least five years in a senior management role with significant experience in data governance, data management and data analytics.
Strategic Orientation:
A track record as a strategic and innovative thinker with an ability to translate vision into outcomes while fostering a positive and innovative workplace.
Collaboration and Engagement:
Proven track record of building partnerships and influencing a diverse set of stakeholders (including C-level) to drive outcomes.
People Leadership:
Experience and ability to provide exceptional leadership to staff and to build enthusiastic, high performing staffteams while focusing on strategic issues.
Data Requirements:
Ability to quickly understand the data requirements of disparate business stakeholders across the enterprise with varying levels of technology sophistication.
Data Architecture:
Knowledge of data modeling, architecture principles and techniques is an an advantage.
Data Governance:
Strong understanding and practical experience with the application of data governance to be a value-add to the business decision making function.
Data Management:
Exceptional critical thinking skills and experience as it relates to data lifecycle management which includes data ingestion, data quality and management.
Advanced Data Analytics:
Experience with designing performance management mechanisms through the use of reporting dashboards and advanced analytics that are effective in driving business outcomes and intuitive for the audience.
Program Management:
Ability to manage multiple concurrent projects/initiatives, objectives, groups or activities.
Communications:
Excellent verbal, written, and presentation skills. Able to engage with stakeholders at all levels across the enterprise with succinctness and clarity of thought.
Education and Professional Designations:
A bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science and Analytics, Engineering, Finance. A MBA or masters level education is an asset.

Benefits of working for the AGCO

Compensation + additional incentives
– $142,113 to $177,639 (under review) plus a pay for performance bonus up to ten percent.
Benefits –
a robust employer paid benefits package, a defined benefits pension plan through the Ontario Pension Board, discounted underground parking.
Flexible Hours of work
– while the AGCO has transitioned to an in-office work environment the AGCO does offer flexible work hours to accommodate work life balance.
Location
– conveniently located within blocks of the subway at Yonge and Sheppard in Toronto.

How to Apply

quoting project AGCO-DA2. Should you wish to speak to our Executive Recruiter please contact Jon Stungevicius at 416-214-9299 x1, jon@waterhousesearch.net.

The Director of Data Management and Business Intelligence leads the enterprise data function for Top Aces. Reporting to the Chief Information Officer, the Director defines how data is governed, integrated, protected, and used across aviation operations, maintenance and engineering, supply chain, finance, safety, quality, human resources, commercial programs, and executive management.

The role will establish trusted enterprise data products and decision-ready analytics while respecting aviation record integrity, contractual obligations, export controls, data residency, and need-to-know access. A central priority is to improve the quality and usability of data from Ramco and connected systems so that leaders and front-line teams can manage aircraft availability, maintenance execution, material readiness, program performance, and financial results with greater confidence.

Top Aces Business Context

Top Aces provides advanced operational training and aircraft sustainment services to Canada, the United States, NATO members, and allied nations. The company operates globally in a safety-critical and security-sensitive environment that combines flight operations, maintenance and repair, engineering, supply chain, training, and proprietary technology. The data environment therefore requires strong governance across business units, legal entities, jurisdictions, and security domains.

The Director will translate these operating realities into an enterprise data strategy that supports growth, operational readiness, regulatory compliance, and disciplined investment. The role must balance standardization with the access boundaries required for Canadian, U.S., and international programs.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Data Strategy and Operating Model

Partner with the CIO to develop and execute a multi-year enterprise data and BI strategy aligned with Top Aces' business strategy, operating model, technology roadmap, and investment priorities.
Create a practical data operating model that defines decision rights, ownership, stewardship, architecture standards, delivery methods, and support responsibilities across corporate and regional teams.
Chair or support the enterprise data governance council and maintain a prioritized roadmap based on operational value, regulatory risk, data quality, and delivery capacity.
Partner with the CIO and U.S. IT and security leadership to establish appropriate data segregation, access controls, and technology control plans for FOCI-related and export-controlled environments, where applicable.

Data Governance Quality and Protection

Establish enterprise policies and standards for data ownership, classification, quality, lineage, retention, archival, residency, access, and acceptable use.
Define authoritative sources and common business terms for critical domains, including aircraft, fleets, components, serialized parts, maintenance programs, work orders, defects, inventory, suppliers, customers, contracts, personnel, and financial dimensions.
Implement data quality controls, issue-management workflows, and scorecards that identify root causes and assign corrective action to accountable data owners.
Work with Cybersecurity, Legal, Export Compliance, Privacy, Quality, and program security personnel to protect personal, proprietary, controlled, and customer information throughout its lifecycle.
Ensure analytics and data-sharing practices comply with applicable contractual clauses, the Canadian Controlled Goods Program, ITAR and EAR requirements, privacy laws, and customer security obligations.

Data Architecture Integration and Platforms

Define the target enterprise data architecture, including ingestion, integration, master and reference data, lakehouse or warehouse services, semantic models, reporting, metadata, and monitoring.
Establish integration patterns and data contracts for Ramco and other enterprise platforms using secure APIs, event-based interfaces, ETL or ELT pipelines, and controlled file exchange where required.
Reduce duplicate datasets and spreadsheet-dependent reporting by creating reusable, governed data products and certified semantic models.
Set engineering standards for observability, reconciliation, change control, testing, performance, resilience, backup, and recovery across the data platform.
Manage the data-platform lifecycle, capacity, licensing, vendor performance, and total cost of ownership, with particular attention to Microsoft Fabric, Azure data services, Power BI, and connected technologies.

Aviation and MRO Data

Lead data remediation and governance for Ramco MRO and ERP, focusing on master data, transactional integrity, usability, reporting structures, and interfaces with finance, supply chain, engineering, and flight operations.
Partner with Maintenance, Engineering, Airworthiness, Quality, Supply Chain, and Operations to improve the completeness and consistency of aircraft configuration, component history, flight hours and cycles, maintenance plans, work packages, defects, technical records, and inventory data.
Preserve the integrity and auditability of approved maintenance and airworthiness records while enabling controlled downstream analytics.
Develop trusted measures for aircraft availability, dispatch reliability, mission-capable status, maintenance schedule compliance, turnaround time, component reliability, inventory availability, and aircraft-on-ground events.
Support data readiness for operational and regulatory audits, customer reporting, contract performance reviews, and fleet-planning decisions.

Business Intelligence and Performance Management

Lead the design and delivery of executive, operational, and functional dashboards using consistent definitions, clear ownership, and traceable data sources.
Build an enterprise performance framework that connects mission delivery, safety, fleet readiness, maintenance, supply chain, program, customer, workforce, and financial measures.
Develop governed self-service analytics so business users can answer routine questions without creating uncontrolled copies of sensitive data.
Improve forecasting and scenario analysis for fleet utilization, maintenance demand, materials, labour capacity, contract delivery, revenue, cash flow, and program profitability.
Maintain a transparent intake and prioritization process for BI requests, balancing regulatory deadlines, operational urgency, enterprise reuse, and expected value.

Advanced Analytics and Artificial Intelligence

Identify and govern analytics and AI use cases such as predictive maintenance, component reliability, inventory optimization, demand forecasting, anomaly detection, and program risk monitoring.
Require documented business ownership, suitable data quality, human oversight, security review, and measurable benefits before analytics or AI solutions move into production.
Coordinate with engineering, operations, and technology teams when operational, training, mission-system, or live and synthetic data may be used, ensuring the work remains within approved classification and authorization boundaries.
Monitor model performance, data drift, access, and business outcomes, and retire solutions that no longer meet operational, security, or financial requirements.

Leadership and Stakeholder Partnership

Build and lead a capable team spanning data governance, architecture, engineering, BI, and analytics; define roles, develop talent, and manage succession for critical skills.
Partner with executives and functional leaders to convert business questions into governed data products, clear measures, and practical decisions.
Create an active network of business data owners and stewards and hold regular reviews of quality, adoption, access, and value realization.
Manage external partners and vendors through clear outcomes, architecture standards, service levels, security requirements, and commercial accountability.
Communicate data risks, progress, tradeoffs, and investment needs to senior leadership in concise business terms.

Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree in computer science, information systems, data engineering, analytics, business, engineering, or a related discipline. A graduate degree or relevant professional certification is an asset.
At least 10 years of progressive experience in data management, analytics, BI, enterprise applications, or data architecture, including at least five years leading teams or major cross-functional programs.
Experience in aerospace, defense, aviation, MRO, or another highly regulated and asset-intensive industry is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated experience improving data quality and reporting in a complex ERP or MRO environment. Direct experience with Ramco is a significant asset; experience with comparable aviation or enterprise platforms is also relevant.
Experience operating across multiple countries, legal entities, or security domains, including Canada and the United States, is preferred.

Technical and Regulatory Knowledge

Strong knowledge of enterprise data architecture, dimensional and semantic modelling, master data management, metadata, data quality, lineage, SQL, APIs, and ETL or ELT integration.
Hands-on understanding of modern cloud data platforms and BI technologies. Experience with Microsoft Fabric, Azure, Power BI, and Microsoft data services is preferred.
Working knowledge of aviation maintenance and supply-chain data, including serialized components, configuration, maintenance planning, technical records, reliability, and inventory transactions.
Familiarity with aviation regulatory and quality environments such as Transport Canada, FAA, EASA, safety management systems, and AS9100 is an asset.
Working knowledge of information classification, access control, auditability, privacy, data residency, the Canadian Controlled Goods Program, ITAR and EAR, CUI safeguards, CMMC, and NIST SP 800-171, as applicable to the role and programs supported.
Ability to obtain and maintain the security clearances, controlled-goods eligibility, and customer or program authorizations required for the position.

Leadership Competencies

Business judgment that connects data investment to safety, mission readiness, contract delivery, customer commitments, and financial performance.
Ability to influence executives, operational leaders, technical specialists, and front-line users without relying solely on formal authority.
Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain data limitations, security constraints, and architectural decisions to non-technical audiences.
Disciplined program leadership, with practical experience managing priorities, budgets, vendors, risks, and organizational change.
Commitment to Top Aces' values of Service, Integrity, Excellence, and Together.
Professional fluency in English is required. French and additional languages us

jobs.description:
Come... Enjoy... Work
in a fast paced, dynamic environment. Located on the Tsuut’ina First Nation, Grey Eagle Resort & Casino is Calgary’s number one entertainment facility. We are looking for talented, energetic and motivated individuals to join our diverse workforce! We offer competitive salaries, benefits and opportunities to grow your career.

Position Overview

The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is a key executive leader responsible for the financial stewardship, strategic planning, governance support, and long-term sustainability of Grey Eagle Resort & Casino (GERC).

Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the CFO serves as the principal financial advisor to the Board and Executive Leadership Team, providing leadership across financial operations, capital investment planning, enterprise risk management, business growth initiatives, and stakeholder relations.

The CFO plays a critical role in supporting the Board's vision for sustainable economic growth while protecting and enhancing the assets of Grey Eagle Resort & Casino for future generations of the Tsuut'ina Nation.

The role oversees all financial functions and provides executive leadership for major capital projects, resort renovations, business development initiatives, financing strategies, and governance matters affecting the organization.

As one of the most senior leaders within GERC, the CFO must balance strategic thinking, operational understanding, financial discipline, and relationship-building with a diverse group of stakeholders including the Board of Directors, Tsuut'ina Nation leadership, regulators, financial institutions, development partners, and operational leaders.

Education And Experience

CPA designation.
Bachelor's Degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, or related discipline.
Minimum 10 years progressive financial leadership experience.
Minimum 5 years in a senior executive role.
Experience in hospitality, gaming, resort, entertainment, tourism, real estate development, or similarly complex operations.
Experience reporting directly to a Board of Directors.
Experience leading major capital projects exceeding $10M.
Demonstrated success managing banking and financing relationships.

Preferred

MBA or Master's Degree.
Experience working with Indigenous-owned organizations, governments, or economic development entities.
Experience in a regulated gaming environment.
Experience supporting Board committees and governance functions.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Strategic Leadership & Board Support

Serve as the primary financial advisor to the Board of Directors.
Provide recommendations on strategic initiatives, capital investments, financing structures, business growth opportunities, and organizational performance.
Prepare and present comprehensive financial and operational reports to the Board.
Support the Board in strategic planning and long-term sustainability initiatives.
Participate in governance discussions and provide financial guidance regarding organizational priorities.
Assist the Board in evaluating significant business opportunities, acquisitions, partnerships, and development projects.

Financial Leadership & Stewardship

Lead all aspects of financial management and reporting.
Develop and execute financial strategies aligned with organizational goals.
Oversee:
Budgeting, Forecasting, Financial Reporting
Treasury Management, Cash Flow Management
Internal Controls
Tax Compliance
Audit Functions
Capital Planning
Ensure financial integrity and accountability throughout the organization.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators and financial metrics.

________________________________________

Capital Projects, Renovation & Development Oversight

The CFO will provide executive leadership for capital investment planning and project governance across the resort.

Responsibilities Include

Develop long-term capital investment strategies.
Oversee financial planning and governance for renovation and expansion projects.
Lead financial evaluation and business case development for all major capital expenditures.
Monitor project budgets, timelines, risks, and return on investment.
Ensure appropriate project controls and reporting mechanisms are in place.

________________________________________

Master Site Development Planning

Participate in long-term master planning for Grey Eagle Resort & Casino lands and facilities.
Evaluate future development opportunities through financial modeling and strategic analysis.
Support land use planning, phased development initiatives, and infrastructure investment decisions.
Provide financial leadership related to future resort expansion opportunities.
Collaborate with Nation leadership, developers, consultants, and external advisors regarding future growth initiatives.

________________________________________

Banking, Financing & Capital Structure Management

Lead relationships with financial institutions and lending partners.
Develop financing strategies to support operational and capital requirements.
Negotiate banking agreements, credit facilities, and financing arrangements.
Manage cash reserves and liquidity planning.
Advise the Board regarding capital structure optimization and debt management strategies.

________________________________________

Hotel Asset Management & Resort Performance

Provide strategic oversight regarding the financial performance of hotel and resort assets.
Evaluate asset performance and investment priorities.
Support lifecycle planning for hotel, gaming, entertainment, and food & beverage facilities.
Monitor asset utilization and return on investment.
Develop recommendations regarding reinvestment and asset enhancement opportunities.

________________________________________

Casino Reinvestment Strategy

Develop and maintain a long-term casino reinvestment strategy.
Assess gaming floor performance and capital replacement needs.
Support strategic decisions regarding gaming technology and facility improvements.
Ensure reinvestment planning aligns with market conditions and guest expectations.
Evaluate opportunities to enhance competitiveness and profitability.

________________________________________

iGaming Strategy, Financial Oversight & Business Development

Provide executive financial leadership for the establishment, launch, growth, and ongoing financial performance of GERC's iGaming business unit.
Lead financial modelling, budgeting, forecasting, capital planning, and business-case evaluation related to iGaming operations and strategic initiatives.
Establish and oversee appropriate financial reporting, revenue assurance, reconciliation, treasury, payment processing, settlement, and internal control frameworks for iGaming activities.
Develop and monitor key iGaming performance indicators, including Gross Gaming Revenue (GGR), Net Gaming Revenue (NGR), gaming margins, customer acquisition costs, promotional and bonus costs, player value, deposits and withdrawals, chargebacks, operating costs, and profitability.
Work collaboratively with iGaming leadership, Compliance, Legal, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Marketing, and Operations to ensure appropriate financial governance and risk management.
Ensure financial processes, controls, reporting, and recordkeeping support applicable regulatory requirements and GERC's obligations to Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis (AGLC) and the Alberta iGaming Corporation (AiGC).
Provide financial oversight of banking arrangements, payment service providers, gaming technology providers, platform vendors, and other significant iGaming commercial relationships.
Evaluate future iGaming products, partnerships, technology investments, and business expansion opportunities from a financial and strategic perspective.

Ensure transparency, accountability, and value-for-money principles.
Develop policies and controls supporting major purchasing initiatives.
Participate in evaluation and approval processes for significant contracts and vendor relationships.
Ensure procurement activities align with Board-approved financial policies.

Support initiatives that align with the Nation's economic development goals.
Identify opportunities for strategic partnerships that advance organizational objectives.
Participate in partnership discussions with Indigenous and non-Indigenous organizations.

BOARD FINANCE & AUDIT COMMITTEE SUPPORT

jobs.title: Senior Procurement Specialist, AVP Strategy Enterprise Comm
jobs.description:
Description

Supply Chain Management
within AVP Strategy Enterprise Comm
is currently seeking 2 Full-time Limited Term Senior Procurement Specialists
for approximately 12 months with the potential for extension.

Reporting to leadership within Supply Chain Management, the Senior Procurement Specialist is responsible for procuring materials, supplies, equipment and services in the most cost-effective manner and compliant manner for the University. The role requires strong collaboration skills and a commitment to delivering high-quality customer service to a diverse group of campus stakeholders. This position works closely with members of the Supply Chain Management team including Procurement Services, Card & Supplier Services, Distribution Services, as well as with internal clients across the institution. The Senior Procurement Specialist operates in a dynamic, high-volume, and complex environment and must effectively manage competing priorities and deadlines.

Summary of Key Responsibilities
(job functions include but are not limited to):

Strategic Sourcing, Contracting and Supplier Management

Oversee the preparation and execution of competitive procurement documents (e.g., RFQs, RFPs, tenders), ensuring compliance with the University's policies, government regulations, and applicable trade agreements and legislation.
Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the University's contractual and sourcing requirements, providing expert guidance on complex and high risk procurement activities.
Lead supplier interviews, negotiations, and debriefs to enhance supplier performance, address service issues, and support the development of new or strategic sources of supply.
Lead the identification and implementation of cost saving, value creation, and process improvement initiatives that support institutional objectives and total cost management principles.

Procurement Governance, Risk and Compliance Advisory

Provide expert advisory support on procurement governance and risk by interpreting and applying institutional policies, trade agreements (e.g., CFTA, CETA, NWPTA), and public sector procurement requirements, and by guiding internal stakeholders on appropriate sourcing strategies for complex, high value, or sensitive procurements.
Support institutional compliance and research funding requirements by advising on procurement approaches related to research, scientific, and externally funded initiatives (e.g., grant funded or CFI funded projects), ensuring alignment with sponsor conditions, audit expectations, and university governance frameworks.
Provide senior level advisory support to internal stakeholders by reviewing, analyzing, and evaluating competitive submissions, quotations, and tenders, and by facilitating evaluation processes and consensus based award recommendations.

Capability Building and Continuous Improvement

jobs.title: Field Chief Technology Officer - North America East
jobs.description:
1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $400M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing. 

 About 1Password 
 At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work. 

 If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future. 

 Technical authority and commercial judgement create the bridge between architecture and business outcomes. As a 1Password Field Chief Technology Officer (Field CTO), you’ll help the world’s largest organizations navigate that bridge while shaping the future of enterprise identity security.
 The Field CTO is the most senior customer-facing technical advisor within the 1Password Solutions Engineering organization. You’ll influence enterprise technology leaders, accelerate adoption of the 1Password platform and help define how modern organizations secure every sign-in to every application from every device, including AI agents.
 You’ll partner with executive buyers, enterprise architects, developers and security practitioners to solve some of the industry’s most complex identity and access challenges. You’ll engage in our most strategic customer opportunities, represent 1Password in executive briefings, customer advisory boards, industry events and executive forums, and serve as a trusted advisor to Product, Engineering and GTM leadership. You’ll focus your efforts where executive technical leadership can materially influence customer outcomes, while transforming those experiences into repeatable technical motions that scale across the broader Solutions Engineering organization.
 Beyond customer engagement, you’ll help scale the technical capabilities of the entire Solutions Engineering organization. You’ll transform customer insights into repeatable playbooks, mentor senior Solutions Engineers, influence product direction and establish technical strategies that improve how we engage enterprise customers around the world.

 How we’re using AI today 
 Across GTM, we’re transforming the way we work with AI. We expect every seller, CSM, and team member to become a power user, using it daily to work smarter and move faster. AI is already embedded in how we operate – from real-time coaching that sharpens how we sell and interact with customers, to surfacing insights that help us anticipate needs – creating more time for meaningful customer engagement. If you’re excited to reshape how you think, make decisions, and drive growth with AI, you’ll feel right at home here.

 This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.

 What we're looking for: 
 12+ years of experience in enterprise technology, cybersecurity, consulting, solutions engineering, enterprise architecture or technical leadership roles.

 Demonstrated success influencing executive technology leaders within Fortune 500 organizations.

 Deep technical expertise across identity, access management, privileged access, cloud security, developer platforms, SaaS security or AI security.

 Exceptional executive communication skills with the ability to translate complex technical concepts into business outcomes.

 Demonstrated ability to simplify highly complex technical concepts into compelling narratives for executive audiences.

 Proven ability to influence enterprise architecture decisions across large, complex organizations.

 Experience supporting strategic enterprise sales opportunities and partnering closely with executive sales teams.

 Strong understanding of enterprise buying processes and modern sales methodologies such as MEDDPICC.

 Experience building technical strategies, reusable methodologies or customer engagement frameworks that scale beyond individual contributions.

 Demonstrated ability to influence product strategy through customer engagement and market insights.

 Proven ability to build trusted relationships across Product, Engineering, Sales and executive leadership while influencing without direct authority.

 Experience speaking to diverse audiences at industry conferences, executive forums and analyst events.

 Willingness to travel up to 50%.

 Success in This Role 
 Within your first 12 to 18 months, you will:
 Influence the successful outcome of 1Password’s most strategic customer opportunities and executive relationships.

 Build trusted partnerships with Product, Engineering and GTM leadership that shape future platform investments.

 Create repeatable technical plays, executive messaging and reference architectures adopted across the global Solutions Engineering organization.

 Elevate the technical capabilities of the field through mentorship, thought leadership and executive engagement.

 Expand 1Password’s influence across the identity security community through conference speaking, customer advisory boards and industry events.

 What you can expect: 
 Serve as a trusted technical advisor to strategic customers 
 Build relationships with CIOs, CISOs, CTOs, Chief Architects and technical decision makers across Fortune 500 organizations.

 Participate in executive briefings, architecture reviews and strategic workshops to help customers solve complex identity, access and security challenges.

 Participate in executive customer meetings where senior technical leadership is needed to build consensus, align C-level priorities with technical teams and accelerate strategic initiatives.

 Provide technical leadership throughout the sales cycle, helping account teams navigate architecture discussions, competitive evaluations and executive decision making.

 Support our most strategic opportunities by accelerating technical alignment, reducing execution risk and building customer confidence.

 Shape the Future of Solutions Engineering 
 Build repeatable technical motions, executive messaging, reference architectures and technical playbooks that scale across the global Solutions Engineering organization.

 Mentor senior Solutions Engineers and help raise the technical and consultative capabilities of the broader team.

 Partner with Sales Leadership, Solutions Engineering Leadership and Enablement to identify emerging technical trends, strategic opportunities and areas for organizational investment.

 Develop enablement programs that prepare the field for emerging technologies and evolving customer challenges.

 Serve as a technical thought leader across the organization, helping define best practices for enterprise engagement.

 Influence Product Strategy 
 Serve as the executive voice of the field by bringing customer feedback, competitive intelligence and implementation insights directly to Product and Engineering leadership.

 Partner with Product Management and Engineering to influence roadmap priorities, validate emerging capabilities and support early customer adoption programs.

 Help translate emerging market trends into actionable product and GTM strategies.

 Represent 1Password Externally 
 Speak at conferences, executive events, customer advisory boards, analyst briefings and industry forums.

 Develop technical thought leadership through presentations, blogs, webinars, whitepapers and executive content.

 Build credibility with customers, industry analysts, strategic partners and the broader security community while strengthening 1Password’s market position.

 Be called upon to join high-impact, in-person customer engagements where executive technical leadership can build alignment, accelerate decision-making and strengthen strategic relationships.

 Serve as the executive technical face of 1Password for our most strategic customers and partners.

 Shape how 1Password engages enterprise organizations around identity security, AI, developer security and modern access management.

 Partner directly with executive leadership across Product, Engineering, Marketing and Go-to-Market to influence company strategy.

 Help define the future of Solutions Engineering by mentoring technical leaders and building scalable customer engagement models.

 Represent 1Password on some of the industry’s biggest stages while helping organizations securely navigate the future of identity.

 USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $228,000 USD and $342,000 USD, and is commission-eligible. This role is also eligible for immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

 Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $228,000 CAD and $342,000 CAD and is commission-eligible. This role is also eligible for immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

 This posting is for an existing vacancy. 

 Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. 

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. 

 How we work with AI 
We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission.
