 Cross-team narratives and business insights are synthesized into a single, coherent point of view — so leadership always knows where the business stands and what decisions need to be made.

  

 Build the infrastructure that makes it all scalable 

 Forecasting processes that are repeatable, auditable, and aligned with Accounting's close process.

 Business Unit P&Ls are designed and live, enabling clearer accountability and more rigorous investment decisions.

 Internal capital allocation decisions are timely, organized and effective — providing financial frameworks to seamlessly align and execute key business decisions.

 Grow the team and raise the bar 

 A high-performing team is operating at a consistently elevated standard — stronger analytical rigor, sharper business judgment, and clear ownership across the function.

 Cross-functional partners — including the CFO, Strategic Finance, Accounting, Investor Relations, Legal, and other Business partners — rely on this function as a proactive, trusted advisor, not just a reporting engine.

  

 The secret ingredients we're looking for 

 Must-have pantry staples (Minimum Qualifications) 

 12+ years of experience in a relevant field with demonstrated financial acumen and a track record of leveraging data to drive business impact

 Proven experience in FP&A, Corporate Finance, or Strategic Finance at a high-growth or public technology company, with direct ownership of consolidated financial reporting and forecasting processes

 Deep understanding of GAAP financial statements and comfort operating across both GAAP and non-GAAP financial frameworks

jobs.description:
We are seeking a highly experienced and strategic leader to join our Third Party Risk Management (TPRM) function as a Director, Line 1B. This role is accountable for leading the Quality Assurance and governance oversight function across Vendor Information Security Management (VISM), Vendor Governance Management (VGM), and Sourcing.

 The Director will lead and manage a team, providing clear direction, oversight, and ongoing development, while ensuring procurement-related third-party risk activities are executed in line with internal policies, audit expectations, and regulatory requirements.

 The successful candidate will bring deep expertise in audit, regulatory compliance, and Risk & Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) and will serve as a key point of contact for regulators (e.g., OSFI), Internal Audit, and Second Line Risk. This role requires a strong, confident leader with a strategic and critical mindset, capable of influencing stakeholders, challenging constructively, and delivering consistent, high-quality outcomes.

 Position Responsibilities: 
 Quality Assurance & Control Oversight 
 Lead and execute a comprehensive Quality Assurance Program across VISM, VGM, and Sourcing teams

 Ensure all activities are completed in accordance with defined TPRM processes, system requirements, and documentation standards

 Identify, challenge, and escalate non-compliance, including:
 Contracts executed prior to completion of required risk assessments

 Perform effective challenge on risk assessments, including PSQ outputs that did not trigger IRQ where further review is warranted

 RCSA Ownership & Risk Governance 
 Own and lead all Procurement-related RCSAs, including design, execution, and ongoing monitoring

 Ensure risks and controls are clearly defined, consistently applied, and aligned to enterprise and regulatory expectations

 Provide clear, defensible articulation of risk positions using audit and regulatory language

 Oversee governance of:
 Key Risk Indicators (KRIs)

 Centralized issues management and remediation tracking

 Risk data accuracy and reporting integrity

 Regulatory, Audit & Compliance Engagement 
 Act as a primary point of contact for:
 Regulators (including OSFI), Internal Audit, and Line 2 Risk

 Lead responses to:
 Regulatory reviews and examinations

 Internal audit inquiries and testing

 Supplier due diligence and external questionnaires

 Ensure all outputs are accurate, consistent, evidence-based, and defensible

 Policy, Guidelines & Advisory 
 Develop and maintain TPRM guidelines, processes, and playbooks aligned to regulatory expectations

 Provide guidance to business units on:
 Handling supplier confidential documentation requests

 Application of TPRM requirements in complex or non-standard scenarios (e.g., exceptions, travel-related vendors)

 Leadership & Strategic Direction 
 Lead, manage, and develop a high-performing team, providing clear direction, priorities, and performance expectations

 Set and execute a strategic vision for Quality Assurance and TPRM governance

 Foster a culture of accountability, integrity, and continuous improvement

 Apply a critical and independent mindset to challenge processes, identify gaps, and strengthen the control environment

 Build team capability through training, coaching, and ongoing development

 Partner with senior stakeholders across Procurement, Risk, and Business Units to influence outcomes and strengthen risk management practices

 Required Qualifications: 
 10+ years of experience in Third Party Risk Management (TPRM), Operational Risk, Audit, or Compliance

 Deep expertise in:
 Audit practices and regulatory expectations

 RCSA frameworks, control design, and risk assessment methodologies

 Strong experience engaging with:
 Regulators (e.g., OSFI)

 Internal and external audit functions

 Proven ability to communicate complex risk positions using audit-grade, regulator-ready language

 Demonstrated experience leading and managing teams and delivering high-quality outcomes

 Preferred Qualifications: 
 Strong leadership and people management capability

 Strategic thinking with a forward-looking risk mindset

 Critical thinking and effective challenge capability

 Executive presence and strong stakeholder influence

 Fluency in audit and regulatory language with the ability to produce defensible outputs

 High degree of integrity, accountability, and sound judgment

 Strategic Leadership

 Technical Excellence

 12+ years experience of professional experience in related IT field with 4+ years experience in leadership, planning and communication roles.

 Deep expertise in Microsoft Azure data services ecosystem (Azure Data Factory, Synapse Analytics, Data Lake Storage, Event Hubs, Cosmos DB)

 Advanced proficiency with Databricks platform and advanced analytics workflows

 Extensive experience with BI development, administration, and enterprise deployment 

 Strong foundation in modern data architectures, scalable Lakehouse using Medallion patterns and Unity Catalog; "RAG-ready" infrastructures and AI-driven data observability to automate quality and drift detection, real-time streaming, and event-driven systems

 Proficiency in multiple programming languages (Python, Scala, SQL,.NET) and infrastructure

 Strong technical aptitude and experience with a wide variety of technologies 

 Ability to rapidly learn and if required evaluate a new tool or technology 

 Strong verbal & written communication skills 

 Demonstrated technical leadership experience 

 Be an innovative thinker 

 Must have a strong customer and quality focus 

 Have been successful in working across organizational boundaries, bringing together people with diverse perspectives and experience to find solutions to complex technical issues 

 Proven experience in architecting AI-First Data Platforms, leveraging Generative AI to automate data curation workflows and implementing RAG-ready architectures that serve both structured BI and unstructured LLM applications.

 Azure certifications (Azure Data Engineer Associate, Azure Solutions Architect Expert)

 Databricks certifications (Professional Data Engineer, Professional ML Practitioner)

 Experience in regulated industries (healthcare, financial services, manufacturing)

 Education 
 Master’s. Degree in Computer Science, Engineering or equivalent.

 Résumé du poste 
 Le Directeur principal, Finance – FP&A corporatif, est responsable de l’élaboration, de la communication et de la mise en œuvre de la planification et de l’analyse financières pour la consolidation de McKesson Canada. Il agit comme principal interlocuteur financier auprès de McKesson Corporate et des équipes de direction des différentes unités d’affaires pour les prévisions, le budget, le plan à long terme ainsi que pour tout projet ponctuel nécessitant une analyse financière. Il conseille la haute direction en tant que partenaire d’affaires dans la consolidation des budgets, des prévisions et des plans à long terme, tant au niveau stratégique que tactique.

 Responsabilités principales 
 • Agir comme partenaire d’affaires et conseiller financier clé auprès du VP, Finance, FP&A corporatif, ainsi que du CFO.
• Diriger et superviser toutes les activités liées à la planification et à l’analyse financières pour l’unité d’affaires de McKesson Canada, incluant notamment les rapports financiers, les budgets annuels, les prévisions mensuelles, les revues opérationnelles trimestrielles, les plans à long terme et les analyses financières ponctuelles.
• Conseiller la haute direction sur les implications financières des décisions d’affaires, identifier et gérer les risques et opportunités associés aux opérations et au plan à long terme (consolidation McKesson Canada).
• Fournir du soutien stratégique, de la planification de scénarios, ainsi que des analyses de risques et d’opportunités afin d’atteindre les objectifs financiers prévus et à long terme.
• Diriger le développement d’évaluations continues des objectifs financiers stratégiques à court et long terme et recommander des solutions aux parties prenantes, en tenant compte des facteurs internes et externes, de l’impact du marché, de la législation et de l’alignement avec les objectifs financiers corporatifs.
• Diriger les discussions et favoriser le consensus entre les équipes sur les sujets interdépendants entre les BU.
• Jouer un rôle clé dans l’avancement de la stratégie FP&A de McKesson Canada à travers les différents groupes.
• Soutenir l’équipe dans l’identification et la mise en œuvre de stratégies visant à maximiser la précision des prévisions au sein des différentes unités d’affaires.
• Appuyer l’équipe dans les livrables de fin de mois.
• S’assurer qu’à un niveau consolidé, les objectifs budgétaires sont atteints et que la croissance attendue pour les années futures est adéquate. Communiquer clairement au VP, Finance FP&A et M&A ainsi qu’aux CFO des BU les risques et opportunités pour l’année en cours et les années futures.
• Diriger des équipes interfonctionnelles pour suivre la performance des indicateurs clés par rapport au budget ou aux analyses financières prévues.
• Déterminer les normes et indicateurs permettant de mesurer la performance financière de McKesson Canada.
• Concevoir et communiquer des modèles flexibles (tests de résistance, gestion des dépenses, analyse coûts variables vs coûts fixes, etc.) afin d’assurer une communication efficace avec les parties prenantes et une intégration fluide dans les processus de clôture mensuelle, de prévision et de budgétisation annuelle.
• Identifier et communiquer les KPI/indicateurs clés à la haute direction, en mettant en lumière leur impact global sur l’entreprise avec des rapports clairs et concis.
• Assurer un environnement de contrôle interne hautement efficace et veiller au respect de tous les processus SOX dans le cadre du budget et du plan à long terme.

 Analyse et performance financière 
 • Diriger l’analyse des résultats financiers de l’entreprise en lien avec les profits, tendances, coûts, et conformité aux budgets, prévisions et plan à long terme.
• Surveiller les résultats financiers mensuels, trimestriels et annuels et recommander des solutions stratégiques essentielles à la croissance de l’entreprise.
• Développer et mettre en œuvre des KPI appropriés et ponctuels pour l’équipe de direction des BU, ainsi que des indicateurs permettant la gestion en temps réel des activités.
• Remettre en question les soumissions financières des BU pour les budgets, plans à long terme et prévisions continues afin d’assurer que les économies nécessaires sont prises en compte et que les coûts sont correctement reflétés.
• Guider la direction dans le développement des hypothèses mensuelles lors des prévisions et du rolling forecast; élaborer des plans de réussite pour les budgets et le plan à long terme qui seront examinés et approuvés par l’équipe de direction exécutive.
• Agir comme partenaire d’affaires du groupe des relations avec les investisseurs chez Corporate pour représenter les principaux moteurs et la performance du Canada par rapport à l’année précédente.
• Diriger et soutenir les initiatives d’amélioration des processus et les projets de mise en œuvre de systèmes liés à la planification financière (incluant les projets dirigés par le corporate).

 Responsabilités générales 
 • Agir comme la ressource principale de l’entreprise dans son domaine d’expertise, en fournissant leadership et orientation sur tous les enjeux connexes.
• Promouvoir les principes I2CARE et ILEAD de McKesson Canada et de McKesson, en démontrant l’exemple et en encourageant les autres à faire de même.
• Gérer efficacement l’équipe: soutenir, guider et diriger le personnel. Favoriser un haut niveau d’engagement, déléguer adéquatement et fournir orientation, soutien et attentes claires.
• Encourager une communication ouverte, constructive et en temps opportun. Effectuer l’évaluation des performances des employés et soutenir leur développement.
• Promouvoir la collaboration au sein de l’équipe et entre les différents groupes et départements.
• Maintenir une communication appropriée avec tous les niveaux de l’organisation.
• Veiller au respect des politiques de l’entreprise.

 Qualifications 
 • Baccalauréat en commerce avec spécialisation en finance ou comptabilité. Titre comptable professionnel (CPA) requis; solide expertise comptable.
• Minimum de 15 années d’expérience en comptabilité et gestion dans un rôle similaire, incluant au moins 10 années d’expérience en FP&A, idéalement dans une entreprise internationale.
• Expérience démontrée en interaction avec la haute direction et en développement de stratégies financières innovantes.
• Maîtrise approfondie de la planification et de l’analyse financières, des systèmes associés, ainsi que des principes économiques et analytiques liés aux affaires.
• Pensée stratégique, innovante et proactive, avec désir de travailler dans un environnement en évolution.
• Présence exécutive: capacité à interagir avec les dirigeants, influencer sans autorité et défendre ses positions.
• Habileté démontrée à gérer plusieurs livrables simultanément avec un fort sens de l’urgence.
• Excellente communication et fortes capacités d’influence.
• Esprit d’équipe, leadership et excellentes aptitudes interpersonnelles.
• Esprit analytique et stratégique, sens de l’organisation, autonomie.
• Capacité à synthétiser des analyses complexes en recommandations claires pour la haute direction.
• Leader de talent capable de maintenir une culture d’excellence.
• Jugement exceptionnel, initiative, rapidité d’apprentissage.
• Bilinguisme (oral et écrit).
• Connaissance avancée des systèmes financiers (ERP, suite Microsoft Office, etc.); la connaissance de SAP, HFM et BPC constitue un atout.

 Position Summary    

 The Senior Director of Audit, Compliance & Automation (M5) is a senior enterprise leader responsible for driving end-to-end audit readiness, compliance execution, and large-scale automation of control processes across infrastructure platforms and services.   

 This role provides strategic direction, governance, and operational leadership to ensure regulatory adherence, audit excellence, and continuous control optimization. It integrates   audit, GRC frameworks, and automation engineering   to transform compliance from a reactive process into a proactive, scalable, and technology-enabled capability.   

 Operating at the intersection of   compliance, infrastructure operations, and automation, the role partners with executive leadership, audit committees, and platform teams to ensure enterprise-wide control effectiveness, risk transparency, and measurable improvements in audit outcomes.   

 Key Responsibilities   

 1. Enterprise Audit & Compliance Leadership   

 Lead enterprise-wide audit readiness strategy across data center, infrastructure, and platform environments.   

 Own relationship with internal audit, external auditors, and regulatory bodies.   

 Oversee audit lifecycle (planning, walkthroughs, evidence collection, remediation tracking).   

 Ensure consistent execution of control frameworks (e.g., SOX ITGC, security, operational controls).   

 Drive closure of audit findings, ensuring sustainable remediation and root-cause elimination.   

 2. Automation of Controls & Audit Processes   

 Define and execute a strategy to   automate audit evidence collection, control monitoring, and certification workflows.   

 Partner with engineering and platform teams to embed   automated controls into infrastructure systems.   

 Lead adoption of tools (e.g., ServiceNow GRC, workflow platforms) to digitize compliance processes.   

 Drive continuous control monitoring (CCM) and real-time risk visibility.   

 Eliminate manual audit processes through intelligent automation and integration.   

 3. Governance, Risk & Controls Strategy   

 Design and implement enterprise GRC frameworks integrated with infrastructure transformation initiatives (DDC exit, cloud migration,   colo   consolidation).   

 Establish standardized control libraries, policies, and governance models across platforms.   

 Lead risk identification, assessment, and mitigation strategies for infrastructure services.   

 Provide executive dashboards and   reporting   on compliance posture, risk exposure, and audit health.   

 4. Operational Integration with Infrastructure Teams   

 Embed compliance and audit requirements into   run   and   build   operating models.   

 Ensure controls are integrated into   day-2 operations, provisioning workflows, and platform engineering standards.   

 Partner with infrastructure leaders to align audit compliance with transformation initiatives (cloud, EUC, data center exits).   

 Drive accountability for control ownership across engineering and operations teams.   

 5. Executive Advisory & Stakeholder Engagement   

 Serve as a trusted advisor to   EITP Infrastructure VP   and senior leadership on audit risk, compliance posture, and regulatory exposure.    

 Prepare executive briefings for audit committees and   SteerCos.   

 Represent Infrastructure in enterprise compliance and audit forums.   

 Translate audit and control requirements into business-aligned strategies.   

 6. Organizational Leadership & Talent Development: 

 Build a high-performing organization blending   audit expertise, compliance professionals, and automation engineers.   

 Develop talent pipelines and succession plans for critical governance and automation roles.   

 Foster a culture of accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement.   

 Minimum Requirements: 
 Degree or equivalent experience. Typically requires 13+ years of professional experience and 6+ years of diversified leadership, planning, communication, organization, and people motivation skills (or equivalent experience).

 Critical Skills:

 8 + years of experience in   audit, compliance, risk management, or infrastructure governance.   

 8+ years of leadership experience managing enterprise-scale teams and programs.   

 Proven experience leading large-scale audit programs (SOX, ITGC, regulatory audits).   

 Experience driving automation in compliance or operational processes.   

 Background in enterprise infrastructure, cloud, or data center environments strongly preferred.   

 Technical & Functional Expertise: 

 IT General Controls (ITGC) / SOX compliance   

 Audit lifecycle, walkthroughs, evidence management   

 Risk management frameworks and control design   

 ServiceNow GRC or similar platforms   

 Workflow automation and reporting tools   

 Infrastructure environments (compute, network, storage, DC operations)   

 Strong understanding of integrating compliance into engineering and operational processes   

 Leadership Competencies: 

 Strategic thinking and enterprise influence   

 Executive communication and stakeholder management   

 Ability to drive transformation across siloed teams   

 Strong governance and decision-making discipline   

 Data-driven mindset with focus on measurable outcomes

 Directeur(trice) principal(e) de l’architecture de solutions/Senior Director, Solution Architecture

 À propos du poste

 McKesson recherche un(e) Directeur(trice) Principal(e), Architecture d’Entreprise et Expérience Numérique pour diriger la stratégie d’architecture couvrant l’architecture de solutions, l’architecture applicative, la modernisation des solutions héritées (legacy) et la gestion de l’expérience numérique. Ce leader définira la vision de solutions technologiques modernes, évolutives, sécurisées et centrées sur le client afin de soutenir les priorités de l’entreprise et d’améliorer les résultats opérationnels.
 Dans ce rôle, vous dirigerez les pratiques d’architecture qui relient la stratégie d’affaires à l’exécution technologique. Vous collaborerez avec les dirigeants, les équipes produits, ingénierie, sécurité, opérations et les parties prenantes métier afin de moderniser les plateformes, simplifier les environnements hérités, orienter la stratégie d’expérience numérique et renforcer la gouvernance architecturale. Vous développerez également les talents, influencerez les décisions à l’échelle de l’entreprise et aiderez les équipes à livrer des solutions technologiques à fort impact dans un environnement complexe et réglementé.

 Ce que vous ferez
 Diriger la pratique d’architecture d’entreprise couvrant l’architecture de solutions, l’architecture applicative, la modernisation et la gestion de l’expérience numérique.
 Définir les normes d’architecture, les feuilles de route, les modèles de gouvernance et les cadres décisionnels permettant une livraison technologique sécurisée et évolutive.
 Collaborer avec les dirigeants et les responsables métier afin d’aligner la stratégie d’architecture sur les objectifs d’affaires, les besoins des clients et les priorités de l’entreprise.
 Diriger les stratégies de modernisation des applications et plateformes héritées, y compris la rationalisation applicative, la migration vers le cloud, l’intégration, l’automatisation et la réduction de la dette technique.
 Orienter l’architecture de l’expérience numérique afin d’améliorer l’utilisabilité, l’accessibilité, la performance, la fiabilité ainsi que les parcours clients et employés de bout en bout.
 Conseiller les équipes sur les modèles d’architecture modernes, notamment les API, les microservices, les plateformes cloud natives, l’intégration de données, la gestion des identités, la sécurité et l’observabilité.
 Superviser la planification du portefeuille d’architecture, la stratégie fournisseurs, les recommandations d’investissement et la création de valeur mesurable.
 Développer les responsables et les équipes d’architecture grâce au mentorat, à la gestion des talents, à l’évaluation de la performance et à un leadership inclusif.

 Exigences de base
 13 ans ou plus d’expérience professionnelle en technologie, dont au moins 6 ans dans des fonctions de leadership en architecture, ingénierie, livraison d’applications, plateformes numériques ou transformation technologique. 
 Diplôme universitaire en informatique, systèmes d’information, ingénierie ou domaine connexe, ou expérience équivalente.
 Expérience dans la direction d’architectures d’entreprise, de solutions ou applicatives dans des environnements technologiques de grande envergure.
 Expérience de la conception et de la modernisation d’architectures de solutions d’entreprise en s’appuyant sur des plateformes intégrant l’intelligence artificielle et des technologies émergentes afin de stimuler l’innovation, l’évolutivité et la création de valeur.
 Expérience dans l’élaboration de stratégies d’architecture, de feuilles de route, de normes, de modèles de gouvernance et de recommandations destinées aux dirigeants.
 Expérience dans la modernisation d’applications, de plateformes ou de capacités numériques héritées.
 Expérience en gestion de responsables, d’équipes d’architecture ou d’équipes technologiques multidisciplinaires.
 Expérience de collaboration avec des parties prenantes métier et technologiques de haut niveau pour influencer la stratégie et l’exécution.
 Expérience en planification budgétaire, gestion des fournisseurs, priorisation de portefeuille ou prise de décisions d’investissement technologique.

 Compétences et expériences privilégiées
 Expérience avec les plateformes cloud, les stratégies API, les microservices, l’architecture événementielle (event-driven), le DevSecOps ou l’ingénierie de plateformes.
 Expérience en gestion de l’expérience numérique, plateformes d’expérience client, portails, applications mobiles/web ou solutions omnicanales.
 Expérience dans les secteurs de la santé, de la distribution pharmaceutique, de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, du commerce de détail ou d’autres environnements d’entreprise réglementés.
 Expérience des cadres d’architecture d’entreprise, des comités de revue d’architecture, de la modélisation des capacités ou de la gestion de portefeuille applicatif.
 Expérience de direction de programmes de transformation à grande échelle impliquant plusieurs équipes, fonctions ou unités d’affaires.
 Excellentes compétences en communication avec les dirigeants et capacité à simplifier des décisions technologiques complexes pour des audiences métier.
 Capacité démontrée à améliorer la performance opérationnelle, réduire la dette technique et accélérer la mise sur le marché.
 Style de leadership axé sur la collaboration, la vision stratégique, la conduite du changement, l’orientation client et le développement des talents.

 Déplacements, présence au bureau et exigences physiques
 Le modèle de travail peut être à distance, hybride ou en présentiel selon les besoins de l’entreprise et de l’équipe.
 Des déplacements occasionnels peuvent être requis pour des réunions de leadership, des sessions de planification, des rencontres avec des fournisseurs ou des activités de collaboration d’équipe.
 Le poste requiert une utilisation régulière de l’ordinateur ainsi qu’une participation à des réunions virtuelles et en personne.

 About the Role 
 McKesson is seeking a Senior Director, Enterprise Architecture & Digital Experience to lead architecture strategy across solution architecture, application architecture, legacy solution modernization, and digital experience management. This leader will set the vision for modern, scalable, secure, and customer-centered technology solutions that support enterprise priorities and improve business outcomes.
 In this role, you will lead architecture practices that connect business strategy to technology execution. You will partner with senior leaders, product, engineering, security, operations, and business stakeholders to modernize platforms, simplify legacy environments, guide digital experience strategy, and strengthen architecture governance. You will also develop leaders, influence enterprise decisions, and help teams deliver high-impact technology solutions in a complex, regulated environment.

 What You’ll Do

 Partner with executive and senior business leaders to align architecture strategy with business objectives, customer needs, and enterprise priorities.

 Guide digital experience architecture to improve usability, accessibility, performance, reliability, and end-to-end customer and employee journeys.
 Advise teams on modern architecture patterns, including APIs, microservices, cloud-native platforms, data integration, identity, security, and observability.
 Oversee architecture portfolio planning, vendor strategy, investment recommendations, and measurable value delivery.
 Build and develop architecture leaders and teams through coaching, talent planning, performance management, and inclusive leadership practices.

 Basic Requirements 
 13+ years of professional technology experience, including 6+ years of leadership experience in architecture, engineering, application delivery, digital platforms, or technology transformation. 
 Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or related field, or equivalent experience.
 Experience leading enterprise, solution, or application architecture across large-scale technology environments.
 Lead the design and modernization of enterprise solution architectures, leveraging AI-enabled platforms and emerging technologies to drive innovation, scalability, and business value.
 Experience developing architecture strategy, roadmaps, standards, governance, and executive-level recommendations.
 Experience leading modernization of legacy applications, platforms, or digital capabilities.
 Experience managing leaders, architecture teams, or cross-functional technology teams.
 Experience partnering with senior business and technology stakeholders to influence strategy and delivery.
 Experience with budget planning, vendor management, portfolio prioritization, or technology investment decisions.

 Preferred Skills/Experience 
 Experience with cloud platforms, API strategy, microservices, event-driven architecture, DevSecOps, or platform engineering.
 Experience with digital experience management, customer experience platforms, portals, mobile/web applications, or omnichannel solutions.
 Experience in healthcare, pharmaceutical distribution, supply chain, retail, or other regulated enterprise environments.
 Experience with enterprise architecture frameworks, architecture review boards, capability modeling, or application portfolio management.
 Experience leading large-scale transformation programs across multiple teams, functions, or business units.
 Strong executive communication skills with the ability to simplify complex technology decisions for business audiences.
 Demonstrated ability to improve operational performance, reduce technical debt, and increase speed-to-market.
 Leadership approach aligned to collaboration, strategic insight, change leadership, customer focus, and talent development.

 Work model may be remote, hybrid, or office-based depending on business and team needs.

jobs.title: Directeur(trice) principal(e), Opérations du marketing numérique / Sr. Director, Digital Marketing Operations
jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care. 

 What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you. 

 ENGLISH DESCRIPTION FOLLOWS 

 Modalités de travail: Il s’agit d’un poste hybride qui exige que les candidat(e)s travaillent sur place au moins 2 jours par semaine dans notre bureau de Montréal. Les autres jours peuvent être travaillés à distance, selon les besoins de l’équipe et de l’unité d’affaire.

 À propos du poste (sommaire): 

 Le ou la D irecteur(trice) principal(e), Opérations du marketing numérique est responsable de définir et de mettre en œuvre la stratégie organisationnelle liée aux plateformes numériques et aux technologies marketing. Cette personne dirige les produits numériques, les plateformes marketing, les processus opérationnels et des équipes multidisciplinaires afin d’offrir des expériences numériques performantes, évolutives et alignées sur les objectifs de croissance de l’entreprise et d’engagement de la clientèle. 

 Ce rôle combine le leadership stratégique, la gestion de produits numériques, l’expertise en technologies marketing (MarTech), l’excellence opérationnelle et la prise de décision fondée sur les données. La personne retenue collaborera étroitement avec les équipes Marketing, Technologies, Produits numériques et les leaders d’affaires afin d’optimiser les plateformes, d’améliorer l’efficacité opérationnelle et de faire progresser les initiatives de transformation numérique. 

 Ce que vous ferez (responsabilités): 

 Stratégie numérique et leadership: 
 Élaborer et mettre en œuvre une stratégie pluriannuelle liée aux plateformes numériques et aux technologies marketing, en cohérence avec les objectifs organisationnels et commerciaux. 

 Établir les priorités stratégiques, les normes opérationnelles, les indicateurs de performance et les cadres de gouvernance pour les opérations de marketing numérique. 

 Diriger et développer des équipes hautement performantes en favorisant la collaboration, l’innovation et l’amélioration continue. 

 Gestion des produits et des plateformes numériques: 
 Assurer la responsabilité de la feuille de route et de la gestion du cycle de vie des produits numériques, notamment les sites Web, les applications mobiles et les autres plateformes soutenant les activités marketing. 

 Collaborer avec les équipes Technologies et Produits numériques afin de prioriser les améliorations, garantir la fiabilité des plateformes et offrir une expérience utilisateur exceptionnelle. 

 Représenter les exigences des parties prenantes d’affaires tout au long des activités de planification, de développement, d’essais et de déploiement. 

 Technologies marketing et opérations: 
 Superviser la sélection, l’implantation, l’intégration et l’optimisation des solutions de technologies marketing, notamment les plateformes de gestion de la relation client (CRM), les outils d’automatisation marketing, les systèmes de gestion de contenu et les plateformes analytiques. 

 Mettre en place des processus opérationnels et des mécanismes de gouvernance afin d’assurer un déploiement efficace du contenu marketing sur les canaux numériques de l’organisation. 

 Favoriser l’excellence opérationnelle grâce à des initiatives d’amélioration des processus et à l’identification d’occasions d’automatisation. 

 Analyse et optimisation de la performance: 
 Évaluer les indicateurs de performance, les données sur la clientèle et les analyses numériques afin de mesurer l’efficacité des initiatives et de cibler les occasions d’amélioration. 

 Transformer les données en recommandations concrètes permettant d’améliorer l’expérience client, l’efficacité opérationnelle et les résultats d’affaires. 

 Effectuer une veille des tendances du secteur, des technologies émergentes et des meilleures pratiques numériques afin de maintenir un avantage concurrentiel. 

 Gestion des fournisseurs et des parties prenantes: 
 Établir et entretenir de solides partenariats avec les parties prenantes internes, la haute direction et les fournisseurs externes. 

 Gérer les relations avec les fournisseurs, les négociations contractuelles, les ententes de niveau de service et la performance liée à la livraison des solutions. 

 Influencer les décisions à l’échelle de l’organisation relativement aux capacités numériques, aux investissements technologiques et aux priorités opérationnelles. 

 Exigences de base: 
 Baccalauréat en marketing, en administration des affaires, en technologies de l’information ou dans un domaine connexe. 

 Plus de 10 ans d’expérience progressive en marketing numérique, en opérations marketing, en technologies marketing, en gestion de produits numériques ou dans un domaine connexe. 

 Plus de 5 ans d’expérience en gestion d’équipes, incluant la supervision de gestionnaires et d’équipes multidisciplinaires. 

 Capacité à analyser les données et les tendances du marché afin d’éclairer les décisions stratégiques. 

 Expérience dans l’élaboration et l’exécution de stratégies liées aux plateformes numériques, aux technologies marketing ou à la transformation numérique. 

 Expérience dans la gestion de sites Web, d’applications mobiles, de plateformes numériques ou de solutions technologiques marketing d’envergure organisationnelle. 

 Expérience avec les plateformes CRM, les outils d’automatisation marketing, les systèmes de gestion de contenu et les solutions d’analytique numérique. 

 Expérience en gestion budgétaire et en optimisation du rendement du capital investi (RCI). 

 Excellentes aptitudes en leadership, en communication et en collaboration. 

 Compétences et expérience privilégiées: 
 Maîtrise en marketing, en administration des affaires, en technologies de l’information ou dans un domaine connexe. 

 Expérience dans les secteurs des soins de santé, du commerce de détail, de la distribution ou dans d’autres industries fortement réglementées. 

 Le bilinguisme (français et anglais) est considéré comme un atout. 

 Le/la titulaire de ce poste aura à soutenir de façon quotidienne des clients internes et/ou externes à l’extérieur du Québec et/ou aux États-Unis. Par conséquent, ce poste requiert une maîtrise de l’anglais à l’écrit et à l’oral. Veuillez noter que le nombre de postes dont les tâches requièrent une connaissance de la langue anglaise a été restreint dans la mesure du possible. 

 Work Arrangement: This is a hybrid position requiring candidates to work on-site at least 2 days per week at our office in Montreal. The remaining days may be worked remotely, subject to team and business needs.

 About the Role (Job Summary): 

 The Sr. Director, Digital Marketing Operations is responsible for shaping and executing the organization's digital platform and marketing technology strategy. This leader oversees digital products, marketing platforms, operational processes, and cross-functional teams to deliver scalable, high-performing digital experiences that support business growth and customer engagement.

 This role combines strategic leadership, digital product management, marketing technology (MarTech) expertise, operational excellence, and data-driven decision-making. The successful candidate will partner closely with Marketing, Technology, Digital Product, and Business leaders to optimize platforms, improve operational effectiveness, and advance digital transformation initiatives.

 What You'll Do (Responsibilities): 

 Digital Strategy & Leadership: 
 Develop and execute a multi-year digital platform and marketing technology strategy aligned with organizational and commercial objectives.

 Establish strategic priorities, operational standards, performance metrics, and governance frameworks for digital marketing operations.

 Lead and develop high-performing teams, fostering collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.

 Digital Product & Platform Management: 
 Own the roadmap and lifecycle management of digital products, including websites, mobile applications, and other marketing-enabled platforms.

 Partner with Technology and Digital Product teams to prioritize enhancements, ensure platform reliability, and deliver exceptional user experiences.

 Represent business stakeholder requirements throughout planning, development, testing, and deployment activities.

 Marketing Technology & Operations: 
 Oversee the selection, implementation, integration, and optimization of marketing technology solutions, including CRM platforms, marketing automation tools, content management systems, and analytics platforms.

 Establish operational processes and governance to support the efficient deployment of marketing content across owned digital channels.

 Drive operational excellence through process improvement initiatives and automation opportunities.

 Analytics & Performance Optimization: 
 Evaluate performance metrics, customer insights, and digital analytics to measure effectiveness and identify opportunities for improvement.

 Translate data into actionable recommendations that improve customer experience, operational efficiency, and business outcomes.

 Monitor industry trends, emerging technologies, and evolving digital best practices to maintain a competitive advantage.

 Vendor & Stakeholder Management: 
 Build strong partnerships with internal stakeholders, senior leadership, and external vendors.

 Manage vendor relationships, contract negotiations, service-level agreements, and solution delivery performance.

 Influence enterprise-wide decisions related to digital capabilities, technology investments, and operational priorities.

 Basic Requirements: 
 Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business Administration, Information Technology, or a related field.  

 10+ years of progressive experience in digital marketing, marketing operations, marketing technology, digital product management, or related disciplines.

 5+ years of people leadership experience, including leadership of managers and cross-functional teams.

 Ability to analyze data and market trends to inform strategic decisions.

 Experience developing and executing digital platform, marketing technology, or digital transformation strategies.

 Experience managing websites, mobile applications, digital platforms, or enterprise marketing technology solutions.

 Experience working with CRM platforms, marketing automation tools, content management systems, and digital analytics solutions.

 Experience managing budgets and optimizing ROI.

 Excellent leadership, communication, and collaboration skills.

 Preferred Skills & Experience: 
 Master's degree in Marketing, Business Administration, Information Technology, or a related field.

 Experience in healthcare, retail, distribution, or other highly regulated industries.

 Bilingualism (English and French) is considered an asset.

 The incumbent of this position will provide daily support to internal and/or external clients outside Quebec and/or in the United States. Therefore, he/she must be proficient in spoken and written English. Please note that the number of positions requiring English language skills has been limited where possible.

jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

 What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

 McKesson Technology (MT) has Enterprise Portfolio Management Office (EPMO) which is a centralized function to 1) enable consistent portfolio management 2) build and mature project and program management capabilities and 3) drive project management rigor and standards to enable value realization from investments.
 Principal Technology Portfolio Management Leader will be a key member of the EPMO team. The individual will be responsible for serving as a portfolio lead supporting Cybersecurity service area and a Business Unit. The individual in this role will need to be able to operate within a high level of ambiguity, remain calm under pressure and help establish structure and focus.

 Key Responsibilities: 
 Drive the intake, prioritization, and sequencing of portfolio initiatives with cross-functional partners to ensure alignment with business strategy and maximize business outcomes.

 Monitor and track portfolio health by evaluating execution progress, interdependencies, risks, and capacity constraints, proactively recommending sequencing and highlighting issues to enable successful delivery and value realization.

 Drive connectivity and collaboration across delivery teams, Finance, and portfolio leads, influencing decisions that support achievement of business goals.

 Enable visibility into capacity constraints and facilitate alignment of priorities and trade-offs, ensuring resources are allocated to the most valuable initiatives.

 Establish and lead regular portfolio reviews with stakeholders and executive leadership, providing clear reporting on progress, financials, risks, lessons learned, and business impacts to inform decision-making.

 Drive annual budget planning with Finance, review baseline financials and investment budgets for initiatives, and collaborate with service managers to guide resource allocation and strategic decisions.

 Champion data-driven analysis and actionable insights, connecting project and technology spend to business value, and recommending trade-offs, course corrections, or project terminations as needed.

 Maintain portfolio governance and data integrity, ensure projects adhere to established frameworks, complete necessary lifecycle work, and have approved change requests for budget or schedule deviations.

 Build and maintain strong relationships with stakeholders, ensuring their needs and expectations are met through effective communication and delivery of portfolio information.

 Partner with Finance and embed benefits realization and value tracking into portfolio management by defining clear success metrics upfront, monitoring benefits during and after implementation, and reporting on KPI improvements, cost savings, and revenue growth.

 Promote transparency and alignment by providing stakeholders with visibility into how initiatives support strategic objectives, enabling informed prioritization and optimization of the portfolio’s cost/benefit mix.

 Support dynamic portfolio rebalancing, adapting to changes in business, financial, or capacity conditions to protect core operations while enabling innovation.

 Partner with Finance for ongoing financial forecasting, trend analysis, and investment mix reviews, ensuring high-value opportunities are funded and low-value projects are deprioritized.

 Anchor portfolio decisions in enterprise architecture, preventing proliferation of non-strategic platforms and ensuring alignment with target state architecture.

 Champion holistic performance and risk management, presenting portfolio health in business terms and elevating discussions from project status to business impact.

 Basic Skills and Experience: 
 Degree or equivalent and typically requires 13+ years, with 8+ years of direct work-related experience. Less years required if has relevant Master's or Doctorate qualifications.

 Critical Skills and Experience: 
 8+ years of program and/or portfolio management experience with 5+ years of experience within a technology focused area (Cyber Security, Digital Transformation, IT Infrastructure, Cloud Modernization, etc.).

 Demonstrated experience collaborating regularly with VPs, SVPs, and C-suite executives, supported by a background in consulting.

 Exceptional executive presentation, communication, and influence management skills.

 Experience managing large portfolios and ensuring strategic alignment and prioritization, as well as overseeing investments and value realization—ideally within the technology sector, though a background in general technology combined with business portfolio management is also suitable.

 Experience delivering results by collaborating and influencing business and technology delivery teams in a highly matrixed organization.

 Proven stakeholder management skills & building credibility with executive leadership.

 Ability to intentionally flex between strategy and detail and adapt style to different levels of the organization.

 Experience driving organizational transformation and change management.

 Ability to make complex concepts simple and convey it laymen’s terms.

 Demonstrated ability to establish collaborative relationships and move with speed while bringing people along.

 High degree of emotional maturity and ability to remain calm and focused under pressure.

 Additional Knowledge & Skills desired but not required: 
 Experience managing technology portfolio for a business unit or shared services function is highly desirable.

 Experience working in large matrixed organizations is highly desirable.

 Experience working with portfolio tools (Planview, Clarity PPM, etc.) is desirable.

 Experience in a highly regulated industry is desirable.

 Certification(s) in SAFe Agile, Prince2 / APM, PMP and/or Lean Six Sigma desirable.

 Travel: Hybrid role and may have to travel within the country up to 10%

 Relocation is not budgeted for this role

jobs.title: Senior Director, Platform
jobs.description:
About Miovision: 
 At Miovision, we’re unlocking transportation networks that move you. Our vision and mission is to enable smart, fast, safe communities that simply flow, as we drive the Intelligent Mobility Revolution. Backed by the world’s most advanced traffic AI, Miovision’s innovations in traffic signal planning and operations are making it possible for cities to improve the transportation experience for drivers, cyclists and pedestrians.

Our values drive us. They’re at the core of everything we do. If they align with yours, proceed through the GREEN light!
 All in to win: We're driven by a winning mindset, approaching every challenge with intensity, clarity, and speed.

 One Miovision: We succeed as one team, uniting diverse talents, building on trust, and putting our shared mission before ego.

 Be better every day: We're committed to continuous growth, staying curious, building mastery, and embracing challenges as learning opportunities.

 Make it happen: We are proactive and results-driven, taking ownership, acting with urgency, and focusing on solutions that deliver real impact.

 Earn the customer: We are deeply customer-centric, focused on earning our customers' partnership every day by delivering exceptional experiences that drive their success.

 Position Summary: 
 At Miovision, we are engineering the future of smart transportation, and right now, we are laying down the asphalt for our most ambitious infrastructure project yet. We are building a governed, API-first technology platform that will act as the ultimate express lane for how we build software, enabling new experiences for customers, partners, and AI agents. We are looking for a Senior Director, Platform to serve as the master traffic controller for this massive transformation. Reporting to the SVP of Software Engineering & Technology, you will build the foundational highways that our entire product ecosystem travels on. You will steer our engineering organization away from gridlocked, application-centric development and into a high-speed, contract-driven future. If you are a hands-on leader ready to pave the way for AI-assisted innovation and ensure our platform capabilities always get the green light, it is time to take the wheel!

 Objectives and Responsibilities: 
 Platform Strategy & Architectural Foundation 
 Own the engineering strategy and translate our Platform North Star into clear architectural priorities for both human and AI-driven use cases.

 Spearhead the transition from application-centric integration toward a governed, contract-driven, API-first platform.

 Partner with Architecture to establish a durable technical foundation that protects long-term integrity while pragmatically supporting near-term delivery.

 Drive an engineering culture where teams naturally build on the platform because it is the absolute fastest and most effective path to delivering value.

 Organizational Leadership & Scaling 
 Lead, coach, and aggressively grow the Platform Engineering organization by recruiting top-tier talent with deep expertise in APIs, distributed systems, and AI.

 Build a highly resilient team culture grounded in ownership, curiosity, technical excellence, and high-velocity delivery.

 Lead the shift toward platform-first ways of working, building alignment, adoption, and accountability across the broader Engineering department.

 Create an environment where senior engineers are highly empowered to make decisions while remaining perfectly aligned with a shared architectural direction.

 Platform as a Product (First-Party, Third-Party & Ecosystem Enablement) 
 Partner with Product Leadership to operate the Platform exactly like a customer-facing product, treating internal developers, external partners, and AI agents as your core customers.

 Establish API contracts as first-class products that natively support authentication, observability, usage metering, and scalable commercial models from day one.

 Build a governed, unified entry point for Miovision's strategic capabilities, utilizing adoption data and developer feedback to continuously improve the ecosystem.

 Identify and build reusable, standardized capabilities—partnering with Data Science to integrate models and data products—eliminating isolated alternatives across the company.

 Technical Leadership & Hands-On Builder 
 Remain deeply engaged in the technology—reviewing architecture, exploring code, and prototyping solutions alongside your engineers to blast through ambiguity.

 Build the technical foundations for AI-assisted development, personally utilizing modern agentic tools and establishing AI-native practices across your team.

 Partner with Developer Operations to build automation and tooling that makes standardized, scalable architecture the absolute easiest path for our engineers.

 Bring razor-sharp technical judgment to complex distributed systems, helping teams practically evolve existing architecture without requiring massive, disruptive rewrites.

 Operational Excellence, Reliability & Trust 
 Establish world-class reliability, observability, security, and operational readiness as the fundamental DNA of all Platform capabilities.

 Ensure human and agent identity, delegated authorization, auditability, and guardrails are natively built into the platform rather than siloed across individual teams.

 Define strict lifecycle, compatibility, and service health standards so consumers can depend on Platform services with absolute confidence.

 Ensure the Platform seamlessly scales alongside Miovision’s rapidly growing products, customer base, and engineering organization without multiplying operational complexity.

 The Ideal Profile: 
 The Engineering Veteran: You bring 15+ years of software engineering experience with a heavy focus on platform engineering, distributed systems, and large-scale architecture.

 The Organization Builder: You have a proven track record of successfully leading, scaling, and coaching senior engineering teams in highly complex, multi-product environments.

 The API Architect: You boast deep technical expertise in API design, microservices, contract governance, and full API lifecycle management.

 The Platform Product Thinker: You treat platforms exactly like a product. Experience monetizing a platform, scaling a marketplace, or building a third-party developer ecosystem is strongly preferred.

 The AI-Native Leader: You have hands-on experience executing platform strategies that fundamentally change how engineering teams use AI to build, verify, and deliver software (including exposure to MCP and machine-readable interfaces).

 The Hands-On Builder: You are a highly credible technical leader who is just as comfortable exploring code and prototyping a solution as you are driving an executive strategy meeting.

 The Cloud Heavyweight: You have deep, practical familiarity with cloud-native architectures (AWS), Kubernetes, modern CI/CD, and languages like Java, Python, or Node.js.

 The Transformation Driver: You have demonstrated experience successfully driving massive architectural or engineering operating-model shifts within an organization.

 The Operations Sentinel: You possess a profound understanding of reliability, telemetry, security, and operational excellence in massive, high-stakes production systems.

 The Strategic Diplomat: You wield excellent communication and influence skills, capable of partnering flawlessly with Product Management, Architecture, and C-suite stakeholders.

 The Pragmatic Visionary: You excel at systems thinking—perfectly balancing the need for long-term architectural integrity with the reality of pragmatic, incremental delivery.

 Your Rewards & Well-being: 
We invest in our team with benefits designed for modern life and true work-life balance.
 Comprehensive Coverage: Your well-being is covered from day one with comprehensive health benefits, 24/7 virtual healthcare access, and dedicated wellness programs.

 Financial Future: Build for tomorrow with our RRSP/401K Matching Plan and share in the company's success through our Variable Incentive Plan.

 Time to Recharge: Truly unplug with our unique Mio-Days and flexible vacation policy.

 Work & Life Support: We support you with flexible work options, an internet subsidy, a remote work allowance, and enhanced leave for new parents.

 Sound like your next adventure? Apply now and let's start building together! 
 We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. Please indicate if you require accommodation on your application, and our team will work with you to meet your accessibility needs.
 Miovision may use artificial intelligence (AI) to assist in the hiring process for tasks such as helping to identify qualified candidates, taking meeting notes, creating summaries, and streamlining administrative work. These tools are one of several factors considered in the hiring process and do not replace human judgement. We do not use AI to make any final hiring or interview decisions. 
 PLEASE BE AWARE OF FRAUD: Applicants interested in applying for roles at Miovision should apply directly via the details provided on our careers page. jobs.description:
Director, Quantitative Data Products 

 Nasdaq's Alternative Data group specializes in creating unique and insightful data products from non-traditional data sources. Well-known examples of Alternative Data include sentiment measures, real-time tracking of vehicles via GPS transponders, satellite monitoring of industrial facilities, and consumer insights gleaned from anonymized credit card transactions. Our data products empower some of the world's most sophisticated investment funds to outperform. 

 As Director of Quantitative Data Products, you'll play a critical role in defining strategy and driving execution of a portfolio of innovative Alternative Data products. You'll thrive in this position if you're entrepreneurial, data-driven, and strategic, with a deep understanding of investments and a passion for creating products that generate real business impact in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. The ideal candidate has trade floor and/or investments experience, with a strong understanding of buy-side and sell-side trading workflows. 

 Key Responsibilities 
 Conduct market research and engage directly with clients to identify new product opportunities and validate concepts.

 Own the full product lifecycle from ideation and validation through launch, scale, and ongoing optimization.

 Develop and prioritize product roadmaps that align with business objectives and drive measurable revenue growth.

 Partner with cross-functional teams including data science, data engineering, partnerships, client success, sales, and marketing to design and deliver innovative data products.

 Drive go-to-market strategy, including pricing, positioning, and sales enablement to maximize product adoption and success.

 Required Qualifications 
 10+ years of experience in product management, product development, and/or data analysis within the investment industry.

 Deep understanding of capital markets, data product fundamentals, and data feeds/products.

 Proven ability to conceptualize and drive new initiatives from 0-to-1 in a fast-paced and entrepreneurial environment.

 Excellent communicator with strong stakeholder management skills and a revenue-focused, owner mindset.

 Bachelor's degree in finance, economics, computer science, engineering, or related discipline.

 Preferred Qualifications 
 Strong understanding of the alternative data landscape, including key companies and products/services, as well as their competitive positioning.

 Experienced in evaluating and applying alternative data to the investment lifecycle (i.e., programming, statistics, backtesting, etc).

 0-to-1 startup or venture-building experience.

 This position will be located in Toronto and offers the opportunity for a hybrid work environment at least 3 days a week in-office, subject to change, providing flexibility and accessibility for qualified candidates.

 Come as You Are 

 Nasdaq is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds and identities.

 We are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where diverse perspectives, experiences, and identities are valued and celebrated.

 We ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided with reasonable accommodation throughout the hiring process.

 What We Offer 

 We’re proud to offer a competitive rewards package that is meaningful, recognizes the unique needs of our employees and their families and incentivizes employees for their contribution to Nasdaq’s overall success.

The base pay range for this role is $121,000 - $170,000. In addition to base salary, Nasdaq provides a generous annual bonus/commission (short-term incentive), and equity (long-term incentive), comprehensive benefits, and opportunity for growth. Exact compensation may vary based on several job-related factors that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to: skill set, experience, education/training, business needs and market demands.

jobs.title: Director, Commercial FP&A
jobs.description:
At PointClickCare our mission is simple: to help providers deliver exceptional care. And that starts with our people. As a leading health tech company that’s founder-led and privately held, we empower our employees to push boundaries, innovate, and shape the future of healthcare. 

With the largest long-term and post-acute care dataset and a Marketplace of 400+ integrated partners, our platform serves over 30,000 provider organizations, making a real difference in millions of lives. We also reinvest a significant percentage of our revenue back into research and development, ensuring our employees have the resources to innovate and make a lasting impact. Recognized by Forbes as a top private cloud company and honored as one of Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, we offer flexibility, growth opportunities, and meaningful work.

Employees harness AI as a catalyst for creativity, productivity, and thoughtful decision-making. jobs.description:
Job Description 

 Director of Solution Architecture, Capital Markets
 WHAT IS THE OPPORTUNITY? 

 As Head of Data Architecture, you will lead the strategic design and governance of RBC Capital Market's data platform ecosystem. This high-impact leadership role shapes how the organization captures, stores, processes, and leverages data to drive business value. You'll oversee architecture of critical systems supporting capital markets operations, guide teams through data modernization initiatives, and establish standards that enable innovation while maintaining integrity and security. Partner with senior business and technology leaders to deliver transformational outcomes and influence enterprise-wide technology decisions.
 WHAT WILL YOU DO? 
 Consult on major initiatives within CM (Capital Markets) to help design solutions that meet the specific needs of the delivery while also progressing the broader architectural strategy of the department (align with architecture principles, modernize and simplify the estate, re-use capabilities/technologies, etc).

 Review proposed architectures from CM delivery teams to align specific team requirements to high level goals of CM leadership and the bank.  For instance, why are you ordering a physical machine instead of using internal cloud?  Why are you using Redis over MemSQL?  Why are you pulling X from RBCAppA instead of RBCAppB?  Etc..

 Help lead an architecture council in which proposed architectures are debated for their merits and scrutinized by a broad set of stakeholders. 

 Help to form and communicate technology guidance to standardize development of commonly needed capabilities.  For instance, figure out what our API strategy should be, document it on confluence, present it to senior leadership, and show dev teams how to implement it.

 WHAT DO YOU NEED TO SUCCEED? 

 Must have 
 • Undergraduate degree coupled with transformational experience in complex programs with and multiple priorities and stakeholders
 • Demonstrated ability in written and oral communication skills along with strong presentation skills; ability to determine the information and communication needs of stakeholders and projects.
 • Strong organizational awareness, relationship management, project management, and time management capabilities.
 • A strong understanding of financial services industry with specific knowledge of capital markets data technologies including: Kafka (capture/stream trade and market data), kdb+ (real-time in-memory storage), Snowflake/Databricks (historical archive and batch analytics), and MongoDB (flexible storage).

 Flexible work/life balance

 RBC has embarked on a transformational journey leveraging Generative AI and AI as a catalyst to drive significant productivity gains and revenue growth across the enterprise. We are seeking an exceptional, strategic leader to serve as Director of AI & Digital Transformation Programs, playing a pivotal role in shaping and executing RBC's most critical AI initiatives.

 As a Director within the RBC AI Group, you will lead the strategic direction and execution of enterprise-wide AI Transformation programs. You will serve as a trusted advisor to senior executives, orchestrating cross-functional collaboration across business lines, technology, risk, finance, and compliance. Reporting to executive leadership, you will be accountable for delivering measurable business impact while navigating complex organizational dynamics and driving cultural change across the bank.

 Your responsibilities will include: 
 Define and drive enterprise AI strategy: Partner with senior executives and business leaders to shape, structure, and prioritize AI programs that deliver measurable bottom-line impact and align with RBC's strategic objectives

 Lead complex, enterprise-scale transformations: Support the planning, governance, and execution of multiple large-scale AI programs with interdependencies across platforms, business units, and geographies

 Build strategic partnerships and influence at the executive level: Establish and maintain executive-level relationships across Finance, Risk, Compliance, Technology, Procurement, and Business Units to secure alignment, funding, and support for AI initiatives

 Provide executive counsel and thought leadership: Lead storytelling in executive forums through compelling presentations, business cases, and strategic communications that drive informed decision-making and maintain stakeholder confidence

 Optimize enterprise processes for AI delivery: Partner with senior leaders to streamline governance, risk, compliance, and procurement frameworks, enabling faster, more efficient deployment of AI solutions

 Manage risk and resolve strategic blockers: Proactively identify program risks, dependencies, and organizational impediments; escalate strategically to executive leadership to drive resolution and maintain momentum

 Develop and mentor program leadership: Build and guide a team of program managers, fostering a high-performance culture focused on delivery excellence and continuous improvement

 You're our ideal candidate if you: 
 Must-have:
 8+ years of progressive experience in strategy, digital transformation, management consulting, or financial services leadership roles

 Proven track record leading large-scale, enterprise-wide transformation programs with demonstrated business impact

 Deep expertise in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and emerging digital technologies, with the ability to translate technical concepts for executive audiences

 Advanced degree (MBA, Master's in relevant field)

Some of our Blogs might help you get a better understanding of what we do here. You can find them all here.
 Thriving at Rewind: 
 We embrace the fast-paced, ever-changing nature of startup life. If you love working with speed, agility, and creativity, you’ll feel right at home here. Here's what it takes to succeed with us:
 Team-First Mentality: We put teamwork at the core of everything we do, believing that we are better when we are together. Success is shared, and when the team wins, we all win.

 Performance-Driven Mindset: We are proactive, goal-oriented, and focused on delivering tangible, high-quality results. We go beyond meeting expectations - we aim to exceed them.

 Flexible Work-Life Approach: We encourage balance and understand the need to recharge. While we stay agile for urgent needs, we make sure there's time to recover and enjoy life.

 Customer Centricity: Our commitment to customers shapes everything we do. We listen, build relationships, and innovate - from our dedicated customer support team to our engineers, everyone at our company is focused on solving problems that matter most to our users.

 Taking Initiative: We value ownership and proactive problem-solving. We encourage team members to think creatively, take ownership, and lead improvements. Your ideas and actions drive our success.

 We Make Time for Fun: We work hard and make time to enjoy the journey. It’s not just about hitting milestones—it’s about making the experience rewarding along the way.

 About the role 
 We’re looking for a senior finance leader to own and evolve Rewind’s full finance function spanning accounting, financial planning, and controller responsibilities. This role sits at the intersection of strategy and execution: you’ll bring a strong accounting foundation, step confidently into hands-on operational work when needed, and guide the business with clear, data-driven insight.
 This is a hands on builder role. You’ll shape the broader finance strategy, while also performing core Accounting and Controller responsibilities. You should expect to roll up your sleeves and operate as both a leader and an individual contributor, handling everything from Board reporting, to financial modelling, to processing payroll and driving month end close. You’ll partner closely with the executive team, particularly the CEO and CRO to ensure Rewind scales with financial clarity, discipline, and confidence.

 What you’ll do 
 Financial leadership & strategy 
 Own company-wide financial planning, forecasting, and performance tracking, including SaaS metrics and operating models

 Partner with leadership to guide investment decisions, pricing strategy, and growth planning

 Deliver clear, actionable financial insights to executives, board members, and investors

 Support strategic finance work including scenario planning and executive-level analysis.

 Accounting, close operations & compliance 
 Oversee and continuously improve the month-end close process, ensuring accurate and timely reporting across P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow

 Maintain high-quality financial reporting and variance analysis to support decision-making

 Step into hands-on accounting work where needed, ensuring no gaps in execution as the team scales

 Own all core accounting operations, including AP/AR, payroll, treasury, and general ledger management

 Lead audits, tax filings, and compliance across jurisdictions, including SR&ED and international subsidiaries

 Manage equity administration (e.g., Carta), ensuring accurate cap table and regulatory compliance

 Controls, governance & infrastructure 
 Strengthen internal controls and financial processes to safeguard company assets and support scale

 Oversee vendor relationships, banking, insurance programs, and external partners (auditors, consultants)

 Build and evolve systems, tooling, and workflows to improve accuracy, efficiency, and visibility

 Oversee the stock option/equity program and management of the cap table.

 Leverage Agentic AI 
 Use Agentic AI to automate key processes such as: accounts receivable, month-end close, and financial package preparation

 Team leadership & development 
 Lead and mentor the finance and accounting team, setting a high bar for accountability and performance

 Foster a culture of ownership, continuous improvement, and cross-functional collaboration

 What you’ll bring 
 Experience in a venture-backed or scaling SaaS company

 CPA designation (or equivalent) with 10+ years of progressive experience across accounting and finance

 Early-career foundation in accounting (e.g., audit, controllership) with a transition into broader finance leadership

 Experience owning both accounting operations and FP&A in a high-growth SaaS or tech environment

 Strong understanding of SaaS metrics, revenue recognition, and financial best practices

 Proficiency using AI tools to streamline and enhance financial modelling, reporting and workflows

 Comfort operating as a hands-on leader, including stepping into payroll, reporting, or operational tasks when needed

 Proven ability to build, improve, and scale financial processes and systems

 Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate complex financial data into clear insights

 Experience with modern finance tools (e.g., NetSuite, Salesforce, Stripe, Carta, QuickBooks Online)

 Nice to have 
 Exposure to international finance operations and multi-entity structures

 Experience managing or implementing financial systems and automation initiatives

 Familiarity with BI or dashboarding tools (e.g., Metabase, Looker, Tableau)

 Experience supporting board reporting and investor relations

 Location 
 There is a strong preference for candidates based in Ontario for easier collaboration and occasional in-person meetings in our HQ office (Ottawa).

 Compensation Philosophy 
The actual base salary will vary based on various factors, including market and individual qualifications objectively assessed during the interview process. 
 In some cases, we’re open to hiring at a higher level for the right person and are committed to paying competitively and fairly.
 If your experience is closer to an earlier career stage, we may still consider your application. In that case, we would evaluate the role at a different level within our levelling framework.
 Pay is just one part of the overall compensation at Rewind.

 Why join Rewind 
 At Rewind, you’ll help shape the future of data protection for thousands of businesses. We’re performance-driven, innovative, and not afraid to challenge what’s possible. You’ll join a team that values trust, accountability, and respect for people’s time — and encourages every employee to experiment, think critically, and grow.
 We support innovation through experimentation — including smart use of AI tools — and believe the best ideas come from those who aren’t afraid to push boundaries.

 How Rewind Will Support You 
We know that enjoying the journey is just as important as reaching our goals. We work hard to create a positive, inclusive environment where fun and laughter are part of our everyday routine. We also offer a variety of benefits to support your success both at work and in your personal life which includes but is not limited to: 
 Flexible work hours

 Employee stock options

 Health benefits

 3 weeks vacation

 7 life leave days

 2 Level Up days for professional development

 1 volunteer day

 Summer Fridays and office closed during the holiday break in December

 Paid parental leave

 $5000/year professional development allowance

 Rewind is committed to building an inclusive, supportive place for you to do the best and most rewarding work of your career. We strongly encourage candidates of all different backgrounds and identities to apply.
